> Historical conversion record. Quoted source comments and old branch paths
> below describe the recovery process, not the shipping build. The current
> tree uses the compile-time `NW_DEBUG_TOOLS` gate and the `NW_DEBUG_*`
> environment names documented in `docs/BUILD.md`; old probe names are retained
> here only as provenance.

# Conversion provenance

This file records the original recovered files represented by the structured C tree.
The source tree intentionally contains no fixed-address matching requirement. The table
in `CONVERSION_MAP.tsv` is the machine-readable index; this document keeps the leading
conversion notes removed from each file during cleanup. The `c/...` paths are
archive paths in `../clean_c/c` (or the original checkout); `clean_v2` has no
top-level `c/` directory.

The map now points each original unit at its consolidated group file and records
the group's unit selector. `FUNCTION_INDEX.tsv` is the direct original-file ->
implementation-file table, and `GROUPS.tsv` lists the member units of every
group. The notes below remain keyed by the original unit, so a provenance anchor
still leads to the exact section inside its group file.

### `include/GridDeltaApply.h`

- Original file: `c/GridDeltaApply.h`
- Source SHA-256: `04bd61a1c1595af0013c7b24476533705db69ee4b4067910977d60111604a0b5`

<details><summary>Original leading conversion notes</summary>

````text
/* Shared primitive for the four grid-delta stream decoders.
 *
 * The originals use `lodsb; add al,(edi); inc edi; dec <counter>; jne`
 * loops.  They are bottom-tested: a zero counter means 2^32 iterations, not
 * zero.  The callers only pass nonzero lengths from valid streams, but the
 * loop shape is kept exactly so a malformed stream behaves like the original
 * rather than silently turning into a no-op.
 */
````

</details>

### `include/NwVmTrace2.h`

- Original file: `c/NwVmTrace2.h`
- Source SHA-256: `04a6f69a117c2c65e5faa3c985828163205c6f3c3c76f1f147e5901d5675ecf2`

<details><summary>Original leading conversion notes</summary>

````text
/*
 * NwVmTrace2.h -- opt-in VM trace v2 record layout and emitters.
 *
 * This is diagnostic code, not part of the original game design.  It is
 * additive to v1 (NWVMTRACE) and is selected independently with NWVMTRACE2.
 *
 * The two emitters are intentionally at well-defined dispatch boundaries:
 *
 *   S  the dispatcher fetch point, before the opcode at `cursor` executes.
 *      In the asm reference this is the 0x409760 fetch head, i.e. the point
 *      reached after the previous opcode's handler completed.
 *   O  the operand executor entry.  In the asm reference this is
 *      0x004054b8, before its 31-arm switch body.
 *
 * `NwVmTrace2Regs` is filled by the C dispatcher.  Fields are all 32-bit so
 * the layout is the same on i386 and on a host test build.  The ESP field is
 * the dispatcher's private value-stack pointer, not the host stack pointer;
 * the emitter never dereferences it.
 */
````

</details>

### `include/nwdebug.h`

- Original file: `c/nwdebug.h`
- Source SHA-256: `5d567c669fedae5500b651e6e1bdaa52745d757b4cb61f622757abe4614c9e97`

<details><summary>Original leading conversion notes</summary>

````text
/*
 * nwdebug.h -- a removable debug-print facility.
 *
 * USAGE
 *   #include "nwdebug.h"          once, near the top of a .c file
 *   NWDEBUG("label %d\n", x);     prints only when NWDEBUG_ENABLED is defined
 *
 * TO TURN ON
 *   i686-w64-mingw32-gcc -DNWDEBUG_ENABLED ...      (or edit the default below)
 *
 * TO TURN OFF
 *   Delete the NWDEBUG(...) lines. Nothing else references this header, and no
 *   other code depends on it, so removal cannot break the build. Each call site
 *   is self-contained: the macro expands to nothing, arguments included.
 *
 * WHY IT WRITES TO A FILE, NOT stderr
 *   This is a GUI subsystem binary (-mwindows): it has no console attached, so
 *   anything written to stdout/stderr is simply lost. OutputDebugString is not
 *   visible without a debugger attached. A file next to the executable is the
 *   only channel that works when the process is launched unattended, which is
 *   exactly when the output is needed.
 *
 * The handle is opened on first use and kept open in append mode for the life of
 * the process; NWDEBUG_CLOSE (called from the loader) flushes and closes it.
 */
````

</details>

<a id="include-nwglobals-h"></a>
### `include/nwglobals.h`

- Original file: `c/nwglobals.h`
- Source SHA-256: `6922723ad1a5b45aa2cfea79eb914bb555d517dbc9b687b06fcd2e2d4d324fc4`

<details><summary>Original leading conversion notes</summary>

````text
/* nwglobals.h -- globals the corpus DECLARED but never DEFINED.
 *
 * A name declared `extern` by some files and defined by none links against a
 * COMMON symbol in .bss: the build succeeds, nm reports the name, and every
 * reader sees zero. The link is clean and the program is still wrong.
 *
 * Each name below is mapped back to the slot the ORIGINAL binary used, from the
 * address annotation the corpus already carried. Those slots live in the data
 * window, so the storage already exists in nw_datablock.bin -- the value the
 * original's startup wrote is the value we read.
 *
 * Macros, not declarations, on purpose: the original had exactly one object per
 * address. Defining a name in each using file would produce two .bss cells that
 * silently disagree, which is strictly worse than the bug.
 *
 * Include before any use, and do not re-declare these names -- a surviving
 * `extern` line shadows the macro back into a COMMON symbol.
 */
````

</details>

<a id="include-nwgridctxrec-h"></a>
### `include/nwgridctxrec.h`

- Original file: `c/nwgridctxrec.h`
- Source SHA-256: `3e48dc0e5b03c5b990ebb0cf21e232c6d2217924ed13b3c63d024575a2f51dd7`

<details><summary>Original leading conversion notes</summary>

````text
/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- GridCtxRec
 * The grid-context record behind g_pCurGridCtx (slot 0x417218).
 *
 * The corpus named this record in seven unrelated spellings (GridCtxRec,
 * CurGridCtxRec, PGridSpanSlot, uint8_t*, ...) and no single declaration ever
 * existed, so `->` could not compile.  This is that one declaration.
 *
 * EVERY offset below is pinned by an access in the ORIGINAL binary's bytes.
 * Nothing is inferred from a name.  Where two names denote the SAME storage the
 * member is a union, so both spellings compile to the same access:
 *
 *   +0x00  byte   bStatusFlags / bCtxFlags
 *     0x402b50  mov (%ecx),%dl ; and $0xf0      -> high nibble is the mode byte
 *     0x402b84  andb $0xf,(%eax)                -> low nibble (record class)
 *     0x402b92  or   %al,(%ecx)                 -> mode nibble OR'd back in
 *     0x4074ce  orb  $0x4,(%ecx)                -> "offsets are ref-relative"
 *   +0x01  byte   bAux
 *     0x402b5d  mov 0x1(%ecx),%al               -> low byte of the restamp word
 *   +0x02  byte   bPendingIndex / bStampLow
 *     0x402b3d  mov %cx,0x2(%edx)               -> stamp word, low byte
 *     0x4025xx  MOV word [EAX+2],0xF0FE         -> 0xFE = "nothing pending"
 *   +0x03  byte   bDispatchFlag / bStampHigh / bLinkFlags
 *     0x402b47  or  %bl,0x3(%ecx)               -> high byte; low nibble kept
 *     (advance) MOV word [EAX+2],0x10xx         -> 0x10 dispatch flag
 *     0x407616  or byte [eax+3],0x2             -> "span group pending" bit
 *     0x4023df  test byte [edi+3],0x2           -> same bit, sweep arming test
 *   +0x04  byte   bLayerFlags
 *     0x406ff1  mov 0x4(%eax),%al ; and $0x90  -> mask 0x90 query
 *     0x407009  mov 0x4(%eax),%al ; and $0xa0  -> mask 0xa0 query
 *     0x407021  mov 0x4(%eax),%al ; and $0xb0  -> mask 0xb0 query
 *     0x407041  mov 0x4(%eax),%al ; and $0x4f  -> mask 0x4f query
 *     This is a SEPARATE byte from bLayer at +0x05.  The first conversion of
 *     the four mask predicates read +0x05 and broke the EXIT click path.
 *   +0x05  byte   bLayer / bLinkSrc
 *     0x407c92  mov 0x5(%ecx),%dl               -> layer selector
 *     0x4073f4  mov 0x5(%ecx),%cl               -> link source, the same byte
 *     0x407c96  mov %bl,0x5(%ecx)               -> layer latch, NOT link flags
 *   +0x06  word   wCellStamp   (bCellKeyLow +0x06, bCellKeyHigh +0x07)
 *     0x402b05  mov %cl,0x6(%edx)               -> cell-key low byte
 *     0x402b14  mov %cl,0x7(%edx)               -> cell-key high byte
 *     (process) MOVZX EDX,word [EAX+6]          -> the stamp, zero-extended
 *   +0x08  word   wCurXIdx / wDepthIndexX
 *     0x407c99  movzwl 0x8(%edi),%esi
 *     0x407425  movzwl 0x8(%ecx),%edi
 *   +0x0A  word   wCurYIdx / wDepthIndexY
 *     0x407cb5  movzwl 0xa(%edi),%esi
 *     0x407429  movzwl 0xa(%ecx),%edx
 *   +0x0C..+0x0F   padding: 0x417218 points at one 16-byte arena slot.
 *
 * WRITE an offset only against those bytes.  The +0x00/+0x01/+0x02/+0x03 and
 * +0x05..+0x0A bytes above are the whole record; an earlier revision of this
 * header inserted two extra fields ahead of the cursor words, which silently
 * shifted bLinkSrc to +0x06 and the cursors to +0x0C/+0x0E and made the retire
 * path compute a slot index from the wrong word (fault at 0x4012d6).
 */
````

</details>

<details><summary>Original leading conversion notes</summary>

````text
// ClearWritableDataSpanOnce @ 0x0040ef90 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NETWALK.EXE)
// Run-once start-up initialiser called first from entry(): on the first pass only it byte-zeroes the writable span [0x4121b0, 0x417820) (0x5670 = 22128 bytes) and then latches its guard dword to 1; later passes do nothing.
// Status: done
/*
 * Body 0x0040ef90..0x0040efc0, 17 instructions, 49 (0x31) bytes. Non-degenerate;
 * disassembly and decompiler agree. PURE LEAF: no calls (get_function_callees is
 * empty), no stack arguments, no return value.
 *
 * Disassembly (verbatim, from the bridge):
 *
 *   0x0040ef90  PUSH EDI
 *   0x0040ef91  PUSH ECX                 ; register save; ECX is also the REP counter
 *   0x0040ef92  MOV EAX,[0x00411dc0]     ; EAX = guard dword (statically 0)
 *   0x0040ef97  OR  EAX,EAX
 *   0x0040ef99  JNZ 0x0040efbe           ; guard != 0 -> skip everything
 *   0x0040ef9f  MOV EDI,0x4121b0         ; EDI = span begin
 *   0x0040efa4  MOV ECX,0x417820         ; ECX = span end (one past last byte)
 *   0x0040efa9  SUB ECX,EDI              ; ECX = end - begin = 0x5670
 *   0x0040efab  JCXZ 0x0040efbe          ; tests CX only (low 16 bits!)
 *   0x0040efae  XOR EAX,EAX              ; AL = 0, the STOSB fill byte
 *   0x0040efb0  CLD                      ; force DF = 0 (forward fill)
 *   0x0040efb1  STOSB.REP ES:EDI         ; zero ECX bytes at ES:EDI, byte-granular
 *   0x0040efb3  MOV ECX,0x1
 *   0x0040efb8  MOV [0x00411dc0],ECX     ; guard = 1 (dword)
 *   0x0040efbe  POP ECX
 *   0x0040efbf  POP EDI
 *   0x0040efc0  RET
 *
 * SIZE (both ways). body_start 0x40ef90, body_end 0x40efc0; the last byte is the
 * 1-byte plain RET at 0x40efc0, so size = 0x40efc0 - 0x40ef90 + 1 = 0x31 = 49.
 * The selector's 52 spans 0x40ef90..0x40efc3 inclusive and swallows the three
 * INT3 pad bytes CC CC CC at 0x40efc1..0x40efc3; the next function,
 * InitializeGlobalsAndInstanceTag (first instruction PUSH 0x8c = 68 8c 00 00),
 * begins at 0x40efc4. 49 + 3 = 52, exactly the 3-byte excess.
 *
 * (a) THE SPAN. EDI = (nw_data_window + 0x11b0) and ECX = 0x00417820 are two absolute virtual
 * addresses; SUB ECX,EDI reduces the pair to a LENGTH, ECX = 0x00417820 -
 * (nw_data_window + 0x11b0) = 0x5670 = 22128, consumed directly as the REP count. So the two
 * constants are an ADDRESS PAIR reduced to a length, not a length plus an
 * address. The zeroed region is [(nw_data_window + 0x11b0), 0x00417820) -- END EXCLUSIVE --
 * 22128 bytes; the last byte cleared is (nw_data_window + 0x681f), and the byte AT 0x00417820
 * is NOT touched.  (0x00417820 is a bound, not a cleared byte.)
 *
 *   SECTION CONTEXT (PE section table, ImageBase 0x00400000). Both endpoints are
 *   INTERIOR to one section, ".CRT$XIA", VA [(nw_data_window + 0x0), 0x00418000), so they are
 *   NOT a data-section boundary pair. That section's raw data is only 0x1200
 *   bytes (file-backed VA [(nw_data_window + 0x0), (nw_data_window + 0x1200))); the remainder is loader-zeroed
 *   BSS, so this span straddles that raw/BSS boundary at (nw_data_window + 0x1200) (0x50 bytes in).
 *   Raw image bytes at the endpoints are all 0x00: (nw_data_window + 0x11b0) = 00 00 00 00 ...,
 *   (nw_data_window + 0x681f) = 00, 0x00417820 = 00. Just before the span, a pointer table ends at
 *   (nw_data_window + 0x11b0) ((nw_data_window + 0x11a0) holds 0x0040dfb0, 0x0041008c, 0x0040dfd8, 0x0041009c).
 *
 * (b) THE JCXZ. After SUB ECX,EDI the code runs JCXZ, which tests the 16-bit CX,
 * i.e. the LOW 16 BITS of ECX, not the 32-bit count. It can only detect a
 * difference whose low 16 bits are all zero; a difference of 0x10000 (65536) or
 * any multiple of 0x10000 reads as "zero length" and would SILENTLY skip the
 * fill. It is therefore not a general zero-length guard. A complete guard would
 * test all 32 bits: JECXZ, or TEST ECX,ECX / JZ. Here the low 16 bits are 0x5670
 * (non-zero), so JCXZ is NOT taken and the fill runs.
 *
 * (c) REP STOSB SEMANTICS. XOR EAX,EAX zeroes AL, and CLD explicitly clears the
 * direction flag, so the code FORCES DF = 0 rather than relying on it already
 * being clear. REP STOSB then writes the single byte 0x00, ECX (= 0x5670) times,
 * through ES:EDI with EDI incrementing -- a BYTE-granular forward fill, not a
 * dword fill. Byte-at-a-time costs roughly 4x the store traffic of REP STOSD, but
 * it is alignment-agnostic (no requirement that the span be dword-aligned), which
 * is why a byte fill is used for an arbitrary-address span.
 *
 * (d) GUARD AND ORDERING. The guard dword at (nw_data_window + 0xdc0) is READ and tested first
 * (0x40ef92) and written only at the END (0x40efb8), after the fill. BOTH early
 * exits -- JNZ at 0x40ef99 and JCXZ at 0x40efab -- target 0x0040efbe, the
 * POP ECX / POP EDI / RET epilogue, which is AFTER the guard store at 0x40efb8.
 * So the guard is set ONLY on the fall-through path that actually performed the
 * fill; a JCXZ-taken skip does NOT latch the guard and will re-attempt on the
 * next call rather than being treated as done. No path sets the guard without the
 * fill. The value stored is 1, as a dword (MOV ECX,1; MOV [0x411dc0],ECX).
 *
 * (e) PROLOGUE / EPILOGUE. PUSH EDI / PUSH ECX preserve EDI and ECX across the
 * body (ECX is also overwritten as the REP counter, so the pushed copy is
 * restored by POP ECX). The function reads no arguments off the stack, returns
 * nothing, and contains no calls: a plain leaf. Memory at (nw_data_window + 0xdc0) in the
 * image is the dword 0x00000000 (immediately followed at (nw_data_window + 0xdc4) by the ASCII
 * string "\win32s.ini"), so the guard is zero on load and the FIRST run in the
 * static image DOES perform the fill.
 *
 * (g) CALLER. get_function_callers returns exactly one caller, entry (VA
 * 0x0040def8 = PE AddressOfEntryPoint RVA 0xdef8 + ImageBase 0x00400000). The
 * CALL to this function is the FIRST call entry makes, right after its SEH
 * prologue and MOV [EBP-4],0, and before entry calls InitializeGlobalsAndInstanceTag
 * (0x0040efc4) and the rest of the start-up chain (0x40f250, an import via
 * [0x401aa8], 0x40f290, 0x40f370, 0x40f380, 0x40ec00, then the window/audio
 * bring-up). It zeroes exactly one 22128-byte span, not the whole writable
 * section, so it is a targeted run-once zero-fill, NOT a general zero-BSS
 * initialiser.
 */
````

</details>

<details><summary>Original leading conversion notes</summary>

````text
/* DispatchExitHooksAndClearShutdownFlags -- NETWALK.EXE, entry 0x0040ed04.
 *
 * The shipped body is 0x0040ed04..0x0040ed98 (149 bytes), ending in the bare RET
 * at 0x0040ed98; 0x0040ed99..0x0040ed9b are int3 padding.  It takes one 4-byte
 * argument and is cdecl: each forwarding call pushes the incoming argument and
 * then executes `add esp,4` itself (0x0040ed4b/0x0040ed55 and
 * 0x0040ed80/0x0040ed89), so the callee does not pop it.
 *
 * The window slots, derived from the original absolute operands and the
 * original window base 0x00411000 (nw_data_window is that window at
 * 0x00418030, delta +0x7030):
 *
 *   0x00411dbc -> +0xdbc   shutdown-in-progress dword (set to 1)
 *   0x00411db8 -> +0xdb8   shutdown flag tested after the direct drain
 *   0x00411db4 -> +0xdb4   shutdown flag tested before Terminate
 *   0x00411ccc -> +0xccc   current entry of the descending exit-hook table
 *   0x00417410 -> +0x6410  runtime-patched one-argument override hook
 *   0x00417414 -> +0x6414  runtime-patched no-argument exit hook
 *
 * (The task note's +0xfcc for 0x00411ccc is off by 0x300: 0x411ccc - 0x411000
 * is 0xccc, and fix_movdir.py independently records the rebased address as
 * 0x418cfc = nw_data_window + 0xccc.)
 *
 * Callback ABIs are fixed by the call sites, not by their names:
 *
 *   - 0x0040ed2f `ff 10` (call dword ptr [eax]) with no pushes and no stack
 *     cleanup: one no-argument callee.  A no-argument stdcall and a no-argument
 *     cdecl are indistinguishable and both leave the stack unchanged, so the
 *     table entries are typed `void (*)(void)`.
 *   - 0x0040ed4f `ff 15 10 74 41 00` after `push [esp+4]`, followed by
 *     `add esp,4`: software-cdecl, one 32-bit argument.
 *   - 0x0040ed71 `ff 15 14 74 41 00` with no push and no cleanup: one
 *     no-argument callee.
 *   - 0x0040ed84 calls 0x0040ee90 after one push and then `add esp,4`; the
 *     existing definition of TerminateWithExitStatusCode is cdecl with one
 *     UINT argument and never returns.
 *   - 0x0040ed5a calls DrainHandlerTableAndCallExitHooks, whose existing
 *     definition is __stdcall(void).
 *
 * The descending table is walked exactly as the bytes do: the initial state is
 * skipped when [0xdb8] is nonzero, when the table pointer is NULL, or when the
 * pointed-to entry is zero.  Each iteration calls the current entry, subtracts
 * 4 from the table pointer, and repeats only when the next entry is nonzero.
 * The globals are volatile because the original reloads them after every call;
 * a callback is allowed to patch the table pointer or the flags.
 *
 * This is ordinary C and is not in the verbatim .nwleaf section.  This leaf
 * base has no .nwdiag output-section pin, and forcing the section attribute
 * here makes the orphan .nwdiag land on .data at 0x00418000, so the object is
 * left in .text; a build that pins .nwdiag can move it there with one section
 * attribute.  The bare symbol name is retained because the remaining asm
 * caller at 0x0040df6d references it without a leading underscore.
 */
````

</details>

<details><summary>Original leading conversion notes</summary>

````text
/*
 * DispatchPendingCommandLoop -- NETWALK.EXE 0x00405ab0..0x00405eba (inclusive),
 * 1035 bytes (0x40b), 257 instructions.  Ordinary-C reconstruction of the
 * record/command pump.
 *
 * ABI
 *   One dword stack argument, read at [esp+0x78] after the 0x64-byte local
 *   frame and the EBX/EBP/ESI/EDI saves.  Both exits are `ret 0x4`, so the
 *   effective signature is:
 *
 *       uint32_t __stdcall DispatchPendingCommandLoop(uint32_t arg);
 *
 *   The argument is stored at (nw_data_window + 0x62f0) and the second entry
 *   index checked by this invocation is arg + 2.
 *
 * THE INCOMING ESI VALUE
 *   In the original, ESI is a live register argument: the function never
 *   initialises it, and every tag-4/5/0xff path reads it before the 0x405e78
 *   arm replaces it with `pending_byte & 0x7f`.  The three direct call sites
 *   were traced:
 *
 *     0x403c20 (InitGlobalRngAndResetStateFlags) enters with ESI = 0,
 *              arg = 0; verified at runtime under winedbg.
 *     0x406495 (InitializeDispatchRecords) is reached only through native
 *              call-table slot 0x31 -> 0x408eac mode 2 -> 0x406390.
 *     0x4072bc (Fun_004072bc) is reached only through native call-table
 *              slot 0x0e.  Both native call instructions (0x407acb and
 *              0x409879) leave ESI pointing into VM bytecode.
 *
 *   On the latter two paths ESI is a valid bytecode/heap pointer, never a
 *   small opcode.  Every use is therefore identical to ESI = 0:
 *
 *     - tag 5  (0x405c57): `esi == 0x14` is false for a pointer and for 0;
 *     - tag 4  (0x405cc0): `(esi - 0x0f) > 10` sends a pointer and 0 to the
 *       generic opcode path;
 *     - tag 0xff and the generic path pass ESI as EOASO's opcode selector; a
 *       pointer and 0 both miss every comparison and take its default arm;
 *     - the post-EOASO checks at 0x405db6 compare ESI with 0x43/0x11/0x20/
 *       0x40/0x50/0x18/0x19, which a pointer and 0 both miss.
 *
 *   The register therefore has no observable value on any reachable entry
 *   path, and this C version models the incoming state as 0.  This is not a
 *   guessed opcode: it is the unique small value that is behaviourally
 *   equivalent to every proven caller state.
 *
 * LOCALS
 *   Original frame slots +0x10/+0x14/+0x18/+0x1c/+0x20 hold the five dwords
 *   threaded through the decoder and ExecuteOpcodeAndStoreOperand; +0x24..
 *   +0x6f is the 76-byte record scratch buffer; +0x70 holds arg + 2; EDI
````

````text
 *     and 0x0040ecdc "JECXZ 0x0040eccf" (into the body);

 * "\r\nSemaphore error\r\n" -- are an UNCLAIMED neighbour: /get_function_by_address
 * for 0x0040ecf7 returns "No function found". Separate error path, not this body.

 *   That range lies in .CRT$XIA (VMA (nw_data_window + 0x0), size 0x1200) -- the program's

 *   startup and mutable afterwards.

 *   the CMP -> else ZERO THE SLOT IN PLACE (MOV [EDI-4],EAX, with EAX zeroed at
 *   0x0040ecc8) BEFORE calling it. Zeroing first is what makes each registered
 *   handler run exactly once even if this loop were re-entered.
````

````text
// Status: done

 * 242 instructions).  The only return is `mov al,1; ret` at 0x004030f1 /
 * 0x004030fa: no arguments, no callee stack cleanup.

 *   [esp+0x10] record cursor (also the current record)
 *   [esp+0x14] child-list cursor
 *   [esp+0x18] old-sub-span spill (stored at 0x00403052, never reloaded)
 *
 * Record layout, 16-byte stride (all offsets below are byte offsets):
 *   +0x00 flags          low two bits == 3 marks a queued record; bit2 = span
 *                        arm, bit3 = inline reference payload
 *   +0x01 index          mask-table bit index / state-record index
 *   +0x02                untouched here
 *   +0x03 state flags    bit0: clear and skip this record
 *   +0x04, +0x05         copied to child+4/+5
 *   +0x06 word           anchor/span word, 0xFFFF means none
 *   +0x08 word           current span index (AdvanceGridCellSubSpan output)
 *   +0x0A word           previous span index
 *   +0x0C dword          pointer, or inline reference payload when bit3 set
 *
 * Data-window globals (original absolute -> relocated offset):
 *   0x412204 -> +0x1204 deferred record
 *   0x417240 -> +0x6240 record-stack top
 *   0x417244 -> +0x6244 record-stack bottom
 *   0x417388 -> +0x6388 mask-table pointer
 *   0x417218 -> +0x6218 current grid context
 *   0x41721C -> +0x621C grid user data (record depth)
 *   0x417248 -> +0x6248 state-record table
 *   0x417214 -> +0x6214 current state record
 *   0x4173E8 -> +0x63E8 VM base B
 *   0x417804 -> +0x6804 reached-cell flag
 *   0x4177F6 -> +0x67F6 cell mode
 *   0x4173EC -> +0x63EC dispatch index
 *   0x417230 -> +0x6230 current handler
 *   0x4177FF -> +0x67FF opcode flag
 *   0x4110F4 -> +0x00F4 eight-entry handler table
 *
 * The old verbatim blob spelled the handler table as an absolute 0x4110F4,
 * which now lands inside our .text.  All other globals were already rebased in
 * that blob; the table is rebased here like the rest of the window.
````

````text
 *   0040686d   5   68 c4 12 41 00    PUSH (nw_data_window + 0x2c4)   (immediate dword, NOT [mem])

 *              own; there is no SUB ESP and no [EBP+n] reference.
 *   CALL #1    pushes 0x0040686d (the address of PUSH (nw_data_window + 0x2c4)), so the
 *              callee's RET pops it and ESP is back at entry.
````

````text
 *   0x40605e  MOV  EDX,[ESP+0x0c]      ; arg1 (entry ESP+0x04) = key index
````

````text
// CopyDwordsAndFillTailWithSilence @ 0x0040a860 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Copies (dwByteCount>>2) DWORDs from pdwSrc to pdwDst, then pads the REST of a fixed
// 512-DWORD destination up to 0x200 DWORDs with the constant 0x80808080 (four bytes of
// 0x80, the unsigned-8-bit PCM silence level). Pure leaf, three stack args, returns nothing.
// Status: done
/*
 * TRUE SIZE = 44 bytes (0x2c), and BOTH derivations agree EXACTLY:
 *   - body formula: body_end 0x0040a88b - body_start 0x0040a860 + 1 = 0x2c = 44.
 *   - last instruction: RET 0xc == C2 0C 00 (3 bytes) at 0x0040a889, so its final byte
 *     0x00 IS 0x0040a88b. Raw read_memory @0x0040a860 (48 B) =
 *     55 8b ec 56 57 8b 4d 08 8b 75 0c c1 e9 02 8b 7d 10 89 c8 fc f3 a5 b9 00 02 00 00
 *     29 c1 74 07 b8 80 80 80 80 f3 ab 5f 5e 5d c2 0c 00 | 55
 *   - the byte at 0x0040a88c is 0x55 = PUSH EBP, the prologue of the NEXT function
 *     BlendSaturatedByteBuffers (0x0040a88c), NOT padding. Selector said 44: EXACT match.
 * 20 instructions, PURE LEAF, ZERO callees (bridge get_function_callees count=0).
 *
 * ============================ (a) ARGUMENT MAP ============================
 * Prologue PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP + epilogue RET 0xc => callee-cleaned, THREE stack
 * arguments. From the EBP frame:
 *   [EBP+0x04]  return address
 *   [EBP+0x08]  ARG1  dwByteCount  -> ECX   (MOV ECX,dword ptr [EBP+0x8])   BYTE COUNT
 *   [EBP+0x0c]  ARG2  pdwSrc       -> ESI   (MOV ESI,dword ptr [EBP+0xc])   SOURCE pointer
 *   [EBP+0x10]  ARG3  pdwDst       -> EDI   (MOV EDI,dword ptr [EBP+0x10])  DESTINATION pointer
 * So ARG1 is the BYTE COUNT, ARG2 the SOURCE, ARG3 the DESTINATION; RET 0xc pops exactly
 * these three. Confirmed byte-for-byte against the raw opcodes above.
 *
 * ==================== (b) SHR ECX,0x2 -> DWORD COUNT =====================
 * Opcode C1 /5 is SHR, i.e. a LOGICAL shift right by 2: ARG1 is treated as a BYTE COUNT and
 * the QUOTIENT is the REP MOVSD element count. A byte count that is NOT a multiple of four
 * loses its trailing one to three bytes: with count = 4k+r (r in 1..3), only the first 4k
 * bytes are moved. Those r bytes are NEVER copied (they are not loaded, not stored) and the
 * tail fill starts at the DWORD boundary AFTER the truncated count, i.e. source and
 * destination are both advanced in DWORD steps only. The function therefore SILENTLY DROPS
 * the remainder. Because the shift is LOGICAL (not SAR), a count whose bit 31 is set is
 * reinterpreted as a huge POSITIVE DWORD count (~0x40000000); that is a consequence of the
 * encoding but it is NOT reachable from this function's single caller, which clamps the byte
 * count to 0x800 (see (g)).
 *
 * ==================== (c) TAIL FILL and 0x80808080 ========================
 * After the copy, ECX = 0x200 - (copied DWORD count); when non-zero, REP STOSD writes the
 * immediate 0x80808080 into every remaining DWORD. 0x200 = 512 (0x200 = 2^9 = 512 decimal),
 * so the destination is a FIXED 512-DWORD = 2048-BYTE region and everything past the copied
 * data is filled with the byte 0x80. 0x80 is the MIDDLE of the unsigned 8-bit range 0..255 --
 * the SILENCE / zero-crossing level of unsigned 8-bit PCM -- and 0x80808080 replicates that
 * value four times so a single STOSD writes four samples at once.
 * CONFIRMED FROM EVIDENCE, not assumed:
 *   - sibling OpenWaveOutAndPrepareHeaderRing (0x00409f10) opens the device as WAVE_FORMAT_PCM,
 *     nChannels=1, wBitsPerSample=8, 11025 Hz, and builds an 8 x 0x800-byte buffer pool based
 *     at 0x412ea8 (c/OpenWaveOutAndPrepareHeaderRing.c).
 *   - sibling BlendSaturatedByteBuffers (0x0040a88c), the very next function, mixes byte-wise
 *     with an UNSIGNED SATURATING add centred on 0x80 (out = saturate(src + dst - 0x80)).
 *   - this function's caller FUN_0040ac80 mixes the source slots of the 0x412e28 table into
 *     0x412ea8 + index*0x800, i.e. into ONE waveOut pool buffer (see (g)).
 * So the evidence DOES support an unsigned 8-bit PCM sample buffer: it is exactly the waveOut
 * 8-bit mono output pool, and 0x80 is that format's silence value. (The one wrinkle is that
 * the sibling blend clamps to 0xF0, leaving the top 15 levels unused -- a headroom choice in
 * the mixer, not evidence against the format.)
 *
 * ==================== (d) JZ AND THE OVERFLOW EDGE =======================
 * When the copied DWORD count equals 0x200 exactly, SUB gives zero and JZ (74 07 -> 0x0040a886)
 * SKIPS the fill entirely -- correct, because the whole 512-DWORD region was already written by
 * the copy. When the count EXCEEDS 0x200, 0x200 - count wraps to a large positive value and the
 * REP STOSD fill runs WILD past the destination region. The count is NOT bounded by this
 * function itself; that is a LATENT OVERFLOW if it is ever called with more than 2048 bytes. It
 * is unreachable from the only caller, FUN_0040ac80, which clamps the byte count to 0x800
 * (<= 2048) before the call. Stated as a latent hazard, not a design bug.
 *
 * ==================== (e) RETURN VALUE AND CONVENTION ====================
 * The function returns NOTHING meaningful. EAX is left holding:
 *   - 0x80808080 on the fill path (MOV EAX,0x80808080 at 0x0040a87f; REP STOSD and the POPs
 *     never touch EAX), and
 *   - the DWORD copy count on the JZ-skipped path (EAX still holds ECX from MOV EAX,ECX).
 * Either way the caller cannot rely on it; the C returns void. The frame plus RET 0xc identify
 * a callee-cleaned, three-argument __stdcall-shaped Win32 convention.
 *
 * ============================ (f) TRUE SIZE ==============================
 * Covered above: 44 bytes, both ways, and the following byte is the next function's prologue.
 *
 * ============================ (g) THE CALLER =============================
 * get_function_callers returns EXACTLY ONE: FUN_0040ac80 (0x0040ac80). It is the waveOut
 * software MIXER. It walks the 16-byte-stride slot table at 0x412e28 (record: +0 active/handle,
 * +4 source cursor, +8 remaining byte count), computes the destination as
 *   0x412ea8 + (byte returned by handler-table slot [0x411638]) * 0x800
 * (SHL EBP,0xb / ADD EBP,0x412ea8), then for each ACTIVE slot copies
 *   ESI = min([slot+8], 0x800) bytes from [slot+4] to that destination,
 * calling THIS function for the FIRST slot (edi==0) and BlendSaturatedByteBuffers (0x0040a88c)
 * for every later slot -- so one source is laid down and the rest are summed in, i.e. a mixer.
 *   - destination: 0x412ea8 + n*0x800 -- one of the 8 pool buffers that
 *     OpenWaveOutAndPrepareHeaderRing built at the 0x412ea8 audio pool. [0x411638] is
 *     handler-table slot 6, which the audio initialiser binds to the waveOut header-index
 *     selector. It is a WAVEOUT destination, not MIDI and not MCI.
 *   - source: each active entry's [slot+4] cursor (a streaming source buffer).
 *   - byte count: each active entry's [slot+8] remaining length, clamped to 0x800.
 * The caller touches NEITHER the MIDI globals (0x412de0/0x412de4/0x412dec/0x412df0/0x412df8)
 * NOR the MCI globals (0x412e20/0x412e24). REFUTING the brief's "MIDI or MCI" framing: this
 * caller belongs to a THIRD path -- the waveOut / 8-bit PCM software mixer. Its only globals
 * are 0x412e28 (the slot table), 0x412ea8 (the audio pool base), 0x416ea8 (slot count) and
 * 0x416eb0 (processed count), plus the handler-table slots 0x411638 / 0x411620.
 *
 * ============================== (h) NAME ================================
 * CopyDwordsAndFillTailWithSilence -- states the DWORD copy with the 0x80 (silence) tail fill.
 */
````

````text
// DecodeMidiTrackVariableLengthQuantity @ 0x0040a170 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NETWALK.EXE)
// Decodes a one- or two-byte variable-length quantity from the shared MIDI-track read cursor
// g_pMidiTrackCursor (0x00412e00), advancing the cursor in place; returns the value zero-extended.
// Status: done
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// VERIFIED DISASSEMBLY (15 instructions, 0x0040a170..0x0040a1a1 = 50 bytes; plain RET => no
// stack arguments; body has ZERO calls => pure leaf).  Bytes re-read from the image and matched:
//
//   0x40a170  31 d2              XOR EDX,EDX                  ; accumulator = 0 (zero-extended)
//   0x40a172  a1 00 2e 41 00     MOV EAX,[0x00412e00]         ; EAX = track cursor (a POINTER)
//   0x40a177  8a 10              MOV DL,byte ptr [EAX]        ; first byte -> DL (bits 8..31 stay 0)
//   0x40a179  ff 05 00 2e 41 00  INC dword ptr [0x00412e00]   ; advance cursor  (CONSUMES a byte)
//   0x40a17f  f6 c2 80           TEST DL,0x80                 ; continuation bit?
//   0x40a182  74 1b              JZ  0x0040a19f               ; bit7 clear -> return first byte as-is
//   0x40a184  81 e2 7f 00 00 00  AND EDX,0x7f                 ; keep low 7 bits of the first byte
//   0x40a18a  31 c0              XOR EAX,EAX                  ; clear EAX so MOV AL below zero-extends
//   0x40a18c  8b 0d 00 2e 41 00  MOV ECX,[0x00412e00]         ; ECX = cursor (already advanced)
//   0x40a192  8a 01              MOV AL,byte ptr [ECX]        ; second byte -> AL (high bit NOT masked)
//   0x40a194  c1 e0 07           SHL EAX,0x7                  ; SECOND byte shifted left by SEVEN
//   0x40a197  09 c2              OR  EDX,EAX                  ; value = (b1 & 0x7f) | (b2 << 7)
//   0x40a199  ff 05 00 2e 41 00  INC dword ptr [0x00412e00]   ; advance cursor again (2nd byte)
//   0x40a19f  8b c2              MOV EAX,EDX                  ; return value in EAX
//   0x40a1a1  c3                 RET                          ; 1-byte plain RET (last body byte)
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ENCODING  --  a TWO-BYTE-ONLY 7-bit-per-byte packing (a TRUNCATED variable-length quantity):
//
//   * The FIRST byte is read through the global pointer 0x412e00 and the pointer is then
//     incremented.  If bit 7 of that byte is CLEAR the function returns the byte itself
//     (already <= 0x7f).  If bit 7 of that byte is SET the byte is masked with 0x7f, a SECOND
//     byte is read from the NEW pointer value WITHOUT masking its high bit, shifted left SEVEN,
//     ORed into the accumulator, and the pointer is incremented a second time.
//   * The second byte's own bit 7 is NOT tested.  It therefore LEAKS into the result as bit 14
//     -- it is DATA here, not a continuation flag.  (For 0x40a192 loads the whole byte with no
//     AND, and 0x40a194 shifts the whole 32-bit EAX by 7.)
//   * There is NO loop and NO continuation test on the second byte, so the function handles
//     encodings of AT MOST TWO BYTES.  It is a genuine two-byte decoder, NOT the classic 3-/4-byte
//     MIDI variable-length-quantity loop (which tests bit 7 of every byte and keeps shifting).
//     It is a TRUNCATED loop: correct for a standard two-byte VLV (value < 0x4000, where the
//     second byte's bit 7 is 0 by construction), but for a standard 3-/4-byte VLV it produces a
//     WRONG value (a spurious bit 14) and consumes only the first two bytes.
//
// BIT WIDTH & SHIFT  --  SHL EAX,0x7 is a shift by SEVEN (imm8 = 0x07), proven at 0x40a194.
//   The second byte contributes bits 7..14 and the first byte's low seven bits are bits 0..6,
//   i.e. 7 bits per byte.  The returned value can therefore occupy AT MOST 15 bits
//   (range 0..0x7FFF = (0x7f) | (0xff << 7)).  The accumulator is the 32-bit register EDX and
//   the result is copied to EAX, so the C return type is a 32-bit DWORD even though neither byte
//   supplies a bit above bit 14.
//
// RETURN TYPE / CONVENTION  --  returns the decoded value in EAX; takes NO arguments and ends in a
//   plain RET (pops only the return address), so it is a no-argument cdecl/leaf function.  XOR EAX,EAX
//   at 0x40a18a clears the upper 24 bits before MOV AL loads the second byte (and EDX is XOR-ed to 0
//   at entry before MOV DL), so the value is ZERO-EXTENDED: there is NO sign extension and the value
//   is UNSIGNED.
//
// CURSOR  --  0x00412e00 is a POINTER variable (loaded into EAX/ECX and dereferenced).  Both INC
//   instructions advance it IN PLACE, so it is a read cursor SHARED ACROSS CALLS: the function
//   CONSUMES bytes from a byte stream and is NOT idempotent (two calls on the same cursor return
//   different bytes).  read_memory at 0x412e00 returns 0x00 (its static image value is zero), so the
//   pointed-to buffer is RUNTIME-populated -- the whole 0x412de0..0x412e2x audio-globals block is
//   zero in the image.
//
// THE STREAM (from the single caller)  --  get_function_callers(0x40a170) returns exactly ONE caller,
//   FUN_0040a1a4 (0x0040a1a4, 0x40a1a4..0x40a2e4).  That function is a MIDI-file / sequencer playback
//   loop writing channel events through midiOutShortMsg (IAT 0x61) and pacing them with timeGetTime
//   (IAT 0x62); it handles running status, the 0x80/0x90/0xC0/0xD0 channel-status nibbles, and the
//   0xF0/0xF7 sys-ex and 0xFF meta events.  It calls THIS function twice:
//     (1) 0x40a1e6  CALL 0x40a170 then 0x40a1eb  ADD [0x412e00],EAX  -- decode the LENGTH field of a
//         0xF0/0xF7/0xFF event and SKIP that many bytes of the track stream, and
//     (2) 0x40a2b2  CALL 0x40a170  -- decode the DELTA-TIME before an event, which the caller scales
//         x10 (LEA EAX,[EAX+EAX*4] / ADD EAX,EAX) and accumulates into the clock accumulator at
//         0x412dec, busy-waiting on timeGetTime until the target is reached.
//   So the consumed stream is a MIDI track/event byte stream (SMF-style).  This cursor is NOT the MCI
//   CD-audio command stream: the recovered MCI/CD-audio functions in c/ use 0x412e20 (winmm task id)
//   and 0x412e24 (audio-enabled gate), and the recovered MIDI-output functions use 0x412de0
//   (g_hMidiOut) / 0x412de4 / 0x412de8 / 0x412e05 / 0x412e08 -- the same audio-subsystem region but
//   DIFFERENT fields.  No recovered file in c/ names 0x412e00; it is used only by FUN_0040a1a4.
//
// SIZE  --  TRUE size = 0x0040a1a1 - 0x0040a170 + 1 = 0x32 = 50 bytes (the RET at 0x40a1a1 IS the last
//   byte); confirmed both by get_function_by_address(body_end = 0x40a1a1) and by byte inspection.
//   The inventory selector's size column ("34B" = 0x34 = 52) is = distance to the NEXT function
//   (0x40a1a4); its 2-byte excess is exactly the two 0xCC INT3 alignment-padding bytes at
//   0x40a1a2 and 0x40a1a3 (next function FUN_0040a1a4 begins at 0x40a1a4 with 0x50 = PUSH EAX).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
````

````text
// HandleAudioTransportOpcode @ 0x00408e1c (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Opcode 0-9 handler that drives NetWalk's audio-transport state: it latches a few mode/flag bytes, and on opcodes 8 and 9 calls into the MCI command helpers to stop or start playback; always returns 1.
// Status: done
/*
 * ROLE — This is NOT an mciSendString dispatcher and never formats a reply string into any
 * caller buffer. It contains no string comparison and no string literals of any kind; the only
 * two calls it makes are to the MCI command-message helpers recovered as siblings:
 *
 *   DispatchMciPlaybackCommand  @ 0x0040a9c0  (opcode 8 -> STOP path, op arg 0)
 *   DispatchMciSetFlagsAndPlay @ 0x0040a958  (opcode 9 -> SET-then-PLAY path)
 *
 * Those two use mciSendCommandA (command-message form) against the winmm task id at @0x412e20,
 * gated by the audio-enabled flag at @0x412e24. THIS function never reads either global itself —
 * it only decides WHICH helper to call, and with what one-byte argument. The gate is applied
 * inside the helpers, so opcode 8/9 are dispatched unconditionally here.
 *
 * Shape: `__stdcall` (RET 0x4 pops the single DWORD argument), 38 instructions, one computed
 * dispatch — `CMP EBX,9 / JA epilogue / JMP DWORD [EBX*4 + 0x4114dc]` — through a 10-entry jump
 * table whose contents were read from .data and match the decompilation case for case:
 *
 *   idx 0 -> 0x408e2f   idx 5 -> 0x408e63
 *   idx 1 -> 0x408e2f   idx 6 -> 0x408e6f
 *   idx 2 -> 0x408e37   idx 7 -> 0x408e6f
 *   idx 3 -> 0x408e47   idx 8 -> 0x408e7a
 *   idx 4 -> 0x408e5a   idx 9 -> 0x408e8a
 *
 * Opcodes above 9 (and every other path) fall into the shared epilogue at 0x408ea3, which is
 * `MOV EAX,1 / POP EBX / RET 0x4`. The return value is therefore the constant 1 on EVERY path,
 * including out-of-range opcodes, and including opcodes 8/9 whose helper return values are
 * discarded (the helper result in EAX is overwritten by the epilogue's MOV EAX,1).
 *
 * Per-opcode effect on the latched state:
 *   0, 1  latch the raw opcode into @0x417342 (two opcodes share one slot; the slot is what
 *         later code reads to tell which of the two it was)
 *   2     clear the mode flag @0x417340 and its paired value byte @0x4177fa
 *   3     set @0x417340 = 1 and copy the configured byte @0x417806 into @0x4177fa
 *   4     clear @0x4177fb
 *   5     copy the configured byte @0x417807 into @0x4177fb
 *   6, 7  latch (opcode - 6) into @0x417343 — the asm is `ADD AL,0xfa`, i.e. +250 == -6 mod 256,
 *         so this is a 0/1 selector, not the opcode itself
 *   8     STOP the transport (helper called with op 0 = MCI_STOP, unconditionally), then clear
 *         the playback-armed flag @0x417344
 *   9     if the stored flag byte @0x417345 is not 0xff, sign-extend it and pass it to the
 *         SET-then-PLAY helper; then SET @0x417344 = 1 regardless of whether the helper ran
 *
 * So 8 and 9 are the pair that actually moves the transport (stop vs. configure-and-play), and
 * @0x417344 is the resulting "playback armed" state byte: 0 after a stop, 1 after a start.
 * @0x417345's 0xff sentinel means "no playback request recorded", i.e. opcode 9 is a no-op
 * call-wise but still sets the armed flag.
 *
 * ALL globals touched are single bytes, verified against the image bytes (all 0x00 in the file,
 * i.e. runtime-populated). No dword/pointer global is written anywhere in this body.
 *
 * Entry mechanism (UNRESOLVED IN DETAIL, but the slot is proven): the bridge reports callers=0
 * and a scan of the contiguous .text range 0x401000..0x40de00 finds NO immediate equal to this
 * entry (0x408e1c) — the negative is trustworthy, proven with in-body controls 0x4114dc /
 * 0x417342 / 0x4177fa all found. However, .data slot @0x4113cc holds exactly 0x00408e1c (read
 * directly), and it is entry index 60 of a dense ASCENDING function-pointer table spanning
 * @0x4112dc..0x411400 (74 entries; the entries just outside, @0x4112d8 = 0x2e and @0x411404 =
 * 0x05060700, are not code, so the bounds are real). @0x4112dc IS indexed from code
 * (`JMP DWORD [EBX*4+0x4112dc]`, with `CMP EBX,6 / JA` before it), so this is a genuine
 * indirect opcode-handler table — but the specific dispatcher that selects index 60 was not
 * located in the scanned range, and index 60 is beyond the bounds guard of the dispatchers found
 * (@0x4112f8 with CMP EBX,4; @0x41130c via CALL [reg*4+...]). Therefore: this function is a
 * slot in a handler table, and WHICH code path reaches slot 60 is UNRESOLVED — not invented.
 */
````

````text
// InitializeAudioSubsystemAndUtHandlerTable @ 0x0040a7bc (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Opens the waveOut device and its 8-header ring, opens MIDI out and raises the timer
// resolution, then publishes the twelve audio UT notification handlers; returns FALSE
// (after rolling the whole subsystem back) only when BOTH halves failed.
// Status: done
/*
 * TRUE SIZE = 164 bytes, and BOTH derivations agree exactly:

 *   - real last instruction: RET 0x4 at 0x0040a85c is 3 bytes (C2 04 00), so the last
 *     byte really is 0x0040a85e. The 0xCC at 0x0040a85f is INT3 padding and belongs to

 * which pops the argument the CALLER pushed. Verified at 0x0040a7bc: PUSH [ESP+0x4]

 * ORed here and otherwise passed as the next call's argument.

 * passed to timeBeginPeriod — survives; the identification of which stack slot holds
 * what does not, and "no parameters" is refuted by the only call site, which pushes
 * exactly one dword immediately before the call. Net effect for this caller: the argument
 * is 0 or 1, so the floor always wins and the period comes out as 10 ms.

 * the exact order in the binary and is NOT ascending; the slot index is given for each.
 * These are the same 12 slots the Win9x loader InitializeUtDriverAndHandlerTable

 * 0x0040a0c4 (slot 4), 0x0040a0f4 (slot 9), 0x0040a414 (slot 1), 0x0040a48c (slot 3),
 * 0x0040a494 (slot 5) and 0x0040a4c4 (slot 10) fall outside the dumped range and their
 * bodies are UNEXAMINED — no claim is made about them here.

 * directly, with no thunk wrapper.

 * established: 0x412cd8 + the 0x412ce0 ring from OpenWaveOutAndPrepareHeaderRing, and
 * 0x412de0 + 0x412e08 (and 0x412de8 via ResetMidiOutAndTimerEvent) from

 * INDIRECTLY (`MOV EAX,0x40a7bc ; CALL EAX` at 0x0040ab0c/0x0040ab11). It picks between
 * 0x40a7bc and the UT loader 0x40a684 from GetVersion().

 * `TEST EBX,0x80000000 ; JZ 0x0040ab0c ; CMP BL,0x4 ; JNC 0x0040ab0c ; MOV EAX,0x40a684`.
 * So a CLEAR bit 31 jumps STRAIGHT to THIS function (0x40a7bc), and 0x40a684 is taken ONLY
 * when bit 31 is SET *and* the low byte is BELOW 4. That is the **Win32s-on-3.1** shape
 * (major 3, high bit set). Windows 9x reports major 4 with the high bit set and therefore
 * falls through the `JNC` to THIS function, exactly like NT (bit 31 clear). Hence 0x40a684
 * is NOT a "Win9x UT loader" — it is the Win32s arm, and this function serves BOTH NT and
 * 9x. The orchestration facts (one caller, return consumed) below are unaffected.
 * The brief's "4 callers" is wrong; the live count is 1.
 * The return value IS consumed: `TEST AL,AL ; JZ 0x0040ab6b` immediately after the
 * indirect call at 0x0040ab13, i.e. the caller branches to its own failure path on FALSE.
````

````text
// InitializeAudioSubsystemThenDispatchPlaybackAndPendingSlotHook @ 0x00408f8c (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)

 *   0x408f92 PUSH 0x0                      ; push #2  -> ARG3
 *   0x408f94 PUSH 0x417806                 ; push #3  -> ARG2
 *   0x408f99 PUSH 0x417807                 ; push #4 (last) -> ARG1
 *   0x408f9e CALL 0x0040aae0               ; RET 0x10 callee pops the four dwords
 *   0x408fa3 MOV AL,[0x00417345]
 *   0x408fa8 CMP AL,0xff
 *   0x408faa JZ 0x00408fb5                 ; rel8 +9, target 0x408fb5 (past the next call)
 *   0x408fac MOVSX ECX,AL
 *   0x408faf PUSH ECX
 *   0x408fb0 CALL 0x004090d0
 *   0x408fb5 CMP dword ptr [0x00417364],-0x1
 *   0x408fbc JZ 0x00408fc9                 ; rel8 +0x0b, target 0x408fc9 (the RET)

 * === (a) THE DEDICATED-ARGUMENT CHECK --- CONFIRMED, ARG3 INCLUDED ===
 * The parent's reading is CORRECT. From the callee's own recovered file,
 * c/InitializeAudioSubsystemByOsVersionAndOpenMciDevice.c, its signature is __stdcall
 * RET 0x10 = FOUR arguments:
 *   ARG1 [ESP+0x8]  BYTE  *pbOutSlot5
 *   ARG2 [ESP+0xc]  BYTE  *pbOutSlot4

 *   push #1 [0x41735c]  -> ARG4 = the VALUE at 0x41735c (a DWORD, the count source; the
 *                                 callee reads only its low byte as the slot count)
 *   push #2 0x0         -> ARG3 = the CONSTANT 0 (the unused third argument)
 *   push #3 0x417806    -> ARG2 = the ADDRESS 0x417806 (an OUT byte pointer)
 *   push #4 0x417807    -> ARG1 = the ADDRESS 0x417807 (an OUT byte pointer)

 * third argument the callee never reads. Note the two OUT pointers are ADJACENT bytes
 * (0x417806 and 0x417807); the callee writes slot 4's AL through ARG2 (0x417806) and
 * slot 5's AL through ARG1 (0x417807). Both bytes read 0 in the static image.
 * RETURN VALUE: NOT INSPECTED. The instruction after the CALL (0x408fa3) reads global

 *

 * c/UpdateMciAudioStateAndPlay.c documents that DispatchMciAudioReset @0x4090c0 "resets
 * @0x417345 to 0xff", and 0x417345 is the same byte that callee later overwrites with the

 * the only validation; the callee does not re-check it).

 * (read_memory @0x417340: byte at +5 is 0). Since 0x00 != 0xff the JZ is NOT taken and the
 * playback-dispatch branch IS taken in the static image. (Note: at run time the first call
 * would itself rewrite this byte 0xff via its reset, but statically, before any call, it is 0.)

 * The guard is MOV AL,[0x417345] ; CMP AL,0xff -- an 8-bit compare of the RAW byte (unsigned

 * NEGATIVE 32-bit values (-128..-1). That is a genuine asymmetry between how the byte is

 * on the consumer, and the consumer neutralises it: UpdateMciAudioStateAndPlay reads only
 * [ESP+4]'s low byte (MOV AL,[ESP+4]), stores that byte into 0x417345, and MOVSX EAX,AL again;

 * and NEVER becomes an index or a negative quantity that any code acts on. Verdict: a real
 * guard/use asymmetry in the bytes, but with NO observable effect because the callee consumes
 * the byte, not the 32-bit value. Stated plainly rather than as a bug.
 *
 * === (d) THE SECOND GUARDED STEP --- 0x417364, SENTINEL -1 ===
 * CMP dword ptr [0x417364],-0x1 ; JZ 0x408fc9 (skip to RET) ; else PUSH [0x417364] and
 * CALL 0x004072e4. -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) is the "no index published / nothing pending" sentinel for
 * that global: c/DispatchPendingSlotHookForIndex.c documents that its ResetPendingSlotHookState
 * "resets the pending-result global @0x417364 to -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)". The third callee,
 * DispatchPendingSlotHookForIndex @0x4072e4 (already recovered), is a gated dispatcher taking
 * ONE DWORD index (RET 0x4): it flushes pending state, and when enabled publishes the index into
 * 0x417364 and forwards table[index] through the slot hook. So a non -1 value here means "an
 * index is armed, dispatch it".
 * Static value of 0x417364 = 0x00000000 (read_memory @0x417340: at +0x24 the dword is 0). Since
 * 0 != -1 the JZ is NOT taken and the hook-dispatch branch IS taken in the static image. The
 * first call does not touch 0x417364, so the static 0 is the value seen by this compare.
 *
 * === (e) OVERALL SHAPE ===
 * Straight-line, no-branch-outcome, no-argument, no-return sequence:
 *   1) audio subsystem bring-up (four fixed arguments, return discarded), then
 *   2) IF @0x417345 != 0xff: dispatch the selected MCI playback mode, then
 *   3) IF @0x417364 != -1: dispatch the pending slot hook.
 * The two sentinels (0xff for "no selection", -1 for "no pending index") make the function
 * SAFE TO CALL when nothing is armed: set both to their sentinel and steps 2 and 3 are skipped,
 * leaving only a plain audio bring-up. FAILURE HANDLING: none in this function. The bring-up
 * callee always returns TRUE regardless of whether audio came up (per its recovered file), and

 *   - last instruction: the 1-byte RET (C3) at 0x00408fc9 IS body_end, so the body ends exactly
````

````text
// MixActiveAudioSlotsIntoWaveOutBuffer @ 0x0040ac80 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// waveOut 8-bit PCM software mixer: asks the handler slot for a pool-buffer index, lays the
// first active source slot into that buffer with a copy-and-silence-fill, sums every later
// active slot in with the saturating blend, then posts the mix via the notify slot; returning
// void, cdecl/plain (NO stack arguments).
// Status: done
/*
 * ============================================================================
 * TRUE SIZE = 133 bytes (0x85), and BOTH derivations agree EXACTLY:
 *   - body formula: body_end 0x0040ad04 - body_start 0x0040ac80 + 1 = 0x85 = 133.
 *   - real last instruction: RET at 0x0040ad04 is 1 byte (0xC3), so its only
 *     byte IS 0x0040ad04. Raw read_memory @0x40ac80 (140 B) tail:
 *       ... 40 74 06 ff 15 20 16 41 00 5f 5e 5d 5b c3 cc cc cc ff 15 3c 16 ...
 *     0x40ad00 POP EDI / 0x40ad01 POP ESI / 0x40ad02 POP EBP / 0x40ad03 POP EBX /
 *     0x40ad04 C3 = RET / 0x40ad05 CC / 0x40ad06 CC / 0x40ad07 CC / 0x40ad08 FF 15
 *     The next function begins at 0x40ad08 with CALL dword ptr [0x41163c].
 * 48 instructions (bridge get disassemble_function count=48), plain RET -> NO stack
 * args (get_function_variables: parameters [] locals []).
 *
 * THE SELECTOR'S 136 = 133 + the THREE 0xCC INT3 padding bytes at 0x40ad05, 0x40ad06
 * and 0x40ad07 (136 - 133 = 3). Those three bytes belong to no function.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * (a) *** THE POOL INDEX AND THE DESTINATION ADDRESS ***
 *   0x40ac86  CALL dword ptr [0x00411638]      ; FF 15 38 16 41 00
 *   0x40ac8c  MOVZX EAX,AL                     ; the handler's result is used as a BYTE
 *   0x40ac8f  MOV EBP,EAX
 *   0x40ac91  SHL EBP,0xb                      ; * 0x800 = * 2048
 *   0x40ac94  ADD EBP,0x412ea8                 ; + pool base
 * So the destination = 0x412ea8 + (returned-byte << 11). SHL by 11 IS a multiply by
 * 0x800 = 2048, the size of one waveOut PCM buffer. The MOVZX proves the code consumes
 * only the LOW BYTE of the slot's return value.
 *
 * THE SLOT IS READ STATICALLY AS 0x0040a520 — ReturnConstantOne (MOV AL,1 ; RET), its
 * image default. 0x411638 is INDEX 10 of the ONE CONTIGUOUS 16-SLOT array whose base is
 * 0x411610 (round-55 parent-verified): (0x411638-0x411610)/4 = 10. Equivalently it is
 * INDEX 6 of that array's 12-slot UT sub-table at 0x411620: (0x411638-0x411620)/4 = 6.
 * The slot is RUNTIME-PATCHED, so the static value is only the pre-init default:
 *   - waveOut path (InitializeAudioSubsystemAndUtHandlerTable @0x40a7bc) installs
 *     slot 6 = SelectWaveHeaderIndex @0x0040a030, a wave-header/buffer INDEX source
 *     (raw bytes b9 f0 2c 41 00 f6 01 01 74 0b 89 c8 2d f0 2c 41 00 c1 e8 05 c3 ...
 *     scan 0x412cf0..0x412df0 stride 0x20, return (found-0x412cf0)>>5 = 0..7);
 *   - Win9x/UT path (InitializeUtDriverAndHandlerTable @0x40a684) installs
 *     slot 6 = UtNotifyCode0x205 @0x0040a5c8.
 * On the waveOut path the byte genuinely is a 0..7 buffer index, so the parent's
 * "asks a handler slot for a buffer index" is CONFIRMED — but it is specifically the
 * WAVE-HEADER index selector, and THIS caller multiplies it by 0x800 (a PCM buffer)
 * rather than the 0x20 the header-ring twin (0x40a060) uses.
 *
 * THE POOL: 0x412ea8 is the caller-supplied 0x4000 pool that
 * OpenWaveOutAndPrepareHeaderRing @0x409f10 prepared as eight stride-0x800 WAVEHDRs
 * over (re_doc row 177). Eight buffers of 0x800 bytes:
 *     buffer n : 0x412ea8 + n*0x800,  n = 0..7
 *     index 0 = 0x412ea8..0x4130a7    index 7 = 0x4166a8..0x416ea7
 *     POOL RANGE = 0x412ea8 .. 0x416ea7 inclusive (0x4000 bytes).
 * The byte just past the pool, 0x416ea8, is g_dwAudioSlotCount (below) — a tidy fit.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * (b) *** THE SLOT TABLE AND THE STRIDE ***
 *   0x40ac9a  MOV EBX,0x412e28                 ; table base
 *   0x40acda  ADD EBX,0x10                      ; <-- STRIDE = 0x10 = 16 bytes
 *   0x40acdd  MOV ECX,[0x00416ea8]              ; g_dwAudioSlotCount
 *   0x40ace3  SHL ECX,0x4                       ; * 16
 *   0x40ace6  ADD ECX,0x412e28                  ; end = base + count*16
 *   0x40acec  CMP ECX,EBX
 *   0x40acee  JA 0x0040ac9f                     ; loop while end > EBX (do-while)
 * The loop opens on 0x40ac9f CMP dword ptr [EBX],0x0 / 0x40aca2 JZ 0x40acda: offset 0
 * of the slot is the ACTIVE test, and inactive slots (==0) are skipped straight to EBX+=0x10.
 *
 * SLOT LAYOUT (from the bytes this function touches):
 *   +0x0  ACTIVE, a DWORD. CMP [EBX],0. Nonzero = active. Its own writer (the insert
 *         helper FUN_0040ab88) stores the source block pointer here, so it is
 *         "nonzero pointer = active, 0 = free".
 *   +0x4  SOURCE CURSOR, a DWORD. PUSH dword ptr [EBX+0x4] as arg2; advanced by the
 *         mixed byte count afterwards (ADD [EBX+0x4],ESI).
 *   +0x8  REMAINING COUNT, a DWORD in BYTES. MOV ESI,[EBX+0x8]; clamped to 0x800 by
 *         CMP ESI,0x800 / JBE / MOV ESI,0x800 (UNSIGNED min); decremented by it after
 *         the mix (SUB [EBX+0x8],ESI).
 *   +0xc..+0xf  NOT read by this function. FUN_0040ab88 writes byte fields at
 *         +0xc/+0xd/+0xe per slot (from its args), one of which it tests with 0x80;
 *         their meaning is undetermined HERE and deliberately not named.
 * The parent's "offset 0 active, offset 4 source cursor, offset 8 remaining count,
 * clamped to 0x800" is CONFIRMED from the bytes.
 * VERIFIED AGAINST SIBLINGS:
 *   - InitializeAudioSubsystemByOsVersionAndOpenMciDevice @0x40aae0 zeroes a
 *     0x10-stride table at 0x412e28, the FIRST DWORD ONLY of each entry
 *     (MOV dword ptr [EBX],0x0 ; ADD EBX,0x10), over its own do-while — same base,
 *     same 0x10 stride, and it also publishes g_dwAudioSlotCount @0x416ea8.
 *   - FUN_0040ab88 (the inserter, FUN_0040ac80's caller) writes the slot with
 *     SHL EDX,0x4 (stride 0x10) at 0x412e28/+0x4/+0x8 and the +0xc..+0xe bytes.
 *   Both agree exactly with the 0x10 stride and the +0/+4/+8 fields.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * (c) *** THE FIRST SLOT VERSUS THE REST -- THE LAY-DOWN AND THE SUM ***
 *   0x40acb2  PUSH EBP            ; arg: destination
 *   0x40acb3  PUSH [EBX+0x4]      ; arg: source
 *   0x40acb6  PUSH ESI            ; arg: byte count
 *   0x40acb7  TEST EDI,EDI
 *   0x40acb9  JZ 0x0040acc2
 *   0x40acbb  MOV ECX,0x40a88c    ; EDI != 0 -> BlendSaturatedByteBuffers
 *   0x40acc0  JMP 0x0040acc7
 *   0x40acc2  MOV ECX,0x40a860    ; EDI == 0 -> CopyDwordsAndFillTailWithSilence
 *   0x40acc7  CALL ECX
 * EDI is zeroed at entry (XOR EDI,EDI @0x40ac84) and INC EDI runs after each mixed slot,
 * so EDI == 0 EXACTLY for the FIRST ACTIVE slot and EDI != 0 for every subsequent one.
 * CONFIRMED: the first active slot is laid down by CopyDwordsAndFillTailWithSilence
 * (which fills the whole 512-DWORD destination with 0x80808080 silence and then writes
 * that slot's samples over the head), and every later active slot is summed in by
 * BlendSaturatedByteBuffers (out = saturate(src + dst - 0x80)). That two-phase
 * overwrite-then-sum construction is what makes this a MIXER, not a chained copy.
 * THE DISCRIMINATOR IS EDI (the mixed-slot counter), tested by TEST EDI,EDI / JZ.
 *
 * The blend function 0x0040a88c lies immediately after CopyDwordsAndFillTailWithSilence
 * 0x0040a860 (whose body ends 0x0040a88b, next byte 0x55 = the blend's PUSH EBP). The
 * adjacency is MEANINGFUL only as layout locality — the two are the mixer's twin leaves
 * and were emitted back-to-back by the compiler. The mixer selects between them by
 * ADDRESS (MOV ECX,0x40a88c / MOV ECX,0x40a860), not by adjacency, so the physical
 * ordering carries no dispatch semantics.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * (d) *** THE ARGUMENT EACH MIX CALLEE RECEIVES ***
 * Both call sites push the SAME three values, in the SAME push order (dst, src, count):
 *   PUSH EBP          (destination buffer)
 *   PUSH [EBX+0x4]    (source = slot's cursor)
 *   PUSH ESI          (count   = min(slot+0x8, 0x800))
 * Because the stack grows down, the arg at the LOWEST address (arg1) is ESI (count),
 * arg2 is the source, arg3 is EBP (destination). So the call is
 *   f(count, src, dst)
 * which is the REVERSE of the push order — the standard cdecl/stdcall "push right-to-left".
 * Both recovered callees declare exactly (count, src, dst):
 *   CopyDwordsAndFillTailWithSilence(uint32_t dwByteCount, const uint32_t *pdwSrc, uint32_t *pdwDst)
 *   BlendSaturatedByteBuffers(unsigned int dwByteCount, const unsigned int *pdwSrc, unsigned int *pdwDst)
 * So the caller's stack order matches both signatures. OK.
 *
 * THE COUNT IS IN BYTES, NOT DWORDS. ESI is [slot+0x8] clamped to 0x800 — a BYTE count,
 * the same units as the slot's "remaining bytes" field and the pool buffer size (0x800
 * BYTES). Both callees shift it right by two (SHR ECX,2) to derive their DWORD loop
 * counts, which is only correct if the argument is a BYTE count. Passing a DWORD count
 * would indeed be a bug; the bytes show the BYTE count is what is passed. SETTLED: BYTES.
 * (The count is also safely <= 0x800, so CopyDwordsAndFillTailWithSilence's latent
 * "count > 0x200 dwords" overrun — see its own file — is unreachable from here.)
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * (e) THE TAIL COUNTERS AND THE FINAL INDIRECT CALL ***
 *   0x40acf0  TEST EDI,EDI
 *   0x40acf2  MOV dword ptr [0x00416eb0],EDI   ; STORE mixed-slot count
 *   0x40acf8  JZ 0x0040ad00
 *   0x40acfa  CALL dword ptr [0x00411620]
 * EDI is the number of ACTIVE slots mixed this pass. ONLY 0x416eb0 is WRITTEN here.
 * 0x416ea8 is READ (the slot count / loop bound). 0x416eac is NOT referenced by this
 * function at all — REFUTING the brief's "the writes at 0x416ea8, 0x416eac and 0x416eb0":
 * this body touches exactly two of those three, one read (0x416ea8) and one write
 * (0x416eb0). Static image values of all three (read_memory): 0x416ea8 = 0,
 * 0x416eac = 0, 0x416eb0 = 0 (all zero; runtime-populated).
 *   - 0x416ea8 g_dwAudioSlotCount      : slot-table entry count (READ here).
 *   - 0x416eac (zeroed by 0x40aae0)    : the slot-allocation cursor owned by the
 *                                        inserter FUN_0040ab88 (MOV EBX,[0x416eac] ...);
 *                                        NOT touched by this mixer.
 *   - 0x416eb0 g_dwAudioSlotsMixed     : slots mixed by the LAST pass (WRITTEN here);
 *                                        FUN_0040ab88 reads it at 0x40ac02.
 *
 * THE FINAL CALL resolves exactly like the first: 0x411620 is INDEX 4 of the 0x411610
 * table (0x411620 == base of the 12-slot UT sub-table, so this is UT slot 0). Static
 * value = 0x0040a520 = ReturnConstantOne (image default). Runtime-installed:
 *   - waveOut path (0x40a7bc): slot 0 = UtNotifyUnprepareCurrentWaveHeader @0x0040a060,
 *     raw bytes 6a 20 e8 c9 ff ff ff 0f b6 c0 c1 e0 05 05 e0 2c 41 00 50 ff 35 d8 2c
 *     41 00 ff 15 20 1c 40 00 f7 d8 19 c0 40 c3. It PUSHes 0x20, CALLs SelectWaveHeaderIndex
 *     (0x40a030), scales the index by 0x20, adds the header-ring base 0x412ce0, then calls
 *     the waveOut entry at [0x401c20] with (pHeader, 0x412cd8) and boolifies the result.
 *     So the waveOut-path target UNPREPARES (recycles) the current waveOut header — a
 *     release step, NOT a write/queue. The parent's "waveOut header write/queue step" is
 *     IMPRECISE: the handler releases/frees the buffer rather than filling it (the fill
 *     happens here, in this function). Its exact winmm entry point at [0x401c20] is not
 *     resolved against the import table.
 *   - Win9x/UT path (0x40a684): slot 0 = UtNotifyCode0x202 @0x0040a598 (a bare
 *     "PUSH 0; PUSH 0x202; PUSH 0; CALL [0x412e10]; RET" UT notification).
 * The call is CONDITIONAL: JZ 0x0040ad00 skips it when EDI == 0 (no active slot).
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * (f) TRUE SIZE -- see the top block. 133 bytes (0x85), both derivations agree; the
 * selector's 136 is 133 + 3 INT3 pad bytes (0x40ad05..0x40ad07).
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * (g) CALLERS AND CONTEXT
 * get_function_callers = 2: FUN_0040ab88 (0x40ab88) and FUN_0040b958 (0x40b958).
 *   - FUN_0040ab88 (RET 0x10, 4 args) is the SLOT INSERTER. It scans the table from
 *     0x416eac for a free slot (stride 0x10), fills +0/+4/+8 and the +0xc..+0xe bytes,
 *     then branches on flags: a source whose byte at +0x8 has bit 0x80 set selects
 *     EBX=2 and falls through TWO back-to-back calls (0x40ac20 then 0x40ac25) — two mix
 *     passes; otherwise it may select EBX=1 (one mix) or EBX=0 (no mix). Either way the
 *     mix is kicked IMMEDIATELY when a source is added. Its own only caller is
 *     FUN_00406d8c, a stream-container record handler (a parser loop), so this trigger
 *     is STREAM/INSERT-driven, not a timer.
 *   - FUN_0040b958 is the GMW_PLAYER window procedure (WNDCLASSA.lpfnWndProc; 0 live
 *     callers because Windows calls it). Its message switch maps 0xf/0x100/0x101-less
 *     set/0x102/0x200/0x201/0x202/0x204/0x205/0x20/0x24/0x5/0x2/0x10/0x311/0x30f/0x3bd,
 *     and CASE 0x3bd (0x40ba0d CMP EAX,0x3bd ; JZ 0x40bc76) does
 *     `CALL 0x40ac80 ; XOR EAX,EAX ; RET 0x10` — a WINDOW MESSAGE drives this mix pass.
 *     0x3bd = 957 is a CUSTOM (non-system) message. WHAT POSTS 0x3bd is NOT established
 *     by either caller's bytes: neither body contains a PostMessage/SendMessage of 0x3bd,
 *     and no recovered file references the constant. So: the trigger is a WINDOW MESSAGE
 *     (settled), while whether its poster is a timer, a waveOut notification, or another
 *     thread is UNDETERMINED from these two functions alone. The waveOut device itself was
 *     opened CALLBACK_EVENT (no window callback), so the message is posted to the window
 *     from elsewhere — I will not name the source without bytes.
 * Net, plainly: a mix pass runs (i) when the stream inserts a source slot, and (ii) on
 * the GMW_PLAYER window message 0x3bd. No SetTimer and no audio thread appear in either
 * caller's body.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * (h) NAME
 * MixActiveAudioSlotsIntoWaveOutBuffer -- states the waveOut software mix of the audio
 * slot table into one pool buffer. Kept.
````

````text
 * 0x0040af44 - 0x0040af6a (body_end 0x0040af6b), selector size 40 bytes.

 * Stack trace (entry ESP = S):
 *   0x0040af44  PUSH EAX              ; [S+0] = saved EAX   -> argc bookkeeping
 *   0x0040af45  CMP dword ptr [0x004170b8], 0x0
 *   0x0040af4c  JZ 0x0040af66        ; global not armed -> dead body
 *   0x0040af4e  PUSH dword ptr [ESP+0xc]   ; [S+8] = arg2  -> pushed first
 *   0x0040af52  PUSH dword ptr [ESP+0xc]   ; [S+4] = arg1  -> pushed second
 *   0x0040af56  LEA EAX, [ESP+0x8]         ; EAX = S = &saved EAX (caller local)
 *   0x0040af5a  PUSH EAX
 *   0x0040af5b  CALL DispatchMciCommandViaGlobalHandleAndShowError (0x0040af10)
 *   0x0040af60  ADD ESP, 0x4          ; drop the pointer we pushed
 *   0x0040af63  RET 0x8               ; pop 2 args -> two-argument function
 *   0x0040af66  ADD ESP, 0x4          ; not-taken path: drop saved EAX only
 *   0x0040af69  RET 0x8

 *   param_1 = &saved-EAX (0x0040af56 LEA EAX,[ESP+0x8] / 0x0040af5a PUSH EAX)
 *   param_2 = our arg1 (0x0040af52 push [ESP+0xc] == [S+4])
 *   param_3 = our arg2 (0x0040af4e push [ESP+0xc] == [S+8], pushed first)
 *   so the callee's mciSendCommandA receives (handle, arg2, arg1, &saved_eax):
 *   arg2 is the MCI message and arg1 the flags/dwParam1.
 *

 * flag. If it is 0 the entire body is a no-op: we just drop the pushed EAX
 * and return. Only when it is non-zero do we forward the command to winmm
 * mciSendCommand through DispatchMciCommandViaGlobalHandleAndShowError and
 * let it display any MCI error.
````

````text
// 0x00417404 into a dword local at [ESP+0], then issue an MCI_PLAY / MCI_NOTIFY through
// the global-handle dispatcher and discard nothing — EAX is untouched between the CALL
// and the RET, so the dispatcher's 1/0 result is returned as-is.

//   0x40af6c SUB  ESP,0xc      -> ESP = S-12   (12-byte frame)
````

````text
// TearDownWaveOutAndMidiAudioSubsystem @ 0x0040a7b0 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Full audio teardown: closes the waveOut device first, then shuts down the MIDI/timer audio subsystem.
// Status: done
/*
 * Pure sequencing wrapper — 3 instructions, 11 bytes, no parameters, no locals, no stack frame.
 *
 *   0x0040a7b0  E8 2B F7 FF FF   CALL 0x00409ee0   ; 5-byte rel32, next_ip 0x40a7b5 + 0xFFFFF72B = 0x409ee0
 *   0x0040a7b5  E8 7A FB FF FF   CALL 0x0040a334   ; 5-byte rel32, next_ip 0x40a7ba + 0xFFFFFB7A = 0x40a334
 *   0x0040a7ba  C3               RET               ; plain RET — pops only the return address
 *
 * Raw bytes at 0x0040a7b0 (read_memory, 16 bytes):
 *   e8 2b f7 ff ff  e8 7a fb ff ff  c3  cc ff ...
 *                ^byte 0x0040a7bb = 0xCC (INT3 alignment padding, belongs to NO function)
 *
 * TRUE SIZE = 11 bytes. Both derivations agree exactly:
 *   - body_end formula: body_end 0x0040a7ba - body_start 0x0040a7b0 + 1 = 0x0b = 11
 *   - real last instruction: the C3 (RET) at 0x0040a7ba is 1 byte, so the last byte really is 0x0040a7ba
 * The selector's "12 bytes" is the 11 real bytes PLUS the trailing 0xCC pad at 0x0040a7bb. There is
 * NO undefined near-clone here: 0x0040a7bb resolves to "No function found", and the next defined
 * entry is FUN_0040a7bc (body 0x0040a7bc..0x0040a85e) — two bytes past our last byte.
 *
 * It is a forwarder in the sequencing sense only, and the argument question is moot: both CALLs
 * push NOTHING. There is no PUSH in the body, so there is no argument order to get backwards and
 * no argument is forwarded, dropped, or reordered — this is not a signature-adapting thunk. The
 * plain RET (not RET imm16) confirms it takes no stack arguments of its own; it inherits whatever
 * the caller pushed purely as a pass-through frame that it never touches or pops.
 *
 * Return value: DISCARDED. Both callees are void (the second ends in a plain RET after a guarded
 * midiOutClose whose EAX is likewise dropped), and this wrapper's RET does not forward EAX to
 * anything — it exists only to enforce an ORDER, not to produce a value.
 *
 * The order is the entire semantic content, and it is inner-device-first:
 *   1. UnprepareAndCloseWaveOut()  @0x00409ee0 — unprepares all 8 WAVEHDRs in the ring at
 *      0x412ce0..0x412dfd (stride 0x20, WHDR_UNPREPARED 0x20 forced), then waveOutClose on the
 *      handle at 0x412cd8. Unconditional do/while; no return value tested.
 *   2. ShutdownAudioSubsystem()    @0x0040a334 — calls ResetMidiOutAndTimerEvent() @0x0040a144
 *      (kills the timeSetEvent at 0x412de8 + midiOutReset), then timeEndPeriod on 0x412e08 if
 *      nonzero, then midiOutClose on 0x412de0 if nonzero; both globals cleared to 0 so it is
 *      idempotent.
 *
 * No global is read or written by THIS function. The globals listed above are owned and touched
 * by its callees; this wrapper only sequences them. Because each callee is internally guarded and
 * zeroes its own handles, calling this wrapper twice is safe: the second pass closes nothing that
 * was already closed. It is also safe to call when audio was never opened.
 */
````

````text
// UpdateMciAudioStateAndPlay @ 0x004090d0 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Gate-ordered MCI audio entry point: when the audio subsystem is idle it resets the transport, then (if the playback gate is set) stores the mode byte, configures and plays; every other path returns 1.
// Status: done

 * ROLE — the caller-facing sequencer between the two already-recovered MCI audio leaves.
 * DispatchMciAudioReset @0x4090c0 sits immediately below (16 bytes) and
 * DispatchMciSetFlagsAndPlay @0x40a958 is the configure-then-play leaf; this function is
 * the only thing that orders them, so the two global gates below decide the whole path.
 *
 * Control flow (14 instructions, 0x4090d0..0x409104), decompile and disassembly agree exactly:
 *
 *   CMP BYTE [0x4177f8],0          ; gate A: audio subsystem busy/idle flag
 *   JNZ 0x4090ff                  ; A != 0 -> return 1, nothing else runs
 *   CALL 0x4090c0                 ; DispatchMciAudioReset(): MCI play cmd #0 + [0x417345]=0xff
 *   CMP BYTE [0x417344],0          ; gate B: playback-enabled flag
 *   JZ  0x4090ff                  ; B == 0 -> return 1
 *   MOV AL,[ESP+0x4]              ; AL = the caller's byte argument
 *   MOV [0x417345],AL              ; publish it into the VM audio-state byte
 *   MOVSX EAX,AL / PUSH EAX        ; sign-extended to 32 bits -> the leaf's byte stack slot
 *   CALL 0x40a958                 ; DispatchMciSetFlagsAndPlay(bFlag)
 *   MOVSX EAX,AL                  ; re-read the returned AL, sign-extend
 *   RET 0x4                       ; the callee popped nothing: our own argument is still live
 *
 * Two gates, both must pass for the play path: the RESET/START call happens unconditionally
 * inside the A==0 branch, while the store + configure + PLAY sequence requires B != 0 as well.
 * A!=0 skips the reset entirely — the busy case is the "someone else owns the transport" early out.
 *

 * (that leaf returns 1/0 for PLAY success/failure, or a raw MCI error code when its SET call
 * fails), and the constant 1 from 0x4090ff on both early-out paths. Note the byte-then-MOVSX
 * round trip: only AL survives, so an MCI error code is truncated to its low byte here even
 * though the callee itself propagates the full 32-bit code.
 *
 * The sign-extended argument is not cosmetic: DispatchMciSetFlagsAndPlay re-reads only its
 * one-byte stack slot and hands it to MCI_PLAY, so bMciAudioMode is genuinely a single byte.
 */
````

````text
// Issues the MCI_CLOSE command to the open CD-audio device and then unconditionally zeroes both audio globals: the WinMM device id @0x412e20 and the audio-enabled flag @0x412e24.
// Status: done
/*
 * ROLE — the MCI tear-down leaf, the exact counterpart of the round-54 sibling
 * OpenMciCdAudioDeviceAndArmEnabledFlag @0x40a90c. Where that function OPENS the "cdaudio"
````
