````text
 * both globals on every path.
 *
 * Body 0x40aab4..0x40aadd, 8 instructions, plain 1-byte RET (0x40aadd = 0xC3) so it takes NO
 * stack arguments and the callee (mciSendCommandA, WINAPI == __stdcall) pops its own four
 * arguments. Exactly ONE indirect call, through the IAT slot @0x00401bc8.
 *
 *   0x40aab4  6A 00                 PUSH 0x0                        ; arg4 dwParam2 = 0 (no parameter block)
 *   0x40aab6  6A 00                 PUSH 0x0                        ; arg3 dwParam1 = 0 (no flags)
 *   0x40aab8  68 04 08 00 00        PUSH 0x804                      ; arg2 uMsg     = MCI_CLOSE
 *   0x40aabd  FF 35 20 2E 41 00     PUSH dword ptr [0x00412e20]     ; arg1 mciId    = g_dwMciTaskId
 *   0x40aac3  FF 15 C8 1B 40 00     CALL dword ptr [0x00401bc8]     ; mciSendCommandA
 *   0x40aac9  C7 05 20 2E 41 00 00 00 00 00   MOV dword ptr [0x00412e20],0x0  ; g_dwMciTaskId = 0
 *   0x40aad3  C7 05 24 2E 41 00 00 00 00 00   MOV dword ptr [0x00412e24],0x0  ; g_dwMciAudioEnabled = 0
 *   0x40aadd  C3                    RET
 * All 8 instructions are contiguous and fill the full 42-byte body; there is NO branch (no Jcc),
 * and the EAX result of the CALL is never tested or stored before being overwritten/returned.
 *
 * IMPORT — resolved by reading bytes, NOT trusting the bridge name. The IAT slot @0x00401bc8 holds
 * the dword 0x00001854 (bytes `54 18 00 00`) — an IMAGE_IMPORT_BY_NAME RVA. 0x00001854 + image
 * base 0x400000 = 0x00401854; the bytes there are
 *   `00 00 6D 63 69 53 65 6E 64 43 6F 6D 6D 61 6E 64 41 00` = 2-byte hint 0x0000 followed by the
 * NUL-terminated name "mciSendCommandA" (the next import, at 0x401866, is "waveOutPause").
 * So the imported function is genuinely mciSendCommandA (winmm.dll). This is the SAME IAT slot
 * 0x00401bc8 the sibling OpenMciCdAudioDeviceAndArmEnabledFlag calls, and the SAME resolved name —
 * both functions are thin thunks over mciSendCommandA. (get_function_callees reported the callee at
 * "address":"0000005e", exactly as it did for the sibling; that is spurious — the real IAT target
 * RVA is 0x1854, not 0x5e.)
 *
 * PARAMETER ORDER — mciSendCommandA is __stdcall, so arguments are pushed right-to-left and the
 * LAST push is the FIRST parameter. The four pushes therefore map:
 *   push #4 (0x0)            -> dwParam2 (4th param) = 0
 *   push #3 (0x0)            -> dwParam1 (3rd param) = 0
 *   push #2 (0x804)          -> uMsg     (2nd param) = MCI_CLOSE
 *   push #1 ([0x412e20])     -> mciId    (1st param) = g_dwMciTaskId
 * API shape (mciapi.h): `MCIERROR WINAPI mciSendCommandA(MCIDEVICEID mciId, UINT uMsg,
 * DWORD_PTR dwParam1, DWORD_PTR dwParam2)` — FOUR arguments.
 *
 * MESSAGE CONSTANT — 0x804 == 2048 decimal == MCI_CLOSE. Verified against the installed headers:
 * mciapi.h:145 `#define MCI_CLOSE 0x0804` (vfw.h:1400 has the same value). The parent's belief that
 * 0x804 is MCI_CLOSE is CONFIRMED. The sibling uses 0x803 == MCI_OPEN (mciapi.h:144), so the pair is
 * literally MCI_OPEN / MCI_CLOSE: 0x803 + 1.
 *
 * THE TWO ZERO PARAMETERS — of the four arguments, dwParam1 (arg3, pushed as 0x0) is the FLAGS word;
 * its value of 0 means "no flags" (no MCI_NOTIFY, no MCI_WAIT). dwParam2 (arg4, pushed as 0x0) is the
 * parameter block pointer; 0 means "no parameter block", which is exactly what MCI_CLOSE documents
 * (it accepts neither flags nor a parameter block). So the two zeros are the documented no-flags /
 * null-parameter-block arguments for a close.
 *
 * UNCONDITIONAL CLEAR — the parent's main question. After the CALL, the two dwords are written with
 * the literal 0 (two C7 05 imm32 stores) with NO conditional between them and NO test of EAX, so both
 * @0x412e20 and @0x412e24 become 0 on EVERY path through the function; the CALL's EAX return value
 * (the MCIERROR) is discarded. Given the sibling file, @0x412e20 is the MCI device id
 * (g_dwMciTaskId) and @0x412e24 is the audio-enabled flag (g_dwMciAudioEnabled), so this function
 * invalidates BOTH: it drops its handle on the device and marks the transport as disarmed.
 * Whether clearing the id/flag WITHOUT testing the close result is a latent defect or an intentional
 * contract CANNOT be settled from these bytes (the bytes only show that the error is discarded). The
 * observable consequence — labelled INFERENCE, not byte fact — is that a failing close is silent and
 * the device id is lost, so a later close is impossible from this state; that is the shape a "close is
 * best-effort, the globals are the authoritative open/closed state" contract would also have. The
 * bytes do not decide between the two.
 *
 * DOUBLE-CALL SAFETY — the CALL is issued UNCONDITIONALLY: it is NOT guarded by a check that
 * g_dwMciTaskId is nonzero, so if the device id is already 0 the function still calls
 * mciSendCommandA(0, MCI_CLOSE, 0, 0). A device id of 0 is not a valid open MCI device, so per the
 * Win32 MCI contract such a call returns an error (invalid device id) and has no side effect — but
 * that contract is API behaviour, not something these bytes show. What the bytes DO show: the sequence
 * is idempotent with respect to the globals (they are already 0 and get written 0 again) and the
 * return value is ignored, so calling this a second time cannot corrupt the two globals; it can only
 * issue one spurious, ignored failing call.
 *
 * CALLER — get_function_callers returns exactly ONE: FUN_0040ad18 (body 0x40ad18..0x40ad73). Its very
 * FIRST instruction is `CALL 0x0040aab4`, i.e. the close is UNCONDITIONAL at the top of that function
 * (not behind any branch); after it FUN_0040ad18 executes `CALL dword ptr [0x41164c]` and then resets
 * a table of handler-function pointers at 0x411620..0x41164c to the default stubs 0x40a520/0x40a524/
 * 0x40a52c/0x40a51c (each is a one-or-two-instruction "MOV AL,1; RET" always-succeed stub). So
 * FUN_0040ad18 is a tear-down/RESET routine: close the MCI device, then restore the audio/UT dispatch
 * table to benign defaults. FUN_0040ad18 is itself called unconditionally by FUN_00408f78 (which first
 * stops playback via CALL 0x40a9c0) and by FUN_00404800 (an options/re-init routine that sets several
 * enable flags and copies config, then calls FUN_0040ad18). The close is thus reached from a stop/reset
 * path, not from a per-frame code path. Whether the author intended "shutdown" vs "reset before
 * re-open" cannot be settled from these bytes. FUN_0040ad18 does NOT call the sibling's open
 * (0x40a90c) — the OPEN (0x40a90c) is reached through a different function, FUN_0040aae0, called in
 * turn by FUN_00404590 and FUN_00408f8c. So the immediate caller of this close does not itself pair
 * open+close; the pairing is at the level of the two FUN_0040aae0 / FUN_0040ad18 subsystems.
 *
 * SIBLING PAIRING — side by side (both over the same two globals @0x412e20 / @0x412e24):
 *   open  OpenMciCdAudioDeviceAndArmEnabledFlag @0x40a90c : uMsg = 0x803 MCI_OPEN,
 *         dwParam1 = 0x2100 = MCI_OPEN_TYPE|MCI_OPEN_SHAREABLE, dwParam2 = &MCI_OPEN_PARMSA;
 *         writes the globals only on SUCCESS (JNZ over the two stores).
 *   close CloseMciCdAudioDeviceAndClearEnabledFlag @0x40aab4 : uMsg = 0x804 MCI_CLOSE,
 *         dwParam1 = 0, dwParam2 = 0; clears the globals ALWAYS.
 * They are an OPEN/CLOSE pair over the same state. The asymmetry (open sets only on success; close
 * clears always) cannot by itself leave a STALE NONZERO device id: every write in both functions is
 * either a full clear (this function) or a success-only arm (the sibling), and the sibling ZEROES both
 * globals at the top of every call before it tries to open, so no ordering reaches the close with a
 * nonzero id that corresponds to a device the globals claim is open but the OS has closed. The one
 * thing the asymmetry CAN leave is a nonzero id that the OS no longer honours if an external close
 * happened without going through this function — that is not an ordering these two functions create.
 *
 * ARGUMENT / CONVENTION — the function takes NO arguments (plain RET; nothing reads the caller's
 * stack) and returns nothing meaningful: EAX holds the MCIERROR immediately before the RET discards
 * it, and the two MOVs clobber nothing the caller relies on. It is a no-argument leaf whose only exit
 * is the plain RET at 0x40aadd.
 *
 * TRUE SIZE — body 0x40aab4..0x40aadd inclusive = 0x40aadd - 0x40aab4 + 1 = 0x2A = 42 bytes. The last
 * instruction is the 1-byte plain RET (0xC3) at 0x40aadd, which IS the last byte of the function. The
 * two bytes at 0x40aade and 0x40aadf are `CC CC` (INT3) alignment padding (the byte at 0x40aae0 begins
 * the next function, FUN_0040aae0 = PUSH EBX / 0x53). The selector's claimed 44 counts those two
 * padding bytes (0x40aadf - 0x40aab4 + 1 == 44); the function itself is 42 bytes.
 */
````

</details>

````text
// DispatchMciPlaybackCommand @ 0x40a9c0 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// MCI playback dispatcher: gated by the audio-enabled flag @0x412e24 and validated opcode 0-3, sends one winmm mciSendCommandA on task id @0x412e20 (STOP / PAUSE-if-playing / RESUME-if-paused / SET), returning the MCI status.
// Status: done
/*
 * ROLE — One of the small cluster of VM/interpreter support routines in the low-0x40a range.
 * This is NetWalk's runtime audio (MCI) transport dispatcher. A caller picks a 0-based opcode:
 *
 *   op 0  -> STOP      (MCI_STOP     = 0x808), sent unconditionally
 *   op 1  -> PAUSE     (MCI_PAUSE    = 0x809), only if current status-mode is PLAYING
 *   op 2  -> RESUME    (MCI_RESUME   = 0x855), only if current status-mode is PAUSED
 *   op 3  -> SET       (MCI_SET      = 0x80d, item MCI_STATUS_ITEM=0x100)
 *
 * The dispatcher is guarded by two persistent globals: the audio-enabled flag at @0x412e24
 * must be nonzero before anything is sent, and all commands target the winmm task id stored
 * in @0x412e20. The opcode (a DWORD read from [ESP+0x1c] per the disassembly) is validated
 * to 0..3 by `CMP EBX,3; JA exit` then jumped through a computed table at @0x411688 —
 * modeled below as a switch for readability. Only opcodes that match are acted on.
 *
 * Grounding: constants verified against mmsystem.h (ReactOS psdk). MCI_MODE_* = MCI_STRING_OFFSET(512)+N,
 * so PLAYING=0x20e (STRING_OFFSET+14) and PAUSED=0x211 (STRING_OFFSET+17); commands 0x808/0x809/0x855/0x80d
 * are MCI_STOP / MCI_PAUSE / MCI_RESUME / MCI_SET respectively. Sibling @0x40a958 performs the matching
 * STATUS(0x814)/PLAY(0x806) pair, corroborating that these globals hold the live winmm task id + enabled flag.
 */
````

</details>

````text
// DispatchMciSetFlagsAndPlay @ 0x0040a958 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Gated by the audio-enabled flag: sends MCI_SET(0x400) with flag word 10 on the winmm task id, then MCI_PLAY, returning 1 if the PLAY call succeeded.
// Status: done
/*
 * ROLE — STATUS/PLAY sibling of the MCI dispatcher @0x40a9c0 (DispatchMciPlaybackCommand),
 * sitting 0x68 bytes before it. Where the dispatcher generalizes STOP/PAUSE/RESUME/SET behind an
 * opcode, this one is the fixed "configure-then-play" entry point: set the device's flag word,
 * then start transport. It shares the same two globals as the dispatcher — the audio-enabled
 * gate at @0x412e24 (must be nonzero) and the live winmm task id at @0x412e20 that every
 * mciSendCommandA targets.
 *
 * Control flow (25 instructions, 0x40a958..0x40a9ba), fully covered by the disassembly:
 *
 *   CMP DWORD [0x412e24],0  ; JZ 0x40a9b7      audio disabled -> epilogue with EAX untouched
 *   MOV DWORD [ESP+0x4],0xa                   flag word = 10
 *   LEA EAX,[ESP] ; PUSH EAX ; PUSH 0x400 ; PUSH 0x80d ; PUSH [0x412e20] ; CALL mciSendCommandA
 *   TEST EAX,EAX ; JNZ 0x40a9b7                SET failed -> return the MCI error code
 *   XOR EAX,EAX ; MOV AL,BYTE [ESP+0x1c]       zero-extend the one-byte stack argument
 *   MOV DWORD [ESP+0x10],EAX
 *   LEA EAX,[ESP+0xc] ; PUSH EAX ; PUSH 0x4 ; PUSH 0x806 ; PUSH [0x412e20] ; CALL mciSendCommandA
 *   NEG EAX ; SBB EAX,EAX ; INC EAX            standard "EAX==0" idiom -> 1 on success, 0 on failure
 *   ADD ESP,0x18 ; RET 0x4
 *
 * Command constants, cross-checked against the sibling's already-verified set (mmsystem.h,
 * MCI_FIRST = 0x800): 0x80d = MCI_SET and 0x806 = MCI_PLAY (= MCI_FIRST+6, sitting between
 * MCI_GETDEVINFO 0x807 and MCI_STOP 0x808, matching the sibling's verified MCI_STOP = 0x808).
 * The SET item word 0x400 is MCI_SET_VIDEO_ALL (the MCI_SET item block runs 0x100 time-format,
 * 0x200 audio-all, 0x400 video-all), i.e. this writes the MCI/AVI video-flag word — 10 =
 * 0x02|0x08 = AVIIF_HIRES|AVIIF_FRAMERATEAVG, a high-resolution average-framerate play setup.
 * The PLAY dwParam is the immediate 4, which is NOT a standard MCI wait/notify flag
 * (MCI_WAIT = MCI_NOTIFY = 1, MCI_NOWAIT = 0); it is passed through verbatim as a mode word.
 *
 * Buffer skew (kept, not smoothed over): each call pushes the buffer BASE — LEA [ESP] for the
 * SET, LEA [ESP+0xc] for the PLAY — while the value written is four bytes further on
 * ([ESP+0x4] and [ESP+0x10]). Modeled below as index 1 of a 2-DWORD array so the +4 is visible
 * instead of silently lost.
 *
 * Return value: 1 if mciSendCommandA(PLAY) returned 0, 0 if it returned nonzero, the SET error
 * code if the SET call failed. On the audio-disabled path the original jumps to the epilogue
 * without ever writing EAX, so the caller receives its own EAX image back — an undefined result
 * at the ABI level. That is why dwInEaxImage exists below: it is a register-only input, NOT a
 * stack argument (RET 0x4 still pops only the one byte parameter).
 */
````

</details>

````text
// loop) as soon as the next event's due time is still in the future.

//     0x40a29a 53                    PUSH EBX
//     0x40a29b ff 35 e0 2d 41 00     PUSH dword ptr [0x412de0]        ; hMidiOut
//     0x40a2a1 ff 15 d4 1b 40 00     CALL dword ptr [0x401bd4]        ; midiOutShortMsg
//     0x40a2a7 80 7c 24 04 00        CMP byte ptr [ESP+0x4],0x0       ; ---- flag A test ----
//     0x40a2ac 75 f8                 JNZ 0x40a1a6                     ; flag A != 0 -> next event, no pacing
//     0x40a2b2 e8 b9 fe ff ff        CALL 0x40a170                    ; delta-time VLV
//     0x40a2b7 89 c3                 MOV EBX,EAX
//     0x40a2b9 85 c0                 TEST EAX,EAX
//     0x40a2bb 74 e9                 JZ 0x40a1a6                      ; delta == 0 -> next event, no pacing
//     0x40a2c1 89 d8                 MOV EAX,EBX
//     0x40a2c3 8d 04 80              LEA EAX,[EAX+EAX*0x4]            ; *5
//     0x40a2c6 03 c0                 ADD EAX,EAX                      ; *2  => delta * 10
//     0x40a2c8 01 05 ec 2d 41 00     ADD [0x412dec],EAX               ; clock target += delta*10
//     0x40a2ce ff 15 d8 1b 40 00     CALL dword ptr [0x401bd8]        ; timeGetTime
//     0x40a2d4 3b 05 ec 2d 41 00     CMP EAX,[0x412dec]
//     0x40a2da 0f 83 c6 fe ff ff     JNC 0x40a1a6                     ; now >= target -> next event
//     0x40a2e0 e9 2c ff ff ff        JMP 0x40a211                     ; now <  target -> return
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// (a) EVENT FETCH AND RUNNING STATUS  --  the core.
//   Status byte vs data byte is decided by  CMP DL,0x7f / JBE 0x40a1bf  at 0x40a1b2/0x40a1b5:
//     * byte  > 0x7f : it IS a status byte.  0x40a1b7 INC [0x412e00] CONSUMES it (cursor++), and
//       that byte becomes the status for the event (DL falls through to 0x40a1c5).
//     * byte <= 0x7f : it is a DATA byte.  0x40a1bf reloads DL from [0x412e04] -- the previous
//       status -- so the data byte is NOT consumed and is left to be read as the first operand.
//   That is the classic MIDI RUNNING-STATUS rule, implemented exactly by the  CMP DL,0x7f / JBE.
//   The status (whoever won) is COPIED back to 0x412e04 on every path (0x40a1c5 MOV AL,DL /
//   0x40a1c7 MOV [0x412e04],AL), so 0x412e04 is the persisted running-status latch.
//
//   The [ESP+0x4] scratch written at 0x40a1a6 (into the slot the preceding PUSH EAX reserved):
//   it is flag A, the "there are still immediate bytes / repeat without re-pacing" flag.  It is
//   WRITTEN twice -- 0x40a1a6 (=0, every iteration) and 0x40a28f (= data2 & 0x80) -- and READ once,
//   at 0x40a2a7.  The parent called it "a scratch flag": correct in substance, but it is really
//   the SECOND of two scratch bytes; the sibling byte [ESP+0x5] (flag B) is written at 0x40a235
//   and 0x40a269 and read at 0x40a293.  Both bites are carved out of the discarded PUSH EAX slot.
//
// (b) EVENT DISPATCH TABLE  --  comparison chain on the MOVZX-ed status byte (0x40a1cc..0x40a1e4):
//     status   test            branch        action                                             cursor
//     -------  --------------  ------------  -------------------------------------------------  ------------------
//     0xF0     CMP/0x40a1d4    -> 0x40a1e6   sysex : CALL VLV helper / ADD [0x412e00],len        status++ + variable run
//     0xF7     CMP/0x40a1db    -> 0x40a1e6   sysex : identity to the 0xF0 branch                 status++ + variable run
//     0xFF     CMP/0x40a1e2    -> 0x40a1f6   end   : if [0x412df4]==0xffff ResetMidiOut.. & ret   status only (no length)
//                                             else [0x412df8]:=[0x412df4]; cursor:=[0x412dfc]; ret
//     else (=<0x80..0xEF)  0x40a1e4 JMP -> 0x40a21d  channel short message (see (c))           status++ + 1 or 2 data
//   So 0xF0 and 0xF7 (system exclusive) share one branch: the LENGTH is decoded with the round-57
//   helper 0x40a170 and SKIPPED by  ADD dword ptr [0x412e00],EAX  (0x40a1eb) -- a VARIABLE run is
//   consumed.  0xFF is NOT length-prefixed here: it does not call the helper; it drives the loop
//   markers/teardown.  0xFF writes the status byte only.
//   In the short-message path the high nibble selects the operand count (0x40a23a AND EAX,0xf0):
//     0x8n / 0x9n -> evaluate the [0x412e05] gate then read a SECOND data byte (THREE-byte message)
//     0xCn / 0xDn -> JMP 0x40a293 directly, SKIPPING the 0x40a26d data2 read (TWO-byte message)
//     else 0xAn/0xBn/0xEn -> 0x40a26d and read a SECOND data byte (THREE-byte message)
//   So the branches that consume TWO operand bytes are 0x8n/0x9n/0xAn/0xBn/0xEn; 0xCn/0xDn consume
//   ONE; 0xF0/0xF7 consume a VARIABLE run (status byte + a VLV-decoded length field + that many bytes).
//
// (c) THE SHORT MESSAGE AND midiOutShortMsg.
//   IAT slot 0x401bd8 -> DWORD 0x0000189a -> RVA+0x400000 = 0x40189a -> IMAGE_IMPORT_BY_NAME
//   {hint 0x0000, "timeGetTime"}.  Slot 0x401bd4 -> 0x00001888 -> 0x401888 -> {hint 0x0000,
//   "midiOutShortMsg"}.  (Bytes read at 0x401888: 00 00 "midiOutShortMsg" 00 00 00 "timeGetTime".)
//   The bridge labels are CONFIRMED: [0x401bd8] = timeGetTime, [0x401bd4] = midiOutShortMsg.
//   midiOutShortMsg is called at 0x40a2a1 (PUSH EBX / PUSH [0x412de0] / CALL [0x401bd4]).  The
//   DWORD assembled in EBX is  status | (data1 << 8) | ((data2 & 0x7f) << 16)  -- status in bits
//   0..7, data1 in 8..15, data2 in 16..23 -- which IS the STANDARD 3-byte MIDI short-message
//   packing.  data2 is masked to 7 bits (0x40a27c AND EAX,0x7f) but data1 is stored unmasked.
//
// (d) THE PACING AT THE TAIL AND THE TIMER GLOBALS.
//   0x40a2c1..0x40a2c8: EAX = delta; LEA EAX,[EAX+EAX*4] (*5); ADD EAX,EAX (*2) => delta * 10;
//   ADD dword ptr [0x412dec],EAX.  The times-ten scale converts SMF delta ticks into the ms
//   domain -- the classic 1 ms MIDI tempo unit vs the 10 ms tick (LEA *5 then ADD *2 is the
//   compiler's multiply-by-10).  0x412dec is a running absolute "next event due time" in
//   timeGetTime units.
//   *** PARENT PREMISE REFUTED ***  The tail comparison is  CMP EAX,[0x412dec] / JNC 0x40a1a6
//   (0x40a2d4/0x40a2da, bytes 0F 83).  JNC jumps when EAX >= [0x412dec] -- i.e. it loops back to
//   the head when the CURRENT TIME HAS REACHED the target, and when the time is BELOW the target
//   it FALLS THROUGH to JMP 0x40a211 and RETURNS.  This is the exact opposite of a spin: the
//   routine is NOT a busy-wait; it pumps every event whose due time has arrived and returns
//   (yields) as soon as the next event is scheduled in the future -- a frame-budgeted sequencer
//   pump.  There is NO spin-until-ready loop anywhere in this function.
//   Static value of 0x412dec: 0 (the whole 0x412de0..0x412e0f block reads 0x00 in the image --
//   read_memory 0x412de0 len 48 == all zero).  A fresh timeGetTime() is therefore >= 0, so the
//   very first pacing check passes and the first iteration is IMMEDIATE.
//
// (e) TERMINATION AND THE FINAL JMP.
//   The body's last instruction is the 5-byte  JMP E9 2C FF FF FF  at 0x40a2e0, whose target is
//   0x0040a211 -- the shared in-body epilogue (POP EBX / ADD ESP,4 / RET).  0x40a211 < 0x40a2e4,
//   so that target is INSIDE this function, NOT another function: it is a code-sharing back edge
//   to the local exit, NOT a tail call.  (Three separate paths converge on 0x40a211: 0x40a20c
//   fall-through, 0x40a21b after the reset call, and 0x40a2e0.)  Size derivation: 0x40a2e4 is the
//   last byte of the JMP, so 0x40a2e4-0x40a1a4+1 = 321 bytes.  Verified byte-exact from
//   read_memory 0x40a2c0: ... E9 2C FF FF FF CC CC CC (the trailing CCs are the INT3 pad).
//
// (f) RETURN CONTRACT.
//   The function DOES return normally, through the in-body epilogue at 0x40a211.  EAX on exit is
//   not a deliberate result: on the two 0xFF returns it is the END marker / the ResetMidiOut..
//   result, and on the tail return it is the raw timeGetTime() value left by 0x40a2ce.  The value
//   is therefore model-led as void; the only reachable caller (the POCKET) ignores it.
//
// (g) THE CALLERS AND THE POCKET.
//   get_function_callers(0x40a1a4) == 0 (and get_function_callees lists the four resolved callees
//   above).  The edge exists but is invisible to Ghidra because the caller lives in an UNDEFINED
//   routine:
//     POCKET @ 0x40a2e5..0x40a333 == 3x INT3 (0x40a2e5..0x40a2e7) + a 73-byte routine at
//     0x40a2e8..0x40a330 that Ghidra has NO function for (get_function_by_address on 0x40a2e5,
//     0x40a2e8, 0x40a2f0 and 0x40a300 all return "No function found") + 3x INT3
//     (0x40a331..0x40a333); the next DEFINED function is ShutdownAudioSubsystem @ 0x40a334
//     (body 0x40a334..0x40a377).  Total excess over this body = 3+73+3 = 79 bytes, exactly
//     400(=0x190) - 321(=0x141).  CONFIRMED (bytes read at 0x40a2e5).
//   POCKET DECODE (lead -- NOT written to a file), 10 instructions, ends  RET 0x14 (5 stack args):
//     0x40a2e8 83 3d f8 2d 41 00 00   CMP dword ptr [0x412df8],0x0
//     0x40a2ef 75 2b                  JNZ 0x40a31c
//     0x40a2f1 83 3d f0 2d 41 00 00   CMP dword ptr [0x412df0],0x0
//     0x40a2f8 75 1f                  JNZ 0x40a319                 ; guarded: bail if re-entered
//     0x40a2fa ff 15 d8 1b 40 00      CALL [0x401bd8]              ; timeGetTime
//     0x40a300 3b 05 ec 2d 41 00      CMP EAX,[0x412dec]
//     0x40a306 72 11                  JB 0x40a319                  ; not due yet -> return
//     0x40a308 ff 05 f0 2d 41 00      INC dword ptr [0x412df0]     ; re-entrancy guard ++
//     0x40a30e e8 91 fe ff ff         CALL 0x40a1a4                ; *** CALLS THIS FUNCTION ***
//     0x40a313 ff 0d f0 2d 41 00      DEC dword ptr [0x412df0]     ; re-entrancy guard --
//     0x40a319 c2 14 00               RET 0x14
//     0x40a31c ff 0d f8 2d 41 00      DEC dword ptr [0x412df8]
//     0x40a322 75 f5                  JNZ 0x40a319
//     0x40a324 ff 15 d8 1b 40 00      CALL [0x401bd8]              ; timeGetTime
//     0x40a32a a3 ec 2d 41 00         MOV [0x412dec],EAX           ; resync clock to now
//     0x40a32f eb c0                  JMP 0x40a2f1
//   Rel32 sweep of the pocket: the ONLY rel32 CALL is 0x40a30e E8 91 FE FF FF -> 0x0040a1a4,
//   i.e. the pocket calls THIS function directly; the two other calls are indirect through the
//   timeGetTime IAT slot 0x401bd8.  Every branch rel8 resolves inside the pocket (0x40a319 /
//   0x40a31c / 0x40a2f1).  That undefined pocket edge is exactly why 0x40a1a4 reports callers=0.
//   ResetMidiOutAndTimerEvent @ 0x40a144 (its own recovered body) kills the outstanding multimedia
//   timer event @0x412de8 via timeKillEvent and calls midiOutReset on @0x412de0 -- an audio STOP /
````

````text
/*
 * FindWaveHeaderInUseSlotIndex  --  NETWALK.EXE @ 0x0040a030
 *
 * Recovered from the 14-instruction body 0x0040a030..0x0040a05e
 * (true size 47 bytes; last instruction RET at 0x0040a05e).
 *
 * Bytes, verbatim (objdump -d -M intel):
 *   40a030: b9 f0 2c 41 00    mov    ecx,0x412cf0
 *   40a035: f6 01 01          test   BYTE PTR [ecx],0x1
 *   40a038: 74 0b             je     0x40a045
 *   40a03a: 89 c8             mov    eax,ecx
 *   40a03c: 2d f0 2c 41 00    sub    eax,0x412cf0
 *   40a041: c1 e8 05          shr    eax,0x5
 *   40a044: c3                ret
 *   40a045: 83 c1 20          add    ecx,0x20
 *   40a048: 81 f9 f0 2d 41 00 cmp    ecx,0x412df0
 *   40a04e: 72 e5             jb     0x40a035
 *   40a050: ff 35 d8 2c 41 00 push   DWORD PTR ds:0x412cd8
 *   40a056: ff 15 28 1c 40 00 call   DWORD PTR ds:0x401c28
 *   40a05c: 31 c0             xor    eax,eax
 *   40a05e: c3                ret
 *
 * Semantics. 0x412ce0 is an eight-element array of 32-byte WAVEHDR records;
 * the byte the loop tests is that record's dwFlags at offset +0x10 (WHDR_INUSE
 * = 1). ECX walks the flags fields from 0x412cf0 up to (not including)
 * 0x412df0, i.e. 0x100 / 0x20 == 8 records, and (ptr - 0x412cf0) >> 5 turns
 * the flags address back into a 0-based record index.
 *
 * BRANCH SENSE, as observed (do not infer it from the callee): the JE takes
 * the ADVANCE path when the tested bit is ZERO, so the function returns the
 * index of the FIRST record whose dwFlags bit0 is SET. Only when every one of
 * the eight records has bit0 clear does it fall out of the loop, call
 * waveOutReset() through the IAT slot at 0x00401c28 (a real import: .idata
 * spans 0x00401000-0x00401e00), and return 0.
 *
 * 0x412cd8 holds the single HWAVEOUT global and is read as a plain DWORD, so
 * it is program data, not an IAT slot. 0x412cf0/0x412df0 likewise are the
 * program's own table, not imports.
 *
 * No direct CALL targets. One MEMORY-INDIRECT call (0x401c28, waveOutReset).
 * This body contains no register-indirect call: every line of the listing was
 * read and the only CALL opcode present is the FF 15 form at 0x40a056.
 *
 * Arity: bare RET, no frame, and it reads no incoming slot. Its only caller
 * (0x0040a060) pushes 0x20 for the later waveOutWrite stdcall, not for this.
 */
````

````text
// InitializeAudioSubsystemByOsVersionAndOpenMciDevice @ 0x0040aae0 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Start-up audio/UT bring-up: reads GetVersion(), selects the Win32s UT-loader (0x40a684) or the waveOut/MIDI audio loader (0x40a7bc), passes the copied window handle BY ADDRESS to the chosen initialiser, and on success samples handler-table slots 4 and 5 into two caller OUT bytes, publishes ARG4's low byte as the slot count and pre-zeroes the first DWORD of every 16-byte slot entry, then UNCONDITIONALLY opens the MCI CD-audio device; always returns TRUE (1).
// Status: done
/*
 * Body 0x0040aae0..0x0040ab75, 41 instructions, __stdcall, RET 0x10 = FOUR stack
 * arguments. No stack frame (only PUSH EBX), no locals.
 *
 * TRUE SIZE = 150 bytes, both ways:
 *   - body formula: body_end 0x0040ab75 - body_start 0x0040aae0 + 1 = 0x96 = 150.
 *   - last instruction: RET 0x10 == C2 10 00 (3 bytes) at 0x0040ab73, so it ends
 *     exactly at 0x0040ab75. Raw read_memory @0x0040ab70 (8 B) =
 *     b0 01 5b c2 10 00 cc cc  ->  MOV AL,1 ; POP EBX ; RET 0x10 ; CC CC.
 *   The SELECTOR's 152 (= 0x98) is next-function-start minus body_start:
 *   next function begins at 0x0040ab78 (PUSH [ESP+0xc] ; CALL [0x00411624] ;
 *   RET 0xc), and 0x0040ab78 - 0x0040aae0 = 0x98 = 152. The two extra bytes are
 *   the INT3 pair at 0x0040ab76-0x0040ab77 (padding, not code); the function is 150.
 *
 * === (a) ARGUMENT MAP -- DERIVED FROM BOTH CALL SITES, not from the brief ===
 * There are TWO live callers (bridge get_function_callers total=2; brief said 3).
 * Both push exactly the same FOUR dwords, in the same order:
 *   FUN_00404590 @0x004045d7:  PUSH [0x41735c] ; PUSH 0x0 ; PUSH 0x417806 ; PUSH 0x417807 ; CALL 0x40aae0
 *   FUN_00408f8c @0x00408f8c:  PUSH [0x41735c] ; PUSH 0x0 ; PUSH 0x417806 ; PUSH 0x417807 ; CALL 0x40aae0
 * The last push is the LEFT-most argument (stdcall). So at entry:
 *   [ESP+0x4]  = 0x417807        ARG1
 *   [ESP+0x8]  = 0x417806        ARG2
 *   [ESP+0xc]  = 0x00000000      ARG3   (a literal zero pushed by the caller)
 *   [ESP+0x10] = *[0x41735c]     ARG4   (the VALUE of the global, first pushed; a DWORD)
 *
 * The function's own frame is ONE push (EBX), then PUSH 0x412ea8 which is the
 * SINGLE argument to the chosen initialiser. CONFIRMED CONSUMED: both initialisers
 * end in RET 0x4 (0x40a684 -> RET 0x4 at 0x0040a7a2 and 0x0040a7ac; 0x40a7bc ->
 * RET 0x4 at 0x0040a852 and 0x0040a85c), so CALL EAX pops the pushed 0x412ea8.
 * Stack state, ESP = after PUSH EBX and the (consumed) PUSH 0x412ea8:
 *   [ESP+0x0]  saved EBX
 *   [ESP+0x4]  return address
 *   [ESP+0x8]  ARG1  (0x417807)
 *   [ESP+0xc]  ARG2  (0x417806)
 *   [ESP+0x10] ARG3  (0x0)
 *   [ESP+0x14] ARG4  (count source)

 *   0x0040ab1d MOV ECX,[ESP+0xc] = ARG2 -> byte store of slot-4 handler's AL
 *   0x0040ab29 MOV ECX,[ESP+0x8] = ARG1 -> byte store of slot-5 handler's AL

 * 4-byte slot; RET 0x10 still implies FOUR arguments because the caller pushed

 * NOTE the cross-over: ARG1 receives the SLOT-5 (0x00411634) result and ARG2 the
 * SLOT-4 (0x00411630) result -- the bytes are written in the opposite order to the

 * 0x0040ab17 CALL dword ptr [0x00411630] and 0x0040ab23 CALL dword ptr [0x00411634]:
 * each takes NO arguments and returns its value in AL, which is stored through the two

 * before any install holds 0x0040a520 in slots 0,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 and 0x0040a524 in 9,10,

 *   0x00411630 -> offset 0x10 -> handler INDEX 4   (installed to 0x40a5b8 by 0x40a684,
 *                                                    to 0x40a0c4 by 0x40a7bc)
 *   0x00411634 -> offset 0x14 -> handler INDEX 5   (installed to 0x40a658 by 0x40a684,

 * === (e) THE COUNT AND THE ZEROING LOOP ===
 * 0x0040ab31 MOV AL,[ESP+0x14] (ARG4 low byte) ; 0x0040ab35 MOV [0x00416ea8],EAX -- the
 * byte is ZERO-EXTENDED (XOR EAX,EAX precedes it) and stored as the DWORD slot count
 * g_dwSlotCount @0x00416ea8 (the same global c/ClearAllSlotEntries.c consumes).
 * 0x0040ab3c MOV [0x00416eb0],EBX(0) ; 0x0040ab42 MOV [0x00416eac],EBX(0): two more
 * DWORD globals zeroed. Then the loop:
 *   EBX=0 ; SHL EBX,4 ; ADD EBX,0x412e28  (the ROTATED entry, run ONCE)
 *   head 0x0040ab51: [EBX]=0 ; EBX+=0x10 ; EAX=[0x416ea8]; SHL EAX,4; ADD EAX,0x412e28
 *                    ; CMP EAX,EBX ; JA head
 * The JA target is 0x0040ab51 (the head), NOT the SHL at 0x0040ab48, so the SHL/ADD run
 * exactly once -- the FIRST iteration addresses 0x412e28 (0 << 4 + 0x412e28), CONFIRMED.
 * It is a DO-WHILE: with EBX=0 the sole dword [0x412e28] is zeroed even when ARG4==0,
 * because the head is reached before any count test. Only the FIRST DWORD of each
 * 16-byte entry is zeroed (MOV dword ptr [EBX],0x0), NOT the whole 16 bytes. Entries
 * zeroed: indices 0..count-1 (the loop exits when base+count*16 <= cur).
 *
 * === (f) THE UNCONDITIONAL TAIL ===
 * 0x0040ab6b (CALL 0x0040a90c, the MCI open) is reached BOTH by the success path falling
 * out of the loop (0x0040ab69 JA not taken) AND by the JZ at 0x0040ab15 when the
 * initialiser returned FALSE. It is therefore UNCONDITIONAL. 0x0040ab70 MOV AL,0x1 ;
 * RET 0x10 -> the function ALWAYS returns 1 (TRUE). So the return value does NOT report
 * whether audio came up. This is not a lost result in the bytes: 0x0040a90c's own
 * recovered file documents that it gates itself -- it arms g_dwMciAudioEnabled @0x412e24
 * only on MCI success, and that flag is what the transport leaves test. The contract is
 * "report that bring-up was attempted"; audio health lives in the MCI globals, not in AL.
 *
 * === NAMING NOTE ===
 * The two initialisers are addressed INDIRECTLY (MOV EAX,0x40a684 / MOV EAX,0x40a7bc ;
 * CALL EAX), so the bridge's direct-callee list legitimately shows both.
 */
````

````text
// InitializeMidiOutAndTimerResolution @ 0x0040a378 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NETWALK)
// Opens the default MIDI output device and raises the system timer resolution
// to the coarsest period the timer driver permits, returning TRUE on success and
// tearing the whole subsystem down again on any failure.
// Status: done
//
// Machine-code facts the decompilation gets wrong or hides (checked against
// /disassemble_function, which agrees instruction-for-instruction):
//
//  1. BODY SIZE: body_start 0x0040a378 .. body_end 0x0040a411 = 154 bytes /
//     50 instructions. Any figure larger than that for this entry is wrong.
//  2. The period clamp is REGISTER-ONLY. Ghidra prints
//     `local_8.wPeriodMax = local_8.wPeriodMin` inside the branch at 0x0040a3ed,
//     implying the TIMECAPS struct is overwritten. It is not: between 0x0040a3d9
//     and 0x0040a3f1 there is no store to [ESP] or [ESP+4] — only `MOV EAX,reg`
//     shuffling. The struct keeps the driver's own wPeriodMin/wPeriodMax and the
//     chosen value lives in EAX until it is stored to 0x412e08.
//  3. The clamp reads as: EAX = max(wPeriodMin, 10); then
//     EAX = (EAX >= wPeriodMax) ? wPeriodMax : EAX.
//     i.e. period = min( max(wPeriodMin, 10), wPeriodMax )  -- never finer than
//     10 ms, and never coarser than the device maximum.
//  4. [r45 PARENT CORRECTION] The "NO parameters, the 8 stack bytes are the
//     caller's TIMECAPS" claim is REFUTED. 0x0040a7bc does PUSH EAX immediately
//     before CALL 0x0040a378 (0x40a7c8 PUSH EAX / 0x40a7c9 CALL), so one argument is
//     genuinely passed. It takes exactly ONE argument: the BOOL result of
//     OpenWaveOutAndPrepareHeaderRing. [passB correction] The callee's
//     `ADD ESP,0x8` does NOT consume that argument: the body opens with
//     `SUB ESP,0x8` (0x40a378) for its own TIMECAPS locals at [ESP]/[ESP+4],
//     and the epilogue removes exactly those 8 bytes. The argument is
//     cdecl-style and is popped by the CALLER (`pop eax` at 0x40a7d3).
//     Note the callee ALSO reads [ESP] and [ESP+4]
//     as locals of its own frame, which is what made this look parameterless.
//     The clamp conclusion (coarsest-period clamp -> 0x412e08 -> timeBeginPeriod)
//     is unaffected. Update the extern declaration to match: it takes one arg.
//  5. It writes NONE of the 12 UT handler slots 0x411620..0x41164c -- verified over the
//     full body. Those are written by 0x0040a7bc (InitializeAudioSubsystemAndUtHandlerTable).
//  5b. midiOutOpen is called with uDeviceID = -1 (0xffffffff pushed at
//     0x0040a381), i.e. MIDI_MAPPER, and dwFlags/callback/instance = 0.
//  6. FAILURE SHAPE (corrected): 0x40a390 (`test eax,eax / JNE 0x40a40c`) is
//     the ONLY branch to the plain-FALSE tail (0x40a40c: `XOR EAX,EAX /
//     ADD ESP,0x8 / RET` -- no teardown; nothing was opened yet, so the
//     midiOutOpen failure exits directly). The three later failures --
````

````text
// InitializeUtDriverAndHandlerTable @ 0x0040a684 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NETWALK)
// Loads KERNEL32's undocumented Win9x UT interface, resolves UTRegister/UTUnRegister, registers "GMW.DLL" to obtain the UT dispatch hook at 0x412e10, sends the 0x200 notification, allocates the 0xF000 client message buffer at 0x412e0c and overwrites all 12 UT notification callback slots at 0x411620-0x41164c; returns TRUE, and on hook-notify or GlobalAlloc failure unwinds through ShutdownUtDriverAndFreeResources and returns FALSE.
// Status: done
//
// Machine-code facts the decompiler gets wrong or hides (checked against the
// raw bytes with objdump, not just the decompile):
//
//  1. Return value is BOOL. 0x0040a7a0 is `MOV AL,0x1; RET 0x4`, so success
//     returns TRUE. The decompiled `return &LAB_0040a501` is the residue of
//     `MOV EAX,0x40a668` (the last table entry) with only AL then overwritten.
//  2. This is __stdcall with ONE stack argument (`RET 0x4` on both exits),
//     which Ghidra models as `(void)`. The argument is not dead: it is
//     forwarded as the hook's first parameter by `PUSH [ESP+0xc]` at
//     0x0040a700. The decompiler prints the literal "GMW.DLL" there because it
//     under-counts UTRegister's stack cleanup by one slot; 0x411650 sits at
//     [ESP+0x8] of that push sequence, not [ESP+0xc]. Every exit here is
//     stack-balanced only if UTRegister pops 7 args (28) and the hook pops 3
//     (12), which is what fixes [ESP+0xc] to the caller's context pointer.
//  3. ShutdownUtDriverAndFreeResources is reached only from 0x0040a7a5, which
//     is the failure tail of the hook-0x200 call and of GlobalAlloc. Every
//     earlier failure (LoadLibrary, either GetProcAddress, UTRegister itself)
//     jumps straight to the `XOR EAX,EAX; RET 4` at 0x0040a7aa with no
//     teardown, because nothing has been registered yet.
````

````text
// OpenMciCdAudioDeviceAndArmEnabledFlag @ 0x0040a90c (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Opens the WinMM "cdaudio" MCI device (mciSendCommandA MCI_OPEN, MCI_OPEN_TYPE|MCI_OPEN_SHAREABLE) and, only on success, stores the new device id in @0x412e20 and arms the audio-enabled gate @0x412e24 to 1.
// Status: done
/*
 * ROLE — the MCI bring-up leaf. This is the one function that actually OPENS the multimedia device;
 * every sibling in the low-0x40a transport cluster (DispatchMciPlaybackCommand @0x40a9c0,
 * DispatchMciSetFlagsAndPlay @0x40a958, HandleAudioTransportOpcode, UpdateMciAudioStateAndPlay
 * @0x4090d0) only re-uses the two globals this function arms.
 *
 * Body 0x40a90c..0x40a956, 19 instructions, plain 1-byte RET (0x40a956 = 0xC3) so it has NO stack
 * arguments and the callee cleans the stack (mciSendCommandA is WINAPI == __stdcall). Exactly ONE
 * indirect call, through the IAT slot @0x00401bc8.
 *
 *   SUB ESP,0x14                     ; 20-byte frame == sizeof(MCI_OPEN_PARMSA) on 32-bit
 *   XOR EAX,EAX                      ; EAX = 0, reused as the value for every zero fill
 *   MOV [0x00412e20],EAX             ; g_dwMciTaskId = 0   (clear previous device id)
 *   MOV [ESP+0x4],EAX                ; openParms.wDeviceID = 0 (MCI_OPEN requires 0 on entry)
 *   MOV [0x00412e24],EAX             ; g_dwMciAudioEnabled = 0 (disarm until success)
 *   MOV [ESP+0x8],0x41167d           ; openParms.lpstrDeviceType = "cdaudio" (literal @0x41167d)
 *   LEA ECX,[ESP]                    ; ECX = &openParms ([ESP+0])
 *   PUSH ECX                         ; arg4 (last push = first parameter -> pushed 1st of the 4)
 *   PUSH 0x2100                      ; arg3 = MCI_OPEN_TYPE|MCI_OPEN_SHAREABLE
 *   PUSH 0x803                       ; arg2 = MCI_OPEN
 *   PUSH EAX                         ; arg1 = mciId = 0 (must be 0 for MCI_OPEN)
 *   CALL dword ptr [0x00401bc8]      ; mciSendCommandA (see bridge verification note below)
 *   TEST EAX,EAX ; JNZ 0x0040a953    ; MCIERROR != 0 -> FAILURE, skip both stores
 *   MOV EAX,[ESP+0x4]                ; reload the device id mciSendCommandA filled in wDeviceID
 *   MOV [0x00412e20],EAX             ; g_dwMciTaskId = new device id
 *   MOV dword ptr [0x00412e24],0x1   ; g_dwMciAudioEnabled = 1 (ARM)
 *   ADD ESP,0x14 ; RET               ; caller's stack untouched: no args of our own
 *
 * IMPORT — verified by reading bytes, NOT trusting the bridge name. The IAT slot @0x00401bc8 holds
 * the dword 0x00001854 (an IMAGE_IMPORT_BY_NAME RVA). 0x00001854 + image base 0x400000 = 0x00401854;
 * bytes there are `00 00 6d 63 69 53 65 6e 64 43 6f 6d 6d 61 6e 64 41 00` = 2-byte hint 0x0000
 * followed by the NUL-terminated name "mciSendCommandA". So the name is genuinely mciSendCommandA
 * (winmm.dll). NOTE: get_function_callees reported this callee at "address":"0000005e", which is
 * spurious — the real IAT target RVA is 0x1854, not 0x5e.
 *
 * API SHAPE (mciapi.h): `MCIERROR WINAPI mciSendCommandA(MCIDEVICEID mciId, UINT uMsg,
 * DWORD_PTR dwParam1, DWORD_PTR dwParam2)` — FOUR arguments, __stdcall so the CALLEE pops them
 * (the ADD ESP,0x14 here only tears down the 0x14 local frame). Last push is the first parameter:
 *   mciId     = EAX                 = 0        (a zero device id is mandatory to open a new device)
 *   uMsg      = 0x803               = MCI_OPEN (mciapi.h line 144: `#define MCI_OPEN 0x0803`)
 *   dwParam1  = 0x2100              = open flags (see below)
 *   dwParam2  = &openParms          = the MCI_OPEN_PARMSA block built at [ESP]
 * RETURN (EAX): MCIERROR. 0 == success; nonzero == error code, which is what the function then
 * returns unchanged on the failure path.
 *
 * FLAGS 0x2100 — header evidence (mciapi.h): MCI_OPEN_TYPE = 0x00002000 (line 253) and
 * MCI_OPEN_SHAREABLE = 0x00000100 (line 248); 0x2000 | 0x0100 == 0x2100. No single named constant
 * equals 0x2100. MCI_OPEN_ELEMENT (0x200), MCI_OPEN_ALIAS (0x400), MCI_OPEN_ELEMENT_ID (0x800),
 * MCI_OPEN_TYPE_ID (0x1000), MCI_NOTIFY (0x1) and MCI_WAIT (0x2) are all absent. So the parent's
 * guess ("a shareable or type flag with an element or notify flag") is REFUTED on the second half:
 * the flags are exactly MCI_OPEN_TYPE | MCI_OPEN_SHAREABLE — TYPE says lpstrDeviceType names a
 * device TYPE (not an element/file), SHAREABLE requests shared access to the device.
 *
 * PARAMETER BLOCK at [ESP] (0x14 bytes) — mapped onto MCI_OPEN_PARMSA (mciapi.h lines 321-327):
 *   +0x00  DWORD_PTR   dwCallback        NOT written by this function (no MCI_NOTIFY is set, so the
 *                                        callback field is irrelevant and left as-is)
 *   +0x04  MCIDEVICEID wDeviceID         written 0; read back after the call as the new device id
 *   +0x08  LPCSTR      lpstrDeviceType   written 0x41167d -> "cdaudio"
 *   +0x0c  LPCSTR      lpstrElementName  NOT written (MCI_OPEN_ELEMENT not set)
 *   +0x10  LPCSTR      lpstrAlias        NOT written (MCI_OPEN_ALIAS not set)
 * The frame size 0x14 matches sizeof(MCI_OPEN_PARMSA) exactly. Memory at 0x41167d reads
 * `63 64 61 75 64 69 6f 00` = "cdaudio" — the WinMM CD-Audio device type. So this opens the
 * CD-audio MCI device. (wDeviceID/lpstrDeviceType are proven by the write offsets; dwCallback,
 * elementName and alias are only CONSISTENT-with the struct — the code never touches those slots,
 * which is exactly what a TYPE-only, non-notify OPEN looks like.)
 *
 * GLOBALS / ARMING:
 *   @0x00412e20 (g_dwMciTaskId)      <- the MCIDEVICEID returned in wDeviceID, on success only.
 *   @0x00412e24 (g_dwMciAudioEnabled)<- 1, on success only.
 * Both are zeroed (EAX=0) before the call; the JNZ skips both stores on FAILURE, so on a nonzero
 * MCIERROR BOTH globals keep their 0 value. The flag is a plain "armed/enabled" gate: sibling
 * DispatchMciPlaybackCommand @0x40a9c0 reads g_dwMciAudioEnabled (must be nonzero) and
 * g_dwMciTaskId to send STOP/PAUSE/RESUME/SET; HandleAudioTransportOpcode likewise calls @0x412e24
 * "the audio-enabled flag" and @0x412e20 the live winmm task id. It is re-zeroed at the top of
 * every call, so it is armed per successful open rather than a permanent latch.
 *
 * RETURN VALUE: on success the reloaded wDeviceID (the new device id); on failure the MCIERROR code.
 *
 * CALLER: FUN_0040aae0 (its only caller). That function is the audio/UT bring-up: it reads
 * GetVersion(), initialises a driver/handler table (InitializeUtDriverAndHandlerTable @0x40a684 or
 * InitializeAudioSubsystemAndUtHandlerTable @0x40a7bc), and then unconditionally CALL 0x0040a90c as
 * its final step, returning 1. So YES — this is the same open sequence those transport leaves depend
 * on; FUN_0040aae0 is what turns the MCI transport on at start-up.
 *
 * TRUE SIZE: body 0x40a90c..0x40a956 inclusive = 0x40a956 - 0x40a90c + 1 = 0x4B = 75 bytes. The RET
 * at 0x40a956 is the last byte (0xC3); the byte immediately after, 0x40a957, is 0xCC (INT3) alignment
 * padding. The selector's "76" counts that one padding byte (0x40a957 - 0x40a90c + 1 == 76); the
 * function itself is 75 bytes.
 */
````

````text
// OpenWaveOutAndPrepareHeaderRing @ 0x00409f10 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Opens the waveOut mapper as 11025 Hz 8-bit mono PCM with an event callback, then prepares the whole 8-header ring.
// Status: done
/*
 * ROLE — Init-and-setup half of NetWalk's runtime audio subsystem, the exact counterpart of
 * UnprepareAndCloseWaveOut (@0x00409ee0, round 24), which unprepares these same 8 headers at
 * 0x412ce0 and closes the handle at 0x412cd8. 1 caller, returns BOOL (AL = 1 success / 0 failure,
 * RET 4 so it is __stdcall).
 *
 * Original body (89 instructions, decompile <-> disassembly 1:1; stack frame 0x18 locals + 4 saved regs):
 *
 *  A. WAVEFORMATEX built on the stack at ESP+0x10 (offsets are the real WAVEFORMATEX fields):
 *     +0x10 WORD  = 1      WAVE_FORMAT_PCM          (wFormatTag)
 *     +0x12 WORD  = 1      mono                     (nChannels)
 *     +0x14 DWORD = 0x2b11 nSamplesPerSec = 11025
 *     +0x18 DWORD = 0x2b11 nAvgBytesPerSec = 11025 (8-bit mono -> == rate)
 *     +0x1c WORD  = 1      nBlockAlign = 1 * 1 ch * 1 byte
 *     +0x1e WORD  = 8      wBitsPerSample = 8
 *     +0x20 WORD  = 0      cbSize = 0               (PCM, no extra extension)
 *
 *  B. waveOutOpen(&g_hWaveOut @0x412cd8, 0xFFFFFFFF, &wfx, *pParams, 0, 0x10000)
 *        device  0xFFFFFFFF = WAVE_MAPPER, i.e. "any available output device"
 *        callback *pParams  — the caller-supplied WINDOW HANDLE, NOT the pointer itself
 *        hInstance 0 — unused because the callback is not a function pointer
 *        flags    0x10000  = CALLBACK_WINDOW -> completion sends MM_WOM_DONE to that
 *                                       window.  The earlier reading of 0x10000 as
 *                                       CALLBACK_EVENT (0x50000) made the rebuild pass a
 *                                       zero event handle on Windows, where waveOutOpen
 *                                       rejects the open; original trace: callback=main
 *                                       HWND, flags=0x10000.
 *     On failure: sndPlaySoundA(NULL, 0) — uFlags 0 = SND_SYNC, so the classic
 *     "stop whatever sound owns the device, blocking until it has" idiom — then waveOutOpen is
 *     retried with byte-identical arguments. Any second failure returns 0 without touching
 *     the ring (nothing has been prepared yet, so there is nothing to tear down).
 *
 *  C. waveOutGetID(g_hWaveOut, &g_uWaveOutDeviceId @0x412cdc) — the device id is stashed so the
 *     playback loop can compare it against the one delivered to the event callback. Failure
 *     falls into the teardown below and returns 0.
 *
 *  D. Header ring, 8 x sizeof(WAVEHDR) = 8 x 0x20 at 0x412ce0..0x412dfd, walked with a plain
 *     indexed count-out-of-eight loop (the sibling teardown walks the same ring with a
 *     do/while over &ring[8]). Per iteration k:
 *         ring[k].dwFlags        = 1 (in-use/selectable bit) <- BEFORE the call
 *         ring[k].lpData         = (LPBYTE)pParams + k * 0x800
 *         ring[k].dwBufferLength = 0x800 (2048 bytes = one full second at 11025 Hz 8-bit mono)
 *         ring[k].dwFlags        |= 1                 <- and again after the call returns
 *         waveOutPrepareHeader(g_hWaveOut, &ring[k], 0x20 = WHDR_UNPREPARED)
 *     (The original never writes dwBytesRecorded; the ring lives in loader-zeroed
 *      data and winmm ignores that field for playback, so it stays 0.)
 *     The buffer stride 0x800 and the end sentinel pParams+0x4000 give exactly
 *     0x4000 / 0x800 = 8 iterations; the loop breaks early on the first failing header.
 *     WHDR_UNPREPARED is passed to prepare, which forces the "not still playing" transition
 *     rather than WAVERR_STILLPLAYING — the mirror image of the teardown's unprepare call.
 *
 *  E. Success path: the last waveOutPrepareHeader returned MMSYSERR_NOERROR -> AL = 1, RET 4.
 *     Failure path (GetID, or any prepare): CALL UnprepareAndCloseWaveOut @0x00409ee0, which
 *     rolls back the headers that did get prepared plus the device handle, then AL = 0.
 *
 * The parameter is one caller-owned 0x4000-byte block: its first DWORD is the callback event
 * handle and its first 0x4000 bytes are the audio pool itself (header k buffers start at the
 * block base, not after the handle). The two views overlap at +0; the handle is only read once,
 * up front, before any buffer is queued, so the overlap is never observed. Modelled as a union
 * so the overlap is visible rather than silently papered over.
 */
````

````text
// ShutdownAudioSubsystem @ 0x0040a334 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Top-level audio teardown: resets the MIDI/timer-event state, ends the winmm timer period, then closes and clears the MIDI output handle.
// Status: done
/*
 * ROLE — Sequencing caller for NetWalk's runtime audio subsystem. It owns the ORDER in which
 * the low-level teardown steps run; the sibling leaf ResetMidiOutAndTimerEvent @0x0040a144
 * (2 callers) does the low-level work and owns the globals at 0x412de8 / 0x412de0.
 *
 * Body (12 instructions, decompile <-> disassembly 1:1, no parameters, no stack locals):
 *
 *   0x0040a334  CALL 0x0040a144             ; -> ResetMidiOutAndTimerEvent()
 *   0x0040a339  CMP dword ptr [0x00412e08],0x0
 *   0x0040a340  JZ  0x0040a358              ; period not armed -> skip timeEndPeriod
 *   0x0040a342  PUSH dword ptr [0x00412e08]
 *   0x0040a348  CALL dword ptr [0x00401c0c] ; -> timeEndPeriod (winmm import)
 *   0x0040a34e  MOV  dword ptr [0x00412e08],0x0
 *   0x0040a358  CMP dword ptr [0x00412de0],0x0
 *   0x0040a35f  JZ  0x0040a377              ; MIDI handle NULL -> skip midiOutClose
 *   0x0040a361  PUSH dword ptr [0x00412de0]
 *   0x0040a367  CALL dword ptr [0x00401c08] ; -> midiOutClose (winmm import)
 *   0x0040a36d  MOV  dword ptr [0x00412de0],0x0
 *   0x0040a377  RET
 *
 * ORDER is the whole point of this routine, and it is strictly inner-to-outer:
 *
 *   1. ResetMidiOutAndTimerEvent()  — UNCONDITIONAL, always first. Kills the live timeSetEvent
 *      timer (@0x412de8, if armed) and calls midiOutReset(@0x412de0) to silence the device and
 *      flush any queued voices. Doing this before midiOutClose is mandatory: midiOutClose on a
 *      device with queued notes leaks the output queue, and it fails outright if a timer event
 *      is still being serviced on the same thread.
 *   2. timeEndPeriod(@0x412e08)      — GUARDED on nonzero, then cleared to 0. Counterpart to the
 *      timeBeginPeriod that armed the fine-grained timer resolution; clearing the flag means a
 *      later re-arm path calls timeBeginPeriod again rather than assuming the period is active.
 *   3. midiOutClose(@0x412de0)       — GUARDED on nonzero, then cleared to 0. Closes the MIDI
 *      output device last, only after it has been reset, and leaves a NULL handle behind so a
 *      second teardown is a no-op and a restart re-opens cleanly.
 *
 * Both guards are CMP/JZ-skip (not conditional-call on the result), so the winmm calls run
 * once, unconditionally, whenever their flag is live; the JZ only skips the body. Every guarded
 * global is zeroed immediately after its call, so this routine is idempotent — calling it twice
 * runs step 1 (whose own midiOutReset is likewise unconditional) and skips steps 2 and 3.
 *
 * No winmm return value is examined anywhere: EAX from the final midiOutClose is discarded by
 * the plain RET, so all three steps are modelled as void. Failure to end the period or close the
 * device is silently ignored.
 *
 * Not handled here (belongs to other owners in the cluster): the waveOut half — unpreparing the
 * 8-header ring and waveOutClose — lives in UnprepareAndCloseWaveOut @0x409ee0, and the MCI
 * transport state (task id @0x412e20, audio-enabled flag @0x412e24) in
 * DispatchMciPlaybackCommand @0x0040a9c0. Neither global is read here.
 */
````

````text
// UnprepareAndCloseWaveOut @ 0x00409ee0 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Tears down the waveOut audio device: unprepares all 8 queued WAVEHDR headers, then closes the device handle.
// Status: done
/*
 * Audio-teardown leaf in the low-0x40a VM/audio-support cluster. Two callers (both in the
 * NetWalk audio stop/reset path) run this when playback has finished or audio is being shut down.
 *
 * Body, straight from the disassembly (13 instructions, no parameters, no stack locals):
 *
 *   0x409ee0  PUSH EBX
 *   0x409ee1  MOV EBX,0x412ce0          ; pHeader = &g_aWaveHeaders[0]
 *   do {
 *   0x409ee6  PUSH 0x20                  ; WHDR_UNPREPARED
 *   0x409ee8  PUSH EBX                   ; lpWaveOutHdr
 *   0x409ee9  PUSH dword ptr [0x412cd8]  ; hwo = g_hWaveOut
 *   0x409eef  CALL dword ptr [0x401bec]  ; waveOutUnprepareHeader (winmm import)
 *   0x409ef5  ADD EBX,0x20                ; sizeof(WAVEHDR) == 32
 *   0x409ef8  CMP EBX,0x412de0           ; &g_aWaveHeaders[8]
 *   0x409efe  JC 0x409ee6                ; } while (pHeader < end)
 *   0x409f00  PUSH dword ptr [0x412cd8]  ; hwo = g_hWaveOut
 *   0x409f06  CALL dword ptr [0x401be8]  ; waveOutClose (winmm import)
 *   0x409f0c  POP EBX
 *   0x409f0d  RET
 *
 * The loop is a do/while (PUSH 0x20 precedes the MOV that seeds EBX), so all eight headers are
 * unprepared unconditionally — it is not a "skip if empty" loop. Range 0x412ce0..0x412de0 is
 * 0x100 bytes = 8 * sizeof(WAVEHDR), i.e. the device's full double-buffered header ring.
 * WHDR_UNPREPARED (0x20) forces the unprepared transition rather than returning
 * WAVERR_STILLPLAYING for a header still in the queue.
 *
 * Neither winmm call's return value is tested; failure to unprepare one header or to close the
 * device is ignored, which is why the function is void. The callers are expected to have already
 * stopped playback (see the MCI STOP path in DispatchMciPlaybackCommand) — unpreparing a header
 * that is still playing would simply fail here and be discarded.
 */
````

````text
 * permanent VM trace is separately opt-in through NWVMTRACE, and the remaining
 * legacy audit logs (e.g. the audio event log) use NWAUDIT.  With none of
 * those variables set the default build is silent.
 *
 * It exists because the board screen renders as one flat colour and the
 * interesting quantities (the 12-byte stream record header, the decoded block
 * buffer, the published screen geometry) cannot be observed from outside the
 * process on this host: ptrace is refused, so no external reader exists.
 */
````

````text
// AcquireGridCellSpanRecordAndRetirePrevious @ 0x0040738c (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Acquires a free 16-byte arena slot, stamps it as the current grid-cell span record, retires and frees the previous Y- and X-cursor records of the current grid context, rebinds both context cursors to the new record, flags the context when the VM operand states disagree, and hands the record to the grid-reference resolver; always returns 1.
// Status: done
/*
 * Evidence: body 0x0040738c..0x004074f8, 104 instructions, RET 0x10 (bytes
 * c2 10 00 at 0x4074f6). TRUE SIZE = 0x4074f8 - 0x40738c + 1 = 109 bytes, and
 * the last instruction really is that RET 0x10 at 0x4074f6 (3 bytes, final
 * byte 0x4074f8). Both size derivations agree. The INT3 padding after it
 * (0x4074f9..) is NOT part of this body: read_memory shows c2 10 00 cc cc
 * cc cc c6 05 ..., so body_end lands exactly on the RET's last byte.
 *
 * CALLING CONVENTION / STACK ARGUMENTS (RET 0x10 => four dword args, __stdcall).
 * The prologue is SUB ESP,8 + PUSH EBX/EBP/ESI/EDI, so ESP sits 0x18 below
 * entry and every [ESP+X] below maps to entry [ESP+X-0x18]. Read off the
 * disassembly (the Ghidra signature agrees):
 *   [ESP+0x1C] = entry [ESP+4]  = bRefRelative  byte  (0x4073b9, 0x4073e1, 0x4074a5)
 *   [ESP+0x20] = entry [ESP+8]  = wCellOffsetY  word  (0x4073d8 -> record +0x0A)
 *   [ESP+0x24] = entry [ESP+C]  = wCellOffsetX  word  (0x4073cf -> record +0x08)
 *   [ESP+0x28] = entry [ESP+10] = nRefTabIndex  dword (0x407393 -> table index)
 *
 * NOTE the X/Y argument order: the SECOND argument feeds the record's +0x0A
 * (Y) and the THIRD feeds +0x08 (X). That is not a typo in the decompiler --
 * 0x4073cf loads [ESP+0x24] into +0x08 and 0x4073d8 loads [ESP+0x20] into
 * +0x0A, so the caller's Y word is the second stack slot.
 *
 * ESP DISCIPLINE: both callees used below are stack-cleaning, so the spilled
 * locals at [ESP+0x10] / [ESP+0x14] survive the calls. Verified from raw
 * bytes rather than assumed: AddGridCellSpanToExtentList ends `c2 04 00` at
 * 0x40935b, and FreeArenaSlot's epilogue is `RET 0x4` at 0x404b38 -- the c3
 * at 0x404b3c is a mid-body jump target reached by `JMP 0x404b43`, NOT the
 * epilogue. AcquireNextFreeSlot and ResolveGridReferenceAndAddCellSpan take
 * no stack arguments.
 *
 * ORDER, which matters and must not be reordered:
 *   1. compute the reference-selection entry BEFORE allocating anything
 *        ESI = [0x417300] + nRefTabIndex*8          (0x407393-0x40739d)
 *   2. ACQUIRE the slot                             (0x4073a0)
 *   3. FILL the header fields                      (0x4073a7-0x4073dd)
 *   4. RETIRE the old records / rebind the cursors (0x407401-0x4074d1) --
 *      only when bRefRelative == 0, and this is the block that calls
 *      AddGridCellSpanToExtentList and FreeArenaSlot
 *   5. DISPATCH to the resolver, which is what registers the NEW record's
 *      extent entry and fills its +0x0C              (0x4074df-0x4074e5)
 *   6. return 1 unconditionally                      (0x4074ea)
 *
 * So it is acquire -> fill -> retire-old -> rebind -> dispatch, NOT a plain
 * allocate. The AddGridCellSpanToExtentList call in step 4 is on the RETIRED
 * record, not on the new one: the new record's extent registration happens
 * inside ResolveGridReferenceAndAddCellSpan, which calls that same helper at
 * its own tail (0x40955d).
 *
 * Record layout (EBX), 16 bytes, shared with c/AllocGridCellSpanRecord.c and
 * with the GridCellRec of c/ResolveGridReferenceAndAddCellSpan.c:
 *   +0x00 byte    bStatus    arena in-use bit 0 (from AcquireNextFreeSlot),
 *                             OR 0x80 here ("is the current top record"),
 *                             plus bit 2 (0x04) copied from the reference
 *                             entry's +0x01 bit 0
 *   +0x02 byte    bKind      raw copy of reference entry byte +0x03
 *   +0x03 byte    bLink      raw UNMASKED byte copy -- see below
 *   +0x04 byte    bLimitA    0xff when bRefRelative != 0, untouched otherwise
 *   +0x05 byte    bLimitB    0xff when bRefRelative != 0, untouched otherwise
 *   +0x06 word    wUserData  0xffff when bRefRelative != 0, else [0x41721c]
 *   +0x08 int16   iOffsetX   = wCellOffsetX (3rd stack argument)
 *   +0x0A int16   iOffsetY   = wCellOffsetY (2nd stack argument)
 *   +0x0C dword   pRefRec    written by the resolver, not here
 *
 * +0x03 IS WRITTEN UNMASKED -- CONFIRMED, not assumed. All three stores are
 * plain byte copies with no AND/OR between them:
 *   0x4073f9  MOV byte [EBX+3],CL   from [0x417218]+5   (bRefRelative != 0)
 *   0x4074a2  MOV byte [EBX+3],CL   from [0x417218]+5   (ctx live path)
 *   0x4074dc  MOV byte [EBX+3],CL   from [0x417214]+2   (ctx == NULL path)
 * All eight bits reach the record, whatever their sense. The releaser's masked
 * restore (AND AH,0xf0) lives in a different function and is NOT visible from
 * this body, so that half of the round-42 round-trip claim is left unverified
 * here -- this body supplies the unmasked half and nothing more. The only
 * masking this function performs is AND 0x7F on the OLD record's +0x00 at
 * 0x407452, which clears the 0x80 top mark that 0x4073a7 set and preserves
 * every other bit.
 *
 * Context record layout (0x417218), 16 bytes:
 *   +0x00 byte  bCtxFlags  OR'd with 0x04 here (0x4074ce) when the two mirrored
 *                          VM operand-state word pairs disagree
 *   +0x05 byte  bLinkSrc   copied verbatim into the new record's +0x03
 *   +0x08 word  wCurXIdx   arena cursor X: slot index, 0xffff = none
 *   +0x0A word  wCurYIdx   arena cursor Y: slot index, 0xffff = none
 *
 * A slot INDEX is recovered from a pointer by (g_pSlotsTop - rec) / 16, and the
 * reverse by rec = g_pSlotsTop - index*16. Both use the same fixed 0x10 stride
 * as the arena walkers in c/AcquireNextFreeSlot.c and c/FreeArenaSlot.c, so the
 * two cursors index that same chain and 0xffff is the empty-cursor sentinel.
 *
 * The 0xffff sentinels belong to the CONTEXT cursors (+0x08/+0x0A) and to the
 * record's +0x06 -- NOT to the record's +0x08/+0x0A, which this function
 * unconditionally overwrites with the caller's two offset words.
 *
 * ROLE I BELIEVE FOR EACH GLOBAL, and why:
 *   0x417218 is the current grid context and is both read and written here.
 *   0x417214 is a FALLBACK source of the link byte only, reached when 0x417218
 *   is NULL; this body never writes it and never treats it as a context.
 *   0x41721c is a plain 16-bit word (only CX is taken at 0x4073c5).
 *   0x417300 is the base of an 8-byte-stride reference-selection table, the
 *   same table c/AllocGridCellSpanRecord.c addresses as g_pRefSelTable.
 */
````

````text
// AddGridCellSpanToExtentList @ 0x0040931c (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Converts a grid record's computed int16 cell offsets into a bounding rectangle in reference-record space and hands it to the global extent list, subtracting the reference baseline first when the record's 0x40 flag is set.
// Status: done
/*
 * Record layout (EDI), from disassembly 0x40931c-0x40935b and the decompilation:
 *   +0x00 byte    bFlags    bit6 (0x40): offsets are relative to the reference
 *                            baseline, so the int16 baselines at +0x4/+0x6 are
 *                            subtracted from the cell offset before use
 *   +0x08 int16   iOffsetX  cell offset X, MOVSX-signed
 *   +0x0A int16   iOffsetY  cell offset Y, MOVSX-signed
 *   +0x0C dword   pRefRec   pointer to the reference record
 *
 * Reference record layout (EAX / *EBX), matching GridRefRec in
 * ComputeScaledGridOffset @0x40921c — this binary's sibling consumer of the
 * same records, which writes those same int16 fields at +8/+A:
 *   [+0x00] dword -> two consecutive int16 words: source X, source Y.
 *              Both are read here zero-extended (MOVZX word), so they are
 *              unsigned 16-bit quantities, unlike the signed baselines.
 *   [+0x04] int16 iBaseX  baseline X, MOVSX-signed
 *   [+0x06] int16 iBaseY  baseline Y, MOVSX-signed
 *

 * on the unflagged path they are simply the record's own cell offsets, which
 * this function treats as the rectangle's origin. The rectangle's far corner
 * is the source extent's corner plus the same span, hence the pattern
 * (source + n) appearing in the max-coordinate arguments.
````

````text
 *                             bit6 (0x40): offsets already reference-relative,
 *                                        so they are NOT recomputed here
 *   +0x01 byte  bSubIndex    index of the sub-span just emitted
 *   +0x02 byte  bSubCount    number of 8-byte sub-spans in this group

 *                            readings reconcile: it is a POINTER that is advanced in
````

````text
// AdvancePendingGridCellSpanEntryAndDispatch @ 0x0040279c (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Drains the grid context's already-pending entry, then republishes the context's pending index and dispatch flag — either keeping the caller-supplied index or redrawing one by weighted random from the pool table — and dispatches the chosen state entry's script step through its +0x04 cursor.
// Status: done
/*
 * 43 instructions, entry 0x0040279c, `RET 0x8` at 0x00402839 (bytes C2 08 00).
 *
 * SIZE, DERIVED BOTH WAYS, AND THEY AGREE:
 *   formula : body_end 0x0040283b - body_start 0x0040279c + 1 = 0xA0 = 160 bytes
 *   real    : last instruction `RET 0x8` starts at 0x00402839 and the verified
 *             bytes there are C2 08 00, so it ends at 0x0040283b inclusive:
 *             0x00402839 - 0x0040279c + 3 = 157 + 3 = 160 bytes.
 * No trailing INT3 padding is absorbed by either figure: the byte after
 * 0x0040283b is 0x00 and the next three are 83 EC 0C (SUB ESP,0xC), which is the
 * prologue of the very next function at 0x0040283c. There is no gap here.
 *
 * CALLING CONVENTION — `RET 0x8` settles it: __stdcall, two stack arguments, and
 * the callee pops them, so there is no trailing ADD ESP. The two arguments, read
 * off the disassembly and NOT off the decompiler:
 *   S = ESP after the two prologue pushes (PUSH EBX / PUSH ESI), i.e. entry ESP-8.
 *     [S+0x0c] = arg1, a BYTE  — tested against 0 at 0x004027a3 (`CMP byte ptr
 *                 [ESP+0xc],0`). When non-zero the index is redrawn from the pool.
 *     [S+0x10] = arg2, a DWORD — the caller-supplied state-table index.
 *
 * ARG2 IS A SCRATCH SLOT, NOT JUST AN ARGUMENT. [S+0x10] is overwritten twice
 * inside the redraw branch (0x004027cb stores the MUL high word, 0x004027d5
 * stores the picked byte) and is read again at 0x004027f2 and 0x0040280a. So the
 * function CONSUMES its own second argument: there is no way to observe the
 * caller's value after it returns. The decompiler's rendering of arg2 as a local
 * it assigns to is an accurate accident.
 *
 * ORDER OF THE TWO CALLS — ProcessPendingGridCellSpanEntry (@0x004025d0) runs
 * FIRST and UNCONDITIONALLY, at 0x0040279e, before the redraw test at 0x004027a3
 * and therefore before everything else including the flag-set case. It drains the
 * entry the context already had pending and re-arms ctx+2 / ctx+3 to 0xFE / 0xF0
 * (its `MOV word [EAX+2],0xF0FE`). Only THEN does this function pick the new
 * index and overwrite those same two bytes with the pick and 0x10. So the drain
 * is not conditional on the redraw flag: a call with arg1 == 0 still drains, then
 * republishes arg2 unchanged.
 *
 * THE DRAIN'S SENTINEL CAN BE RE-PUBLISHED, because the byte written at 0x004027fc
 * is unconditional. The drain leaves ctx+2 = 0xFE (its "nothing pending" marker)
 * and ctx+3 = 0xF0; this function then overwrites both with the index and 0x10
 * regardless. A caller passing dwStateIndex == 0xFE therefore publishes the
 * sentinel together with flag 0x10, which makes the NEXT drain call (0x004025d0)
 * take its early-out. That is read straight off the two byte stores at
 * 0x004027fc/0x00402807 plus the 0xFE test in the drain at 0x004025dc — no
 * separate evidence for it is claimed.
 *
 * RETURN VALUE: there is none. Ghidra's `void` is correct. The last write to EAX
 * before the epilogue is `MOV AL,0x10` at 0x004027ff, a one-byte write of the very
 * flag byte just stored to ctx+3, so AL is incidentally 0x10 on both exits while
 * the upper 24 bits are whatever the drain call left there (or, on the redraw
 * path, the high dword of the LCG multiply). Nothing reads it and no caller is
 * known to.
 *
 * THE REDRAW IS THE SAME WEIGHTED PICK AS THE POOL PATH IN
 * c/AllocateGridCellSpanRecordAndDispatch.c @0x0040283c, and the two agree
 * instruction for instruction:
 *   with w = the seed's high word read at 0x004111ca (a zero-extended 16-bit
 *   load, the same dword as 0x4111c8) and n = pPickArray[0],
 *     index = pPickArray[ ((w * n) >> 16) + 1 ]
 *   then the LCG advances AFTER the read, so the pick uses the pre-advance seed.
 * `MUL ECX` at 0x004027c6 is 32x32->64 with the high dword discarded; since
 * w <= 0xFFFF and n <= 0xFF the product cannot exceed 32 bits, so the `SHR EAX,
 * 0x10` at 0x004027c8 is exactly (w*n)>>16 and is not a 64-bit shift.
 * THE LCG DOES NOT ADVANCE AT ALL when arg1 == 0.
 *
 * A REAL ASYMMETRY THE ARGUMENT WIDTH CREATES. The published index and the
 * dispatched index are read at DIFFERENT WIDTHS from the same slot:
 *   0x004027f2  MOV AL,  byte ptr [ESP+0x10]   -> ctx+2 gets only the LOW byte
 *   0x0040280a  MOV EBX, dword ptr [ESP+0x10]  -> the table index is the FULL dword
 * so a caller-supplied arg2 >= 0x100 publishes (dwPoolIndex & 0xFF) to the
 * context while dispatching g_pStateTable[dwPoolIndex]. On the redraw path the
 * slot holds a zero-extended byte and the two cannot disagree. The pool lookup is
 * likewise unmasked: 0x004027b3/0x004027b7 use the full dword.
 *
 * THE TWO CALL SITES OF ExecuteScriptInstruction. Its recovered epilogue is
 * `ADD ESP,0x18 / POP EBX / POP ESI / POP EDI / RET 0x20` at 0x00402454, i.e.
 * __stdcall popping 8 dwords — which independently confirms the eight PUSHes
 * here. Pushes are right-to-left, so the LAST push is the callee's FIRST argument:
 *   0x00402830 PUSH 0x10                      -> arg1 bFlag       = 0x10
 *   0x0040282d PUSH dword [ctx+7]             -> arg2 bOperandA   = byte at ctx+7
 *   0x0040282a PUSH dword [ctx+6]             -> arg3 bOperandB   = byte at ctx+6
 *   0x00402822 PUSH 0x0                       -> arg4 dwCtxA      = 0
 *   0x0040281d PUSH 0xffff                    -> arg5 dwCtxB      = 0xFFFF
 *   0x0040281b PUSH 0x0                       -> arg6 dwCtxC      = 0
 *   0x0040281a PUSH EBX                       -> arg7 dwCtxD      = &g_pStateTable[idx]
 *   0x00402817 PUSH dword [EBX+4]             -> arg8 pCursor     = entry->+0x04
 * The dword push at +6 spans +6..+9 and the one at +7 spans +7..+10, but the
 * callee consumes only the low byte of each, so neither leaks neighbouring
 * context bytes into the dispatch. The `POP ESI / POP EBX` pair after the CALL
 * restores the two prologue saves and nothing else.
 *
 * ON THE TWO SIBLING FILES (checked against bytes, not against their prose):
 *   c/ProcessPendingGridCellSpanEntry.c — every structural claim it makes about
 *   this caller is CONFIRMED: drain first, redraw only when the flag is set,
 *   pool table at 0x41724c, ctx+2 = index and ctx+3 = 0x10, dispatch cursor at
 *   entry+0x04 while that file dispatches entry+0x0C. ONE MINOR ORDERING NIT:
 *   it says "advances the LCG ..., picks a new index", but the pick at
 *   0x004027c0-0x004027d5 happens BEFORE the advance at 0x004027d9-0x004027e8.
 *   Its conclusion (the pick uses the pre-advance seed) is unaffected. I did NOT
 *   test its separate claim that this is the only caller of 0x004025d0 — my
 *   absolute-reference scan says nothing about who calls 0x004025d0.
 *   c/AllocateGridCellSpanRecordAndDispatch.c — no contradiction; the pool-pick
 *   idiom matches. ADDITION: that file describes g_pPoolTable as indexed by
 *   dwOpcode byte0 on ITS pool path only. This function indexes the SAME table
 *   by its OWN argument 2 and reads only the +0x4 pick array, never the +0x8
 *   handler array — so the pool table has a second, independent indexer, and the
 *   +8 array is genuinely unused from this direction.
 *
 * ENTRY MECHANISM IS UNRESOLVED, AND THAT IS A FINDING, NOT AN ASSUMPTION.
 * 0x0040279c appears as a 4-byte absolute value nowhere in the scanned image
 * (0x401000-0x419000), so it is not a callback-table entry, not a MOV/PUSH
 * immediate, and is absent from both recovered handler tables at 0x411114 and
 * 0x411178. That negative is trustworthy: the same scan, same code path, finds
 * its genuinely-absolute in-body operands — 0x417218 at 63 sites, 0x4111ca at 19,
 * the LCG multiplier 0x41c64e6d at 24. It proves only that no ABSOLUTE reference
 * exists; it cannot exclude a direct CALL, because CALL rel32 stores an offset
 * from the next instruction and would never match. I did not find a mechanism and

 */
````

````text
// AllocateGridCellSpanRecordAndDispatch @ 0x0040283c (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Allocates and inserts a grid-cell span record for one cell, retiring that cell's existing spans first, then dispatches the resulting script step; a pending-index byte can instead be drawn at random from a weighted pool table.
// Status: done
/*
 * 157 instructions, 0x0040283c-0x00402a64, `RET 0xc` (stdcall, three dword
 * arguments, VOID return — nothing meaningful is left in EAX on either exit).
 * Ghidra reports body_end = 0x00402a66; the real last instruction is the 3-byte
 * `RET imm16` at 0x00402a64, which ends at 0x00402a67. Size is taken from the
 * disassembly, per the documented 3-byte-RET under-report.
 *
 * THE DECOMPILATION IS WRONG ABOUT THE ARGUMENTS AND WAS NOT USED FOR THEM.
 * `/decompile_function` prints `ReleaseGridCellSpanRecordsAndDispatchEntry(1,
 * unaff_retaddr, param_1)` and `ExecuteScriptInstruction(param_2._1_1_,
 * (byte)unaff_retaddr, (byte)param_1, ...)` — i.e. it invents a phantom
 * `unaff_retaddr` and a phantom `unaff_BL` in place of the two real stack
 * argument reads. There is no EBX/BL argument: EBX is set up by the prologue
 * and BL is loaded from [ESP+0x10], a LOCAL. This is the round-36
 * "decompiler drops / mis-maps a direct call's arguments" defect family, and it
 * is maximally misleading here because the function's whole job is handing
 * (major, minor) to two callees. Everything below is reconstructed from
 * `/disassemble_function`; the decompile agreed only on the pool-selection
 * arithmetic and on dispatch args 4-8.
 *
 * Frame: SUB ESP,0xc + PUSH EBX/EBP/ESI/EDI. Let S be ESP after the prologue:
 *   [S+0x20] = param_1  nCellMajor  (the SHIFTED axis)
 *   [S+0x24] = param_2  nCellMinor  (the unshifted axis)
 *   [S+0x28] = param_3  dwOpcode    (a 3-byte word; byte0/byte1 have the
 *                                    meanings given below, byte2 is only ever
 *                                    seen by the opcode handlers, which get
 *                                    a POINTER to the whole dword)
 *   [S+0x10] = local bPickIndex, then reused as the arena depth index
 *   [S+0x14] = local dwPayloadBytes
 *   [S+0x18] = local pPoolRec
 * EBP = pCellEntry (the 2-byte cell entry) and ESI = pStateEntry (the 0x10
 * -stride state entry). Both are callee-saved and survive every call below.
 * `get_function_variables` reports two locals named local_4/local_c and marks
 * BOTH is_phantom; the three real locals are the unnamed stack words above.
 *
 * Control flow, in address order:
 *
 *   pCellEntry = &g_pCellEntryBase[(nCellMajor << g_dwAxisShift) + nCellMinor];
 *                                                  ; 0x402843-0x402859
 *   bPick = (uint8_t)dwOpcode;                      ; 0x40285c-0x402862
 *
 *   if (dwOpcode & 0x100) {                         ; 0x40286a TEST CL,0x1
 *       pPoolRec = &g_pPoolTable[bPick * 0x10];      ; 0x402873-0x402876
 *       pHooks    = pPoolRec->pHandlers;             ; [pPoolRec+0x8]
 *       if (pHooks) {
 *           b = pool[((seed>>16) * pool[0]) >> 16];  ; 0x402883-0x4028a4
 *           LCG_advance();                           ; 0x4028a8
 *           (dwOpcode >> 8) = pHooks[b];             ; 0x4028cd-0x4028d4
 *           g_apPoolHandlers[(dwOpcode>>8)>>4](&dwOpcode);   ; 0x4028dd
 *       }
 *       g_apOpcodeHandlers[(dwOpcode>>8)>>4](&dwOpcode);      ; 0x4028f2
 *       LCG_advance();                               ; 0x4028f9-0x402908
 *   }
 *
 *   bPick = local;                                  ; 0x402912
 *   dwOpcode = (dwOpcode & ~0xFF) | bPick;           ; 0x402916
 *   pStateEntry = &g_pStateTable[bPick];             ; 0x402922
 *
 *   if ((dwOpcode & 0x100) == 0 && bPick == 0xFE) {  ; 0x402a37 (taken from 0x40286d)
 *       ReleaseGridCellSpanRecordsAndDispatchEntry(1, nCellMajor, nCellMinor);
 *       *pCellEntry = (uint16_t)dwOpcode;            ; 0x402a54-0x402a59
 *       return;                                      ; no dispatch, no LCG
 *   }
 *
 *   if (pStateEntry->byte0 != 0) {                   ; 0x402928
 *       ReleaseGridCellSpanRecordsAndDispatchEntry(0, nCellMajor, nCellMinor);
 *       pRec  = AcquireNextFreeSlot();               ; 0x40295c
 *       ... fill 16 bytes ...                        ; 0x40296d-0x4029ab
 *       dwPayloadBytes = pStateEntry->byte3 + 1;     ; 0x4029af-0x4029b5
 *       if (dwPayloadBytes > 4) { pRec->pPayload = AllocHeapBlock(...);
 *                                   FillMemoryWithZeroBytes(...);
 *                                   pRec->bStatusFlags |= 0x08; }
 *       else                { pRec->pPayload = NULL; arg4 = &pRec->+0x0C; }
 *       bDepthIndex = (g_pSlotsTop - pRec) / 0x10;   ; 0x4029e2-0x4029f1

 *           g_pActiveSlot = pRec;                    ; 0x4029f5-0x402a03

 *                            pStateEntry->pCursorA);
````
