 * THE LCG ADVANCES TWICE ON THE POOL PATH AND ONCE OTHERWISE, NEVER ON THE
 * 0xFE PATH. The three `IMUL [0x4111c8],0x41c64e6d / MOV / ADD 0x3039`
 * sequences sit at 0x4028a8 (after the weighted pick, inside `if (pHooks)`),
 * at 0x4029f9 (after the always-run opcode handler) and nowhere else. The
 * 0xFE sentinel path returns at 0x402a64 without reaching either of the last
 * two. State is `seed = seed * 214013 + 2531011` and the selector reads the
 * seed's HIGH WORD at 0x4111ca — which is the same dword, read half-open —
 * so the pick uses the seed value from BEFORE this function's first advance.
 *
 * THE 0xFE SENTINEL IS ONLY TESTED ON THE NON-POOL PATH. 0x402a37 compares the
 * FULL DWORD [S+0x10] against 0xFE, and it is reachable only from 0x40286d
 * (bit 8 clear), where [S+0x10] is the zero-extended low byte of dwOpcode. So
 * the effective test is `(dwOpcode & 0xFF) == 0xFE` and the dword compare is
 * an artifact of how the local was built, not a wider check. When the pool
 * path has run, [S+0x10] holds the picked index and this test is unreachable
 * anyway.
 *
 * THE CELL KEY IS BUILT BY TWO SEPARATE BYTE STORES AND IS LOW-MINOR /
 * HIGH-MAJOR, matching the producer/consumer pair exactly:
 *   0x402980 MOV CL,byte ptr [ESP+0x24] / MOV [EBX+6],CL   -> (byte)nCellMinor
 *   0x402987 MOV CL,byte ptr [ESP+0x20] / MOV [EBX+7],CL   -> (byte)nCellMajor
 * which is little-endian wCellKey = (minor & 0xFF) | ((major & 0xFF) << 8),
 * the identical packing c/ReleaseGridCellSpanRecordsAndDispatchEntry.c builds
 * at 0x4026a3/0x4026ab from ITS (nCellMajor, nCellMinor) parameters. The two
 * agreeing is what pins the axis names: nCellMajor is the SHIFTED axis here
 * (0x40284d) and is the callee's SECOND argument.
 *
 * BOTH RELEASE CALLS PASS (mode, nCellMajor, nCellMinor), and the decompile's
 * argument order is wrong. Tracked with the pushes, since each PUSH shifts the
 * frame by 4:
 *   0x40292d PUSH [ESP+0x24]  -> reads [S+0x24] = nCellMinor  (becomes arg3)
 *   0x402931 PUSH [ESP+0x24]  -> ESP is S-4, reads [S+0x20] = nCellMajor (arg2)
 *   0x402935 PUSH 0x1         -> arg1
 * The 0x40294d/0x402951/0x402955 site is identical with `PUSH 0x0`, and so is
 * the 0xFE site at 0x402a45/0x402a49/0x402a4d with `PUSH 0x1`.
 *
 * FULL-SWEEP MODE IS CHOSEN BY THE ENTRY'S OWN FIRST BYTE, NOT BY THE ARGUMENT.
 * An entry whose byte0 is 0 (inactive) gets mode 1 — retire orphans too — and
 * no new record; an entry whose byte0 is non-zero gets mode 0, which retires
 * only grouped spans, and then gets a fresh record. Same cell, same argument
 * order, opposite sweep policy, decided by the state table.
 *
 * ROUND-37 ARENA CLAIMS — CONFIRMED FROM THE PRODUCER SIDE, which is stronger
 * than the consumer-side evidence the closure was based on:
 *   1. HETEROGENEOUS ARENA: confirmed. This function allocates from the same
 *      arena (AcquireNextFreeSlot / g_pSlotsTop) and writes +0x00 =
 *      (dwOpcode_byte1 & 0xF0) | 0x03, which sets bit 1. It therefore
 *      manufactures the GROUPED flavor that the orphan-path readers cannot see.
 *   2. BYTE +0x00 BIT 1 DISCRIMINATES TWO FLAVORS: confirmed, and bit 1 is set
 *      explicitly here rather than merely tested elsewhere.
 *   3. NEVER READ +0x06 WITHOUT TESTING BIT 1: confirmed, and this function is
 *      why that rule exists — it writes +0x06 as a packed cell key while setting
 *      bit 1, whereas the orphan flavor's +0x06 is the 0xFFFF unset stamp. The
 *      record it builds has 0xFFFF in BOTH +0x08 and +0x0A, so it is also
 *      inert as an orphan record and can only ever be matched by a bit-1 test.
 *
 * CONTRADICTIONS WITH c/ReleaseGridCellSpanRecordsAndDispatchEntry.c, reported
 * loudly because three of its statements about THIS caller are wrong:
 *
 *   A. THE RECORD BYTE ORDER IS SWAPPED IN THAT FILE. It claims
 *      `pbVar5[6] = (byte)param_1` ("LOW byte = minor") and
 *      `pbVar5[7] = (byte)unaff_retaddr` ("HIGH byte = major"). The
 *      disassembly is the other way round: +6 is written from [ESP+0x24] =
 *      param_2 = nCellMinor and +7 from [ESP+0x20] = param_1 = nCellMajor.
 *      That file's PACKING conclusion survives (low byte = minor, high byte =
 *      major) and is confirmed here, but only because its two Ghidra variables
 *      were mislabelled: `unaff_retaddr` is the phantom that stands for
 *      param_2 here. It should read pbVar5[6] = (byte)nCellMinor,
 *      pbVar5[7] = (byte)nCellMajor.
 *
 *   B. BOTH CALL SITES ARE MIS-TRANSCRIBED IN THAT FILE. It writes
 *      `FUN_00402654('\x00', unaff_retaddr, param_1)` and glosses it
 *      "= (minor, major)". The actual call is
 *      ReleaseGridCellSpanRecordsAndDispatchEntry(mode, param_1, param_2), and
 *      the callee's own recovered signature is (bFullSweepMode, nCellMajor,
 *      nCellMinor). Its gloss is backwards, and it missed the mode-1 call in
 *      the 0xFE path entirely (three call sites at 0x402937, 0x402957,
 *      0x402a4f, not two).
 *
 *   C. ITS CLAIM THAT +0x0C IS AN "8-BYTE-STRIDE SUB-SPAN ARRAY" IS REFUTED.
 *      The block is sized in BYTES: dwPayloadBytes = pStateEntry->byte3 + 1
 *      (0x4029b1-0x4029b5) is passed to AllocHeapBlock, whose own body
 *      (0x4048fc) converts a byte size to dwords — SHR EDX,2 / round up / INC
 *      — and to FillMemoryWithZeroBytes, which is
 *      `memset(pDst, 0, dwCount)` (0x409664: PUSH pDst / PUSH 0 / PUSH count /
 *      CALL 0x40de1c). N elements at an 8-byte stride would need 8N bytes;
 *      here N bytes are allocated and N bytes are cleared. With the inline
 *      threshold at 4, the payload is at most 4 bytes and lives inside the
 *      slot's own last dword (&pRec->pPayload is passed as dispatch arg 4).
 *
 *   D. MINOR CORRECTION TO ITS DISPATCH MODEL. It models g_pStateTable as
 *      having cursors at +0x04 and +0x0C and passes +0x0C itself. This function
 *      passes [pStateEntry+0x04] (0x402a12) as arg8 — the same +0x04 that
 *      c/ProcessPendingGridCellSpanEntry.c already attributes to this caller.
 *      Both cursors exist; the two callers use different ones.
 *
 * ADDITIONS TO THE SHARED RECORD MODEL (no contradiction, but the existing
 * files do not carry these):
 *   - BYTE +0x03 IS A TWO-BIT FLAG BYTE and bit 0 is NOT the in-use bit.
 *     0x4029a3/0x4029a9: `CMP EBX,[0x417218] / JNC skip` then `OR byte
 *     [EBX+3],0x1` — bit 0 is set iff the new slot's address is BELOW
 *     g_pCurGridCtx. That is the mirror of RestartCurrentGridSpanGroup's
 *     `OR byte [EAX+3],0x2` (group-pending). Bit 0 = below-current-context,
 *     bit 1 = group-pending, and the in-use bit lives in byte +0x00.
 *   - BYTE +0x01 = the state-entry index this record was built for; that is the
 *     index c/SelectNextActiveSlot.c uses to address g_pStateTable.
 *   - BYTE +0x02/+0x03 receive the cell entry's ENTIRE 16-bit word, unmasked
 *     (0x40299b/0x40299f `MOV CX,word [EBP]`). The releaser's restore store is
 *     masked instead (`AND AH,0xf0`), so the round trip is NOT lossless: the
 *     low nibble of the record's +0x03 is dropped on the way back.
 *   - BYTE +0x04 is set to 0 and BYTE +0x05 copies the state entry's byte 2.
 *
 * Globals touched — the COMPLETE set, verified by dumping every absolute memory
 * operand in the body (32 sites, nothing else beyond the call targets):
 *   @0x417240 g_pSlotsTop      read once, to derive the new record's depth index
 *   @0x417248 g_pStateTable    0x10-stride state entries, indexed by the picked byte
 *   @0x41724c g_pPoolTable     a SECOND 0x10-stride table, indexed by dwOpcode byte0
 *                              on the pool path only; +4 is a byte array to pick
 *                              from, +8 an optional per-pick handler array
 *   @0x417250 g_pCellEntryBase 2-byte-stride cell table (same lookup as the releaser)
 *   @0x417254 g_dwAxisShift    shift for the major axis (NOT masked here)
 *   @0x417218 g_pCurGridCtx    threshold for the record's +0x03 bit 0
 *   @0x4121b4 g_pActiveSlot    adopted when the entry kind is 3 and none is active
 *   @0x4111c8 dwRngState       LCG state; its high word at 0x4111ca is the selector
 *   @0x411114 g_apPoolHandlers 16 slots, indexed by (dwOpcode byte1) >> 4
 *   @0x411178 g_apOpcodeHandlers 16 slots, indexed by (dwOpcode byte1) >> 4
 *

 * `MOV ECX,[0x417254] / SHL EAX,CL` with no `AND CL,0x1f`, yet the
 * decompilation prints `(byte)DAT_00417254 & 0x1f`. The mask is the
 * decompiler's own, not the binary's. c/ReleaseGridCellSpanRecordsAndDispatchEntry.c
 * writes the masked form in its C and says the asm masks it; that is at least
 * true for the two globals' shared role but should be re-checked in the
 * releaser's own bytes, because here it demonstrably is not in the asm.
 *
 * Both opcode tables were decoded live rather than assumed: 0x411114 is mostly
 * a single 0x402140 target (idx 1,2,4 and 8 differ) and 0x411178 is fully
 * populated with 0x402144..0x402384. Both are indexed by the high nibble of
 * dwOpcode byte1, so the two tables are a two-level dispatch on the same
 * operand. Neither table is uniform, so no peer file's claim about "the"
 * handler table can be carried over.
 *
 * All five callees are already recovered; none is a stub.
 */

// ApplyDeltaToUnmarkedEntries @ 0x004061f0 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Walks a table of 16-byte records and adds nDelta to the field at +0xC of every record whose flag byte at +0 has bit 1 clear, then returns.
// Status: done
/*
 * ROLE — Zero-callee leaf inside the NetWalk VM-support / WINMM audio cluster.
 *
 * Disassembly (complete body, 22 bytes, RET 0xC => __stdcall, three stack args):
 *   004061f0  PUSH EBX
 *   004061f1  MOV  EBX,dword ptr [ESP + 0x8]   ; EBX = nDelta      (arg1)
 *   004061f5  MOV  ECX,dword ptr [ESP + 0xc]   ; ECX = nEntryCount (arg2)
 *   004061f9  MOV  EDX,dword ptr [ESP + 0x10]  ; EDX = pEntries    (arg3)
 *   004061fd  MOV  EAX,ECX                     ; EAX = pre-decrement counter
 *   004061ff  DEC  ECX
 *   00406200  TEST EAX,EAX
 *   00406202  JZ   0x00406216                  ; count == 0 -> done (no work)
 *   00406204  TEST byte ptr [EDX],0x2          ; flag byte bit 1 (value 2)
 *   00406207  JNZ  0x0040620c                  ; marked -> skip the accumulation
 *   00406209  ADD  dword ptr [EDX + 0xc],EBX   ; acc += nDelta
 *   0040620c  ADD  EDX,0x10                    ; advance to next 16-byte record
 *   0040620f  MOV  EAX,ECX
 *   00406211  DEC  ECX
 *   00406212  TEST EAX,EAX
 *   00406214  JNZ  0x00406204                  ; loop while pre-decrement counter != 0
 *   00406216  POP  EBX
 *   00406217  RET  0xc                        ; __stdcall, callee pops 12 bytes
 *
 * The loop is the classic Ghidra "do-nothing-once" countdown: EAX is loaded with the
 * counter BEFORE each DEC, so exactly nEntryCount iterations execute for any nonzero
 * count and none for zero. Decompiled form matches instruction-for-instruction.
 *
 * The table is a plain byte array walked by pointer, so no element type is implied by
 * the code; the record layout below is what the two accessed offsets establish and is
 * written out explicitly rather than invented from a struct that does not exist in the
 * binary. Flag bit 1 == 2 is the "do not accumulate" mark; the meaning of the bit itself
 * is not recoverable from this leaf alone (no callees, no strings, 2 callers), so it is
 * described behaviorally only.
 */
````

/* ComposeFrameCellsFromStreamRecords @ 0x00406a68
 *
 * Decode one record-type-1 block: a list of cell rectangles.  Each item carries
 * a flags byte, an optional two-byte origin delta, optional two-byte cell
 * extents, and a compressed grid-delta run.  The item is decoded into the
 * active surface, its dirty rectangle is queued when the frame-flush gate is
 * open, and the message queue is pumped so the window stays responsive.
 *
 * Status: done
 *
 * ABI: no arguments, plain cdecl `_ComposeFrameCellsFromStreamRecords`.  The
 * original tail is `RET`, and the only caller (RetryLockedProbeDispatch's asm
 * at 0x00406e8f) calls it with no pushes and consumes AL.
 *
 * Return, in AL only (the caller MOVSXs it):
 *   0  ReadStreamBlockRawOrLzss failed on the raw/stored path
 *   1  block processed (or no block body was present)
 *   2  the message pump saw command 0x82
 *   3  the message pump saw command 0x83 (WM_QUIT)
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * VERIFIED STACK FRAME AND VALUE ALGEBRA
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * At entry ESP = E.  The body is `sub esp,0xc`, then four callee-saved PUSHes,
 * so with S = E - 0x1c:
 *
 *   [S+0x10]  byte   per-item flags
 *   [S+0x14]  dword  timestamp / pump scratch (initialised to 1)
 *   [S+0x18]  dword  per-item cell height (row count)
 *
 * The item decoder starts from the record origin in ESI/EDI.  Before the
 * grid-delta call the six PUSHes are, in order:
 *
 *   ebx, flags&3, esi, edi, ebp, [S+0x18]
 *
 * ComputeCellAddressAndDispatchGridDelta is stdcall/6 dwords, so its first
 * argument is the last push.  Therefore the call is
 *
 *   (rowCount = cellHeight, colCount = cellWidth,
 *    row = originY, column = originX, decoder = flags&3, pStream = cursor)
 *
 * and its return value is the number of stream bytes consumed.  The dirty rect
 * is passed as (mode 0, bottom, right, top, left), i.e. the bottom/right are
 * origin+extent.  This is the same argument order used by the other four
 * BlitRectOrTileGridToPlayerSurface callers.
 *
 * The three locals above are exactly the original's byte/dword slots; there is
 * no hidden argument.  The original object's `void *param` annotation was
 * stale: no instruction reads [E+4].
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * ITEM HEADER (flags byte first)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *   0x04  add a high byte to the X origin
 *   0x08  add a high byte to the Y origin
 *   0x10  add a high byte to the cell width  (colCount)
 *   0x20  add a high byte to the cell height (rowCount)
 *   0x40  use the record-default width/height; the origin deltas are not read
 *   0x80  last item in this block
 *   0x03  grid-delta decoder index (0..3)
 *
 * The low bytes of the X origin, Y origin, width, and height are always
 * present.  When 0x40 is set the three origin/default reads at 0x406b28 and the
 * direct jump to 0x406ba7 skip the four low bytes as well; that is why the
 * escape is not merely "optional high bytes".
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * FRAME TIMING
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * 0x412750 is the timestamp saved by DispatchQueuedMessagesAndStampStartTime.
 * 0x412754 is both the divisor and the incrementing frame counter; it is set
 * to 1 at entry and incremented on every successful return.  The division is
 * 32-bit unsigned (XOR EDX,EDX followed by DIV dword), so uint32_t subtraction
 * and division preserve wraparound.  The divisor cannot be zero on any path
 * that reaches it: the only stores to it are the initial 1, the 0 in the
 * subtype-1 arm immediately before the common increment to 1, and the common
 * increment itself.
 */
````

// DecodeGridSpanIndexStream @ 0x00407a68 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Decodes a grid-span index stream — plain bytes allocate one span record each, and 0x0F-extended forms resolve a VM-base address, a native call, or a synthetic opcode 0x35 into decimal text whose characters then name the span records to allocate — returning 1 at the terminating NUL.
// Status: done
/*
 * SIZE — both derivations agree, 444 bytes.
 *   body_start 0x00407a68, body_end 0x00407c23 (END-INCLUSIVE, the last byte of
 *   the body)  ->  0x00407c23 - 0x00407a68 + 1 = 0x1BC = 444.
 *   Real last instruction: 0x00407c22 `JMP 0x00407bea` = EB C6, two bytes, so it
 *   occupies 0x407c22..0x407c23 and the body's final byte IS 0x407c23.
 *   The next defined function entry is 0x00407c24 (it is a call-target-table
 *   entry, index 22 of the table at 0x41130c), so there is no INT3 padding and
 *   no swallowed near-clone. The 214B figure in re_doc.md row 117 is wrong.
 *
 * SIGNATURE — four stack dwords, `RET 0x10`, so stdcall. Ghidra's stored
 * prototype (ushort, undefined4, int, byte*) matches the four popped bytes; the
 * decompiler's return of the constant 1 is also correct (0x407a84 MOV EAX,1).
 * Frame: SUB ESP,0x104 + PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI. With ESP = E0-0x110 on the body
 * paths, argument N sits at [ESP+0x10+N*4] and every [ESP+0x120] read in the
 * body is a reference to one of those four argument slots, not a fifth.
 *
 * THE STREAM GRAMMAR (all offsets from this function's own disassembly):
 *   ESI walks the stream. The loop head is 0x407c0d:
 *       MOV CL,[ESI] ; TEST ECX,ECX ; JZ exit ; CMP ECX,0xf ; JZ 0x407a95 ;
 *       JMP 0x407bea
 *   * plain byte B (B != 0x0F, B != 0): AllocGridCellSpanRecord(wOffsetY,
 *     pnCellOffsetX, nGridTabIndex, B); ESI advances by one. B is therefore a
 *     reference-record index — text characters ARE the index stream.
 *   * 0x0F escape: 0x407a95 INC ESI (past the 0x0F) -> AL = sub-opcode,
 *     INC ESI -> dwLen = next byte (stored to [ESP+0xc]), INC ESI -> ESI now
 *     sits on the first operand byte. dwLen is the output FIELD WIDTH.
 *
 * SUB-OPCODE SELECTION uses bits 4-6 only (`MOV ECX,EAX; AND ECX,0x70`):
 *   0x20 -> native-call form        0x00 -> base A (@0x4173e4)
 *   0x10 -> base B (@0x4173e8)      anything else -> JMP 0x407c0d
 * The "anything else" arm is NOT a clean skip: ESI already points at the
 * operand byte, so the dispatch loop reads that operand byte as the next
 * record index. Stated as observed, not explained.
 *
 * BASE FORMS compute puTarget = base + displacement, where bit 7 of the
 * sub-opcode selects the width: clear = zero-extended BYTE displacement
 * (0x407af9), set = 32-bit dword displacement (0x407af2, ESI += 4).
 * Then `MOV BL,AL; AND EBX,7; CMP EBX,5; JA` bounds an 8-entry table at
 * 0x411434 of which only 6 entries are reachable:
 *     0 0x407b1a  decimal text of *(signed char *)puTarget
 *     1 0x407b2f  CopyBoundedStringNulPadded(pbText, *(char **)puTarget, dwLen)
 *     2 0x407b44  CopyBoundedStringNulPadded(pbText, (char *)puTarget, dwLen)
 *     3 0x407b58  decimal text of *(int32 *)puTarget
 *     4 0x407b6b  decimal text of **(int32 **)puTarget   (ECX=[EDI]; PUSH [ECX])
 *     5 0x407b80  synthetic VM instruction, see below
 *     6,7 -> 0x4089cc / 0x4089db: OUTSIDE the body and unreachable past the JA.
 * Every radix pushed at these sites is the literal 0xa — decimal, sign only on
 * negative values (see c/ConvertIntegerToString.c). "Width" therefore never
 * comes from the radix: it is dwLen, and it TRUNCATES. 0x407bac writes
 * pbText[dwLen] = 0 after formatting, so a longer rendering is cut short; the
 * NUL-padded string forms stop the emit walk at their first pad byte.
 *
 * CASE 5 is the interesting one. It writes a five-byte VM instruction into the
 * scratch buffer and runs it through the real dispatcher:
 *     MOV byte ptr [ESP+0x10],0x35        pbText[0] = 0x35
 *     MOV ECX,EDI ; SUB ECX,[0x4173e4]    ECX = puTarget - baseA   (rebase)
 *     MOV dword ptr [ESP+0x11],ECX        pbText[1..4] = that offset
 *     MOV byte ptr [ESP+0x15],0x0         pbText[5] = NUL
 *     ... CALL 0x40967c ; PUSH EAX ; CALL 0x40d190
 * Per Appendix A, opcode 0x35 is the "load DWORD from stream + add base"
 * addressing variant (shared handler 0x4097b4 with opcode 36), so this case
 * asks the VM to load the rebased offset from the synthetic instruction,
 * re-add base A, and formats the resulting word in decimal. The 0x35 constant
 * is read straight out of the PUSH/MOV at 0x407b80 — not inferred from the map.
 *
 * NATIVE-CALL FORM (0x407abd) passes NO arguments at all — `XOR ECX,ECX /
 * MOV CL,[ESI] / INC ESI / CALL dword ptr [ECX*4+0x41130c]` — and formats the
 * returned EAX in decimal. The byte index is taken from the stream AFTER
 * dwLen, so the stream layout here is: 0x0F, sub-opcode, dwLen, callIndex.
 *
 * NOTE WORTH CARRYING: after formatting, the 0x20 form executes an
 * unconditional `JMP 0x407c0d` (0x407adb) straight back to the dispatch loop.
 * It does NOT reach the emit walk at 0x407bb5, so the digits this case writes
 * into pbText are not consumed by this function; the next 0x0F base form
 * overwrites them. That is what the bytes say and is reproduced here as-is.
 *
 * EMIT TAIL (0x407bac, shared by all six base cases): pbText[dwLen] = 0, then
 * from index 0 while non-NUL, one AllocGridCellSpanRecord per CHARACTER, the
 * character passed as the reference-record index. pbCellOffsetX is passed by
 * address to the callee, so the running X offset accumulates across every
 * character of every record for the whole stream.
 *
 * GLOBALS TOUCHED — exactly two data addresses, both read-only here:
 *   0x004173e4  VM base pointer A. Loaded as the addressing base at 0x407ae0
 *               and subtracted as the rebase origin at 0x407b87.
 *   0x004173e8  VM base pointer B. Loaded as the addressing base at 0x407ae8.
 *   Both are the same two globals c/DispatchScriptOpcode.c binds into EDI/EBX;
 *   this file uses the sibling's names so the VM base pair is named one way
 *   across the tree. Table bases 0x0041130c (CALL [ECX*4+...], 62-entry native
 *   call-target table) and 0x00411434 (JMP [EBX*4+...], this function's own
 *   8-entry sub-opcode table) are read-only code-relative constants, not data.
 *   0x417218 / 0x41721c / 0x417300 are NOT touched here — they are reached only
 *   inside AllocGridCellSpanRecord.
 *
 * SIGNATURES HONOURED AT THE CALL SITES (read off this body, not from the
 * decompiler's phantom registers):
 *   AllocGridCellSpanRecord is RET 0x10 stdcall, four dwords, and the pushes
 *   are right-to-left: last pushed lands in the first slot. At 0x407bc7 the
 *   order is (char index), (param_3), (&param_2), (param_1) -> so the callee
 *   sees wOffsetY, pnCellOffsetX, nGridTabIndex, nRefRecIndex. The
 *   decompile gets this call site right; it is the 0x20-form's formatting
 *   calls that it renders with phantom extraout_EDX values.
 *   EAX after all three AllocGridCellSpanRecord calls is discarded (the next
 *   instruction reads memory, not a register), hence the void return below.
 *   RestartCurrentGridSpanGroup is RET 0x4 stdcall and its EAX IS used:
 *   0x407a7d MOV ESI,EAX makes ESI the stream cursor.
 */

// DispatchOneBasedCommandToGridRenderMapper @ 0x00408b38 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Maps a 1-based command selector (accepted range 1..11) through an 11-entry absolute JUMP TABLE at
// 0x41149c to one fixed (mapper-select, command-byte) pair and calls SelectAndDispatchGridRenderMappingByCommand,
// forwarding its own 2nd argument as that call's record index; an out-of-range selector falls to the
// shared epilogue at 0x408c11, which returns the caller's untouched (indeterminate) EAX.
// Status: done
//
// ===========================================================================
// CALLING CONVENTION -- from the epilogue bytes, not assumed.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The real last instruction of the body is 0x00408c12  C2 08 00  (RET 0x8), 3 bytes, ending exactly at
// body_end 0x00408c14. See also the shared default epilogue 0x00408c11 POP EBX / 0x00408c12 RET 0x8.
// A `RET imm16` is authoritative: __stdcall with exactly TWO 4-byte argument slots (RET 0x8 pops
// 0x8 = 8 bytes of arguments after the return address). The single `PUSH EBX` at 0x408b38 is balanced
// by a `POP EBX` on every one of the twelve exit paths (eleven case epilogues + the default), so EBX
// is a preserved register, NOT an argument. Ghidra's own signature agrees on the arg count:
// `undefined FUN_00408b38(undefined4 param_1, byte param_2)` -- one dword + one byte, 2 slots.
//
// ===========================================================================
// (a) THE JUMP TABLE -- CONFIRMED, length and every target.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// read_memory(0x41149c, 44 bytes) = 11 little-endian dwords. 44/4 = 11 entries, and the 12th dword
// at 0x4114c8 is 0x00408de9 (a different family), so the table is EXACTLY eleven entries. Full list:
//     idx 0  0x41149c -> 0x00408b50     idx 6  0x4114b0 -> 0x00408ba7
//     idx 1  0x4114a0 -> 0x00408b61     idx 7  0x4114b4 -> 0x00408bb8
//     idx 2  0x4114a4 -> 0x00408b72     idx 8  0x4114b8 -> 0x00408bc9
//     idx 3  0x4114a8 -> 0x00408b83     idx 9  0x4114bc -> 0x00408bdc
//     idx 4  0x4114ac -> 0x00408b94     idx 10 0x4114c0 -> 0x00408bed
//     idx 5  0x4114b0 -> 0x00408ba7 ... (see left)   idx 10 0x4114c4 -> 0x00408bfe
// (raw hex: 50 8b 40 00 / 61 8b 40 00 / 72 8b 40 00 / 83 8b 40 00 / 94 8b 40 00 / a7 8b 40 00 /
//   b8 8b 40 00 / c9 8b 40 00 / dc 8b 40 00 / ed 8b 40 00 / fe 8b 40 00). Each target is the PUSH
// instruction that opens the corresponding case block, in ascending code order == table order.
// THE SELECTOR: 0x408b39 MOV EBX,[ESP+0x8] / 0x408b3d SUB EBX,0x1 / 0x408b40 CMP EBX,0xa /
// 0x408b43 JA 0x00408c11 / 0x408b49 JMP dword ptr [EBX*4 + 0x41149c]. So EBX = ARG1 - 1 and the
// guard accepts EBX in 0..0xa (0..10), i.e. ARG1 in 1..11 INCLUSIVE. The eleven table entries map
// input commands 1 through 11 one-to-one (index = command-1). ARG1 IS A 1-BASED COMMAND/MESSAGE
// SELECTOR. (Corroborated independently: the 12th dword at 0x4114c8, plus the guard's max index, and
// the fact that all 11 targets are strictly increasing addresses in the 0x408b50..0x408bfe band.)
//
// ===========================================================================
// (b) THE ARGUMENT MAP -- worked out push-by-push (the brief's shorthand is imprecise).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Entry frame: E0 = ESP at entry; [E0+0x4] = ARG1, [E0+0x8] = ARG2. After 0x408b38 PUSH EBX, ESP = E0-4.
//   * 0x408b39 reads [ESP+0x8] = [E0+4] = ARG1 (the command selector). Correct at the base frame.
//   * SHARP CORRECTION to the brief: at the base frame [ESP+0x10] is [E0+0xC], which is NOT ARG2.
//     The push instructions that read "[ESP+0x10]" run AFTER the case's FIRST push has already moved
//     ESP down to E0-8, so there [E0-8+0x10] = [E0+8] = ARG2. The operand text matches ARG2 only in
//     that shifted context; the same happens for "[ESP+0x14]" after the SECOND push (E0-0xC+0x14 =

// POP EBX -> E0, RET 0x8). Pushes are right-to-left, so the LAST push is the callee's 1st argument.
//   push order per block:  PUSH <cmd literal>   -> callee ARG3 (bCommand)

//                          PUSH <-1 | -2 | [ESP+0x14]=ARG2> -> callee ARG1 (bMapperSelect)

// BYTE bCommand) consumes only the LOW BYTE of each slot.
// FULL PER-CASE MAP (n = command; rec = low byte of the dispatcher's ARG2):
//   n=1  (0x408b50): PUSH 0x0  ; PUSH [ESP+0x10] ; PUSH -0x1  -> (-1,  rec, 0x00)
//   n=2  (0x408b61): PUSH 0x0  ; PUSH [ESP+0x10] ; PUSH -0x2  -> (-2,  rec, 0x00)
//   n=3  (0x408b72): PUSH 0xe  ; PUSH [ESP+0x10] ; PUSH -0x1  -> (-1,  rec, 0x0e)
//   n=4  (0x408b83): PUSH 0xe  ; PUSH [ESP+0x10] ; PUSH -0x2  -> (-2,  rec, 0x0e)
//   n=5  (0x408b94): PUSH 0xe  ; PUSH [ESP+0x10] ; PUSH [ESP+0x14]=ARG2 -> (rec, rec, 0x0e)  <== FORWARDED
//   n=6  (0x408ba7): PUSH -0x7e; PUSH [ESP+0x10] ; PUSH -0x1  -> (-1,  rec, 0x82)
//   n=7  (0x408bb8): PUSH -0x7e; PUSH [ESP+0x10] ; PUSH -0x2  -> (-2,  rec, 0x82)
//   n=8  (0x408bc9): PUSH -0x7e; PUSH [ESP+0x10] ; PUSH [ESP+0x14]=ARG2 -> (rec, rec, 0x82)  <== FORWARDED
//   n=9  (0x408bdc): PUSH -0x7d; PUSH [ESP+0x10] ; PUSH -0x1  -> (-1,  rec, 0x83)
//   n=10 (0x408bed): PUSH -0x7d; PUSH [ESP+0x10] ; PUSH -0x2  -> (-2,  rec, 0x83)
//   n=11 (0x408bfe): PUSH -0x7d; PUSH [ESP+0x10] ; PUSH [ESP+0x14]=ARG2 -> (rec, rec, 0x83)  <== FORWARDED
// So:
//   * The literal -1 (0xFFFFFFFF, low byte 0xFF) is the callee's FIRST argument bMapperSelect =
//     0xFF = the callee's SELECTOR_BITMAP (its doc's 0xff -> "expand bits" / "classify span" mapper).
//   * The literal -2 (0xFFFFFFFE, low byte 0xFE) is the callee's FIRST argument bMapperSelect =
//     0xFE = the callee's SELECTOR_SENTINEL_FE (the 0xfe-sentinel mapper).
//   * The three cases n=5, n=8, n=11 forward ARG2 into that FIRST slot instead of a literal, so the
//     callee's bMapperSelect becomes the caller's own 2nd argument.
// The brief's reading of -1/-2 as the SECOND-position/record-index argument is INCORRECT: the record
// index forwarded to the callee is ALWAYS the dispatcher's ARG2 (the middle push), for all 11 cases.
// -1/-2 land in the callee's FIRST slot, bMapperSelect. (And "[ESP+0x14]" is not a distinct value --
// it is the same ARG2, read again after the second push shifted ESP.)
// THIRD-ARGUMENT command values 0x00 and 0x0e: in the callee, bCommand 0x0e takes its GATE B path;
// bCommand 0x00 is neither 0x82 nor 0x83 nor 0x0e, so it takes the callee's DEFAULT path (no bitmap
// gate -- dispatch straight on bMapperSelect); 0x82/0x83 take the callee's GATE A path.
//
// ===========================================================================
// (c) THE THREE-SHAPE PATTERN -- REAL.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Grouping by the FIRST-pushed literal (the callee's bCommand):
//     0x00 : table idx 0,1        (commands 1,2)   -> TWO cases   (variants: -1, -2)
//     0x0e : table idx 2,3,4      (commands 3,4,5) -> THREE cases (variants: -1, -2, forwarded-ARG2)
//     0x82 : table idx 5,6,7      (commands 6,7,8) -> THREE cases (variants: -1, -2, forwarded-ARG2)
//     0x83 : table idx 8,9,10     (commands 9,10,11)->THREE cases (variants: -1, -2, forwarded-ARG2)
// PROVEN: the command-0x00 group has exactly two cases (there is NO forwarded-ARG2 variant for 0x00);
// the other three commands each have all three variants. The grouping is real and matches the table

// Walks a 2-byte-per-cell source table, uses each cell's low byte as a tile index, tests that
// index's ONE bit in a caller-supplied bitmap, and writes 0x02 into the 1-byte-per-cell grid when
// the bit is SET or 0x00 when it is CLEAR; then runs the grid-marking conductor in mode 0x1.
// Status: done
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// CALLING CONVENTION, from the epilogue bytes (not assumed):
//   0x408774  C2 04 00   RET 0x4  -> the real last instruction, 3 bytes, ending
//                                    exactly at body_end 0x408776.
// A `RET imm16` epilogue is authoritative: the callee pops its own argument,
// so this is __stdcall with exactly ONE 4-byte argument. The body contains
// exactly ONE CALL (to 0x0040841c). Instruction count = 48 (bridge agrees).
//
// THE ARGUMENT IS A POINTER, and [ESP+0x1c] is provably entry arg1:
//   after `SUB ESP,0x8` and four PUSHes (4*4 = 16 bytes), ESP has moved down by
//   0x18. At entry, [ESP]=retaddr, [ESP+4]=arg1. So [ESP+0x1c] = (entry_ESP-0x18)
//   + 0x1c = entry_ESP + 4 = ARG1. The body loads it into EBP (0x40872c) and
//   indexes it as a BYTE ARRAY at [EAX + EBP] (0x408730), so arg1 is a pointer
//   to a byte buffer: the caller's bitmap. Named pBitmap below.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// THE BITMAP-BIT MAPPING (the load-bearing core):
//   0x408713  MOVZX ESI,byte ptr [EDI]   <- the source cell's LOW byte = TILE INDEX (0..255)
//   0x408716  MOV EDX,0x1
//   0x40871b  MOV ECX,ESI
//   0x40871d  AND ECX,0x7
//   0x408723  SHL EDX,CL                 <- EDX = 1 << (tile_index & 7)  = the single-bit mask
//   0x408725  XOR ECX,ECX
//   0x408727  MOV EAX,ESI
//   0x408729  SAR EAX,0x3                <- EAX = tile_index >> 3            = BYTE index
//   0x40872c  MOV EBP,[ESP+0x1c]         <- EBP = pBitmap
//   0x408730  MOV CL,byte ptr [EAX+EBP]  <- CL = pBitmap[tile_index >> 3]  (ECX high bits 0)
//   0x408733  AND EDX,ECX                <- isolate the one bit (0, or 1<<(idx&7))
//   So the bit tested is EXACTLY: bit (tile_index mod 8) of pBitmap[tile_index div 8],
//   i.e. the (tile_index)-th bit of the bitmap counting bits LSB-first within each
//   byte. Bit index in the byte = tile_index & 7; byte index = tile_index >> 3.
//
// SAR vs SHR: 0x408729 is SAR (signed). It is behaviourally INERT here because ESI
// was zero-extended (MOVZX, 0x408713) to 0..255, so EAX is a non-negative value and
// SAR EAX,3 == SHR EAX,3 for every reachable index. Signedness does NOT matter.
//
// THE TAIL IDIOM -> THE TWO OUTPUT VALUES (0x408735..0x40873d):
//   0x408735  CMP EDX,0x1
//   0x408738  SBB ECX,ECX
//   0x40873a  AND CL,0xfe      <- 8-BIT AND (opcode 80 E1 FE). CL cannot become 0x100.
//   0x40873d  ADD ECX,0x2      <- 32-BIT ADD (opcode 83 C1 02) on the whole ECX.
//   EDX is either 0 (bit CLEAR) or a single bit 2^k >= 1 (bit SET), so CMP EDX,1
//   sets CF exactly when the bit is CLEAR:
//     bit CLEAR: CF=1 -> SBB ECX,ECX = 0-0-1 = 0xFFFFFFFF. CL becomes
//                0xFF & 0xFE = 0xFE (the AND is 8-bit, so CL = 0xFE, never 0x100);
//                ECX = 0xFFFFFFFE; ADD ECX,2 = 0x100000000 -> truncated to 0x00000000.
//                Stored byte CL = 0x00.
//     bit SET:   CF=0 -> SBB ECX,ECX = 0. CL becomes 0x00 & 0xFE = 0x00;
//                ECX = 0; ADD ECX,2 = 0x00000002. Stored byte CL = 0x02.
//   0x408744  MOV byte ptr [EDX],CL  writes that byte into the destination grid.
//   => bit SET  -> grid byte 0x02
//      bit CLEAR-> grid byte 0x00
//   (The whole idiom works only because the 32-bit ADD carries the 0xFFFFFFFE up to
//   0x100000000 and wraps; the 8-bit AND is what keeps CL from being a wider value.)
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// WALK STRUCTURE (both counters are SPILL LOCALS, not registers):
//   0x4086eb  MOV EAX,[0x004173d4] / 0x4086f0 MOV [ESP+0x10],EAX  <- dest cursor,

//   Source pointer: 0x408700 MOV ECX,[0x417254] / 0x408706 SHL EDX,CL (EDX = row << shift)

//   => [0x00417254] IS a SHIFT COUNT (used as the SHL operand CL): it converts the row
//      index into a source-cell index (the source row is a power-of-two number of cells).
//   => [0x00417250] is the SOURCE TABLE BASE, addressed with a *2 scale: the source cell
//      is 2 bytes wide (a 16-bit word; only its LOW byte is read as the tile index).
//   => The destination is a FLAT BYTE ARRAY walked with INC: 0x408749 INC dword [ESP+0x10]

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

//   base = *(0x417300), c/AllocGridCellSpanRecord.c and c/InstallActiveGridCellRef.c
//   address the same 8-byte-stride table off it. So EDX is *(0x417300), the base.
//   IS 0x417204 A COUNT OR AN INDEX? The bytes make it a COUNT, not an index:
//   it is multiplied by 8 and then 8 is SUBTRACTED, which yields the address of
//   element (count-1). If it were an index, base + index*8 - 8 would be element
//   (index-1) and every loop step would decrement further below it, letting the
//   scan run off the bottom of an array whose size the index never expressed.
//   The reading "count" is the only one that makes the initial pointer the LAST
//   element of a sized array. c/InitializeGridArenaFromMapHeader.c names
//   0x417204 as MAP_HDR_AUX8_ENTRY_CNT ("x8", an 8-byte table's COUNT) -- the
//   same reading, independently.
//   *** NAMING TENSION I CANNOT SETTLE STATICALLY. That same allocator sizes
//   the 0x417300 table from a DIFFERENT count, 0x417200 (MAP_HDR_REF_ENTRY_CNT,
//   allocated at 16 bytes/entry), while this function walks 0x417300 with the
//   0x417204 count at an 8-byte stride. The two counts are adjacent BSS dwords
//   and both read as 0 in the image, so I cannot confirm at load time whether
//   0x417204 really bounds the 0x417300 array or whether the two headers were
//   mapped differently than c/InitializeGridArenaFromMapHeader.c reports. Stated
//   as unresolved; the ROLE (count -> last-element address) is settled, the
//   ARRAY IDENTITY is not.
//
// ===========================================================================
// (b) THE SEARCH AND ITS TERMINATION (the parent got the field offset wrong).
//   The key is read from the ARGUMENT at offset +0xc into ESI:
//     0x40956d MOV ESI,[ECX+0xc]      ; ESI = key, ECX = the argument pointer
//   INITIAL TEST (0x409582): CMP ESI,[EAX+0x4] -- compares the key against the
//   LAST descriptor's dword at +0x4. 0x409585 JNC (jump-if-not-carry = CF==0
//   = UNSIGNED ">=") exits when key >= desc[last].+4, leaving EAX = &desc[last].
//   LOOP BODY, tracked exactly:
//     0x409587 LEA EDX,[EAX+0x4]      ; EDX = EAX + 4
//     0x40958a MOV ECX,0x8
//     0x40958f SUB EDX,ECX            ; EDX = EAX + 4 - 8 = (EAX-8) + 4
//     0x409591 SUB EAX,ECX            ; EAX = EAX - 8      (one record down)
//     0x409593 MOV ECX,[EDX]          ; ECX = *((EAX-8)+4) = desc[EAX].+4
//     0x409595 CMP ECX,ESI
//     0x409597 JA  0x0040958a         ; UNSIGNED ">" : continue while +4 > key
//   *** THE FIELD THAT IS COMPARED IS AT DESCRIPTOR OFFSET +0x4 IN BOTH BRANCHES,
//   NOT +0x0. Because EDX is set to EAX+4 and then 8 is subtracted while EAX
//   itself is also decremented by 8, EDX lands on (new EAX)+4 -- it keeps the
//   +4 offset and follows the cursor down. The parent's reading "reads the
//   descriptor's field at offset 0 through EDX" is REFUTED. The dword at
//   offset +0x0 of a descriptor is NEVER read by this function.
//   PREDICATE, IN WORDS: scanning the array from its highest index DOWNWARD,
//   return the FIRST descriptor whose dword at +0x4 is <= the key (unsigned).
//   For an array sorted ASCENDING by +0x4 this is the PREDECESSOR / floor --
//   the greatest element not above the key -- NOT a lower_bound (a lower_bound
//   would return the first element >= the key, which this is not). The parent's
//   high-level claim ("lower-bound or predecessor", "stops at the first record
//   whose field is not greater than the key") is CORRECT in the predecessor/floor
//   sense; the parent's "+0" detail is wrong. If the array is NOT sorted the
//   function still terminates on the same rule (first-from-top with +4 <= key),
//   so sortedness is ASSUMED for the "predecessor" name and not proven by these
//   18 instructions.
//   BOTH BRANCHES ARE UNSIGNED: JNC is CF==0 after CMP (unsigned >=) and JA is
//   CF==0 && ZF==0 (unsigned >). Consequence: the fields and the key are ordered
//   by UNSIGNED magnitude, so any dword with bit 31 set (a pointer >= 0x80000000
//   on this 32-bit target, or a negative value) sorts ABOVE every dword below
//   0x80000000. A signed reading would reverse that whole half of the range; it
//   is wrong here.
//
// ===========================================================================
// (c) THE RETURN VALUE - a DESCRIPTOR POINTER IN EAX, pointing AT the found
//   descriptor. There is NO instruction that sets EAX after the cursor is
//   established except the cursor updates themselves (0x40957f ADD, 0x409591
//   SUB); EAX IS the running descriptor address. Therefore:
//     - EARLY EXIT at 0x409585 -> 0x409599 (POP ESI; RET): EAX = &desc[count-1],
//       the LAST descriptor.
//     - LOOP EXIT at 0x409597 fall-through to 0x409599: EAX = &desc[k], where k
//       is the index just decremented to and just tested.
//   WHERE DOES IT POINT RELATIVE TO THE TESTED DESCRIPTOR? DIRECTLY AT IT. The
//   decrement (0x409591 SUB EAX,8) happens BEFORE the field load, and the field
//   load reads (EAX_new)+4 -- the SAME descriptor EAX_new points to. So the
//   returned pointer is &desc[k] where desc[k].+4 is the field that terminated
//   the scan. THERE IS NO OFF-BY-ONE. The parent's expected "one step FURTHER
//   DOWN than the descriptor whose field was tested" is REFUTED -- that apparent
//   off-by-one only exists if one (mistakenly) believes the tested field lives
//   at +0 of the NEXT record down; in truth the tested field is +4 of THIS one.
//   It returns a POINTER (an address), not an index and not a boolean.
//
// ===========================================================================
// (d) THE FIELD LAYOUT - 8-byte descriptors; only +0x4 is read here.
//   Stride is 8 (LEA [.. +ECX*8], SUB by 8). This function reads exactly ONE
//   field per descriptor: the dword at +0x4 (the initial test at 0x409582 and
//   the loop loads at 0x409593 both use +0x4). It reads the caller record's
//   dword at +0xc as the key. So the descriptor is { dword A @+0x0 (NEVER read
//   here), dword KEY @+0x4 }, and the comparison is (caller+0xc) vs (desc+0x4),
//   both unsigned. The parent's split "a key at +0 and a second field at +4"
//   is REFUTED: +0x0 is untouched by this body.
//   CROSS-CHECK against c/InitializeGridSpanCommandStreamRun.c (READ, NOT EDITED):
//   that file computes one descriptor's address as base + arg3*8 off the SAME
//   pointer variable (*0x417300) and states that its consumer (the command-stream
//   interpreter) reads the descriptor's BYTES +1 and +2 as an inclusive character
//   range -- it does NOT describe a +0x4 field. So of the two dwords this function
//   uses, only +0x4 is newly pinned by this body; +0x0's +1/+2 bytes are the
//   interpreter's character bounds. Sibling files c/AllocGridCellSpanRecord.c
//   ({byte +0 bBaseIndex, dword +4 pEntries}) and c/InstallActiveGridCellRef.c
//   ({... dword +4 pRefCell}) both model +0x4 as a DWORD POINTER -- consistent
//   with the caller chain below, which dereferences the returned descriptor's +4
//   as a pointer. Reported, not adjudicated; the file cited was not modified.
//
// ===========================================================================
// (e) THE ARGUMENT AND THE CONVENTION.
//   0x409568 PUSH ESI makes the stack one dword deep, so 0x409569 MOV ECX,[ESP+8]
//   reads the single incoming stack argument ([ESP+4] before the push). Its dword
//   at +0xc is the search key (0x40956d). RET 0x4 (C2 04 00) pops 4 bytes beyond
//   the return address => exactly ONE 32-bit argument, CLEANED BY THE CALLEE:
//   the convention is __stdcall (the caller 0x4095a0 PUSHes the argument and
//   never does ADD ESP after the call, relying on RET 0x4). PUSH ESI is balanced
//   by POP ESI at 0x409599. Zero callees (get_function_callees = {}), zero locals.
//   IS THE ARGUMENT STRUCTURE PRIVATE? NOT PRIVATE. In the one caller (0x4095a0)
//   the SAME pointer is pushed to THREE callees -- this function, 0x40931c, and
//   0x409378 -- so the argument is a shared record, not a throwaway. From the
//   caller the argument is a 16-byte arena SLOT: EBX = *(0x417240) - word[ctx+0xa]*16
//   (0x4095b3..0x4095be). 0x417240 is g_pSlotsTop, the top of the fixed-0x10-stride
//   span-slot chain (c/ReleaseSpanRecordByDepthIndex.c, c/StampGridContextLayerAndPublishDepthSlot.c,
//   c/ProcessPendingGridCellSpanEntry.c). This function only ever touches +0xc of
//   that slot. The slot's +0xc is treated as a POINTER by the siblings (0x40931c
//   does MOV EAX,[EBX+0xc] / MOV EBP,[EAX]; the recovered layout calls it pRefRec),
//   so the "key" is really an address compared as an unsigned integer.
//
// ===========================================================================
// (g) THE CALLER (get_function_callers: exactly ONE, FUN_004095a0 @0x4095a0),
//   described from its bytes only:
//     0x4095a3 MOV EAX,[ESP+0x10]     ; arg1 = this caller's argument
//     0x4095a7 MOVZX ESI,word[EAX+0xa]; ESI = word at arg1+0xa
//     0x4095ab CMP ESI,0xffff / JZ    ; 0xffff => no-op (return)
//     0x4095b3 MOV EBX,[0x417240]     ; EBX = g_pSlotsTop
//     0x4095b9-0x4095be SHL ECX,4 / SUB EBX,ECX   ; EBX = slot = top - idx*16
//     0x4095c0-0x4095c1 PUSH EBX / CALL 0x409568  ; <-- THIS FUNCTION(slot)
//     0x4095c6 MOV EDI,EAX            ; EDI = the returned DESCRIPTOR POINTER
//     ... 0x4095c8 PUSH EBX / CALL 0x40931c        ; AddGridCellSpanToExtentList(slot)
//     ... 0x4095ea OR byte[arg1],0x4               ; conditionally flags arg1
//     0x4095f1-0x4095f5 PUSH EDI / PUSH EBX / PUSH 0x0 / CALL 0x409378
//   So the returned descriptor pointer is kept in EDI and passed as the 3rd
//   (last-pushed) argument to 0x409378(0, slot, descPtr). That callee reads the
//   descriptor's +0x4 as a POINTER (0x40938f MOV EAX,[EDX+4]; 0x409531 MOV ECX,[EDX+4];
//   MOV ECX,[ECX+ESI*4]) and stores the result back into slot+0xc -- i.e. the
//   returned descriptor is used to RE-DERIVE the slot's +0xc reference value.
//   THE SEARCH KEY the caller feeds in is slot+0xc: the slot's current reference
//   pointer (pRefRec) BEFORE that overwrite, read by THIS function at [slot+0xc].
//   PURPOSE, stated honestly: the caller resolves a slot named by a 16-bit index
//   in the live grid context (arg1 = *(0x417218), word +0xa = the cursor Y slot
//   index / 0xffff none) and then locates, by a backward unsigned scan of the
//   +0x4 pointers in the 0x417300 descriptor array, the highest descriptor whose
//   +0x4 does not exceed that slot's reference pointer, and hands it to 0x409378.
//   Whether that is a "which band contains this pointer" lookup I cannot prove
//   from these bytes alone -- the mechanism is settled, the intent is not.
//
// ===========================================================================
// NOTE ON UNSIGNED LOWER BOUND: the loop has NO low-end guard. If every field
// from the last descriptor down through index 0 is still > key, the cursor
// decrements past desc[0] and keeps reading at base-8, base-16, ... The caller
// is evidently expected to guarantee key >= desc[0].+4 (or count == 0); the
// bytes do not defend against it.
//
// Instruction list (18, byte-verified, 53 bytes):
//   0x409568 56              PUSH ESI
//   0x409569 8b 4c 24 08     MOV  ECX,[ESP+0x8]
//   0x40956d 8b 71 0c        MOV  ESI,[ECX+0xc]
//   0x409570 8b 0d 04 72 41 00 MOV ECX,[0x00417204]
//   0x409576 8b 15 00 73 41 00 MOV EDX,[0x00417300]
//   0x40957c 8d 04 ca        LEA  EAX,[EDX+ECX*0x8]
//   0x40957f 83 c0 f8        ADD  EAX,-0x8
//   0x409582 3b 70 04        CMP  ESI,[EAX+0x4]
//   0x409585 73 12           JNC  0x00409599
//   0x409587 8d 50 04        LEA  EDX,[EAX+0x4]
//   0x40958a b9 08 00 00 00  MOV  ECX,0x8
//   0x40958f 29 ca           SUB  EDX,ECX
//   0x409591 29 c8           SUB  EAX,ECX
//   0x409593 8b 0a           MOV  ECX,[EDX]
//   0x409595 3b ce           CMP  ECX,ESI
//   0x409597 77 f1           JA   0x0040958a
//   0x409599 5e              POP  ESI
//   0x40959a c2 04 00        RET  0x4
//   0x40959d cc / 0x40959e cc / 0x40959f cc   INT3 padding (next fn 0x4095a0)

// Body: 100 instructions, 0x00405318..0x004054b4. TRUE SIZE = 413 bytes
//   (0x004054b4 - 0x00405318 + 1). get_function_by_address reports body_end 0x004054b4, which
//   is correct: the epilogue is POP ESI (0x4054b2) / POP EBX (0x4054b3) / RET (0x4054b4), a
//   ONE-byte plain RET, so body_end is that RET's own byte and needs no upward correction.

// InitializeGridSpanCommandStreamRun @ 0x004079a0 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Begins a grid-span command-stream run: it is a re-entrancy guard on the run-active flag, seeds the interpreter cursor and the four grid-context parameters from its own arguments, saves the current grid-context triple, then drives the command-stream interpreter from its start byte 0 and returns the interpreter's result.
// Status: done
/*
 * ============================================================================
 * SIZE - 112 bytes, verified two independent ways.
 *   (a) selectors: body_start 0x004079a0, body_end (inclusive, last byte)
 *       0x00407a0f -> 0x00407a0f - 0x004079a0 + 1 = 0x70 = 112.
 *   (b) byte sum: disassemble_function returns 26 instructions; summing the
 *       successive address deltas gives exactly 112 (see the instruction list
 *       below). The final instruction RET 0x10 (C2 10 00) occupies
 *       0x407a0d..0x407a0f, so the body's last byte IS 0x00407a0f.
 *   The selector CLAIMED 200 = 0x407a68 - 0x4079a0, i.e. entry-to-next-
 *   DEFINED-function-entry distance; the next defined function is
 *   DecodeGridSpanIndexStream @0x407a68 (confirmed via get_function_by_address).
 *   The 88-byte excess is NOT padding: it is a THIRD undefined routine region
 *   at 0x407a10..0x407a67 (see the POCKET lead at the bottom). 200 - 112 = 88.
 *   NOTE FOR THE PARENT: the brief's arithmetic "body_end 0x00407a0d minus
 *   0x004079a0 plus 1 gives 112" is internally inconsistent - 0x407a0d is the
 *   START of the last RET, and 0x407a0d-0x4079a0+1 = 110. The correct last byte
 *   is 0x407a0f, giving 112. The concluded size (112) is right; the stated
 *   endpoint/arithmetic was off by 2.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * THE ARGUMENT MAP - __stdcall, FOUR dword arguments (RET 0x10), derived at
 * EACH read from the live stack pointer.
 *   [ESP] = return address; [ESP+4]=arg1, [ESP+8]=arg2, [ESP+0xc]=arg3,
 *   [ESP+0x10]=arg4 at entry (before any push).
 *   0x4079a9 PUSH [ESP+0x10]  - no push yet, so this reads ARG4 and pushes it as
 *      the single argument to RestartCurrentGridSpanGroup (0x40760c).
 *   0x4079ad CALL 0x40760c    - that callee is __stdcall with RET 0x4 (confirmed
 *      from c/RestartCurrentGridSpanGroup.c: "RET 0x4 = stdcall, one dword
 *      argument"). RET 0x4 pops the return address AND the one argument, so ESP
 *      returns to its ENTRY level. Therefore the reads that follow see the
 *      ORIGINAL entry offsets, NOT shifted-by-4 ones.
 *   0x4079b7 MOV EAX,[ESP+8]  -> ARG2
 *   0x4079c0 MOV EAX,[ESP+4]  -> ARG1
 *   0x4079c9 MOV EAX,[ESP+0xc] -> ARG3
 *   The "trap": IF the restart callee ended in a plain RET (not RET 0x4), ESP
 *   would still be 4 low after the call and these three reads would land on
 *   arg1/arg0/arg2. It does NOT - it is RET 0x4 - so the offsets are the plain
 *   entry offsets and are fully consistent with FOUR stack arguments under a
 *   RET 0x10 that cleans exactly those four dwords.
 *
 *   FINAL ARGUMENT TABLE (read offset -> argument -> destination):
 *     [ESP+0x10] arg4  -> pushed to RestartCurrentGridSpanGroup; its return
 *                         (= the same pointer) is stored to 0x412760 (cursor).
 *     [ESP+0x08] arg2  -> stored to 0x412768 (g_nGridCellOffsetX).
 *     [ESP+0x04] arg1  -> stored to 0x41276c (g_nCellOffsetY).
 *     [ESP+0x0c] arg3  -> stored to 0x412764 (g_nGridTabIndex) AND used as the
 *                         descriptor index: 0x412770 = g_pGridRefTab + arg3*8.
 *   The parent read [ESP+0x10]=ARG4, [ESP+0x8]=ARG2, [ESP+0x4]=ARG1,
 *   [ESP+0xc]=ARG3. CONFIRMED, and the ordering (arg4 read FIRST, before the
 *   call, then arg2/arg1/arg3 after the callee popped its argument) is the whole
 *   point of the trap.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * (b) THE GUARD - a re-entrancy guard, and the two readers agree.
 *   0x4079a0 CMP byte ptr [0x00417802],0x0 / 0x4079a7 JNZ 0x00407a0b (short
 *   `75 62`, +0x62 from 0x4079a9). So when the byte at 0x417802 is NON-zero the
 *   entire body is skipped and the function returns 0 (0x407a0b XOR EAX,EAX /
 *   0x407a0d RET 0x10). 0x417802 is therefore a RUN-ACTIVE flag. The recovered
 *   interpreter c/ProcessGridSpanCommandStream.c reads the SAME byte 0x417802 as
 *   its run-in-progress flag (g_bGridSpanRunActive; command 0x00 toggles it and
 *   the file's header explicitly says caller2 "returns 0 if it is already set").
 *   The two agree: this is the begin-a-run entry that refuses to start a second
 *   run while one is live.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * (c) THE STATE SEEDING - every store, and what 0x417300 is.
 *   0x412760 <- EAX, the value RestartCurrentGridSpanGroup returned, which is
 *     the identity of the pointer pushed in (its arg4). So 0x412760 (the
 *     interpreter's byte cursor g_pStreamCursor) is seeded from ARG4 via the
 *     flush+re-arm callee.

// 0x4085da PUSH EDI = 12 bytes), so the single stack argument lives at

// equality, JZ is taken WHEN EQUAL, so EQUAL keeps ECX==0 -> CL==0 -> 0x408607

//   XOR ECX,ECX / MOV CL, byte ptr [EAX + EBP]  ; CL = bitmap[tileindex >> 3]
//   AND EDX,ECX                 ; EDX = bitmask & bitmapbyte  (0 if bit clear)
//   CMP EDX,0x1                 ; CF is set from THIS compare (against 1, not 0)
//   SBB ECX,ECX                 ; ECX = 0 - CF  ->  0 if bit SET, -1 if CLEAR
//   AND ECX,0x3                 ; ECX = 0 if bit SET, 3 if bit CLEAR
//   MOV byte ptr [EDX],CL       ; store the display byte
// The compare is `CMP EDX,0x1`, NOT against 0: because EDX is a single bit
// (0 or 1<<k), CMP EDX,1 sets CF exactly when the ANDed bit is CLEAR (EDX==0),
// which is what makes SBB produce -1 for the clear case. Against 0 it would
// never set CF. So: bit SET -> output 0, bit CLEAR -> output 3. Both ANDs in
// this body are 32-BIT: `81 e1 07 00 00 00` (AND ECX,0x7) at 0x408855, `23 d1`
// (AND EDX,ECX) at 0x40886b, and `81 e1 03 00 00 00` (AND ECX,0x3) at 0x408872
// (imm32 form 81 /4 id). The output is the LOW byte only (MOV byte ptr).
//
// THE WALK (b):
//   [ESP + 0x10]  flat destination byte cursor, seeded from [0x4173d4], then INC
//                 dword ptr [ESP+0x10] once per cell -- 1 byte per cell.
//   [ESP + 0x14]  outer/row index, seeded 0, INC once per row, CMP vs [0x4171ec].
//   EBX           inner/column counter, XOR EBX,EBX at the top of each row, INC
//                 per cell, CMP vs [0x4171e8] -- which is RE-READ FRESH every
//                 inner iteration (0x408886 MOV ECX,[0x4171e8]; 0x40888c CMP
//                 EBX,ECX), not hoisted.
// Both loops test at the BOTTOM (JL back-edges at 0x40888e and 0x40889e), i.e.
// do/while shape: the body runs at least once even for a non-positive bound.
//   Source pointer: 0x408846 LEA EDI,[ECX + EDX*0x2] with ECX=[0x417250],
//   EDX = (row << CL), CL = [0x417254]. So the source base advances
//   (row << shift)*2 bytes per row, and 0x40887e ADD EDI,0x2 advances 2 bytes
//   per cell. SOURCE IS 16-BIT (2 bytes/cell), DESTINATION IS 8-BIT (1 byte/cell).
//   [0x417254] IS a shift count -- it is applied with SHL and, per
//   c/InitializeGridArenaFromMapHeader.c, it is the log2 axis/bucket width
//   (`MOV dword ptr [0x417254],ECX`, a full DWORD slot). Source row stride in
//   bytes is therefore 2^(shift+1).
//   The MOVZX load is a BYTE load at [EDI], i.e. with the 2-byte little-endian
//   cell word it is the LOW HALF; the high byte [EDI+1] is never touched by this
//   body, so its role is UNDETERMINED here (stated plainly, not guessed).
//
// GLOBALS (cross-checked against c/InitializeGridArenaFromMapHeader.c and
// c/RouteGridPathToTargetCell.c, and against this body's own operands):
//   0x004173d4 gpGridBase        grid cell buffer base (dest cursor seed AND stamp base)
//   0x00417250 g_pCellEntryBase  base of the 2-byte-stride grid-cell table (source)
//   0x00417254 g_dwAxisShift     major-axis shift count (log2 bucket width), DWORD
//   0x004171e8 g_nRowStride      bytes per row; here BOTH the inner count and the stamp stride
//   0x004171ec g_nRowCount       outer row count
//   0x00412c94 g_nStartCol       column  -- READ ONLY in this body
//   0x00412c98 g_nStartRow       row     -- READ ONLY in this body
//
// FINAL STAMP AND MODE (c):
//   0x004088a0 MOV EAX,[0x00412c98]   ; row
//   0x004088a5 IMUL EAX,ECX           ; ECX still holds [0x4171e8] from the last
//                                     ; inner-bound load at 0x408886 (nothing
//                                     ; between 0x408890 and 0x4088a5 writes ECX),
//                                     ; so the row STRIDE is taken from a fresh
//                                     ; load, not an assumed constant.
//   0x004088a8 ADD EAX,[0x4173d4]     ; + grid base
//   0x004088ae MOV ECX,[0x00412c94]   ; column
//   0x004088b4 MOV byte ptr [EAX+ECX],0x2   ; grid[row*stride + col] = 2
//   0x004088b8 PUSH 0x0 / 0x4088ba CALL 0x0040841c  ; conductor, mode byte 0
// This body only READS 0x00412c94 and 0x00412c98 -- it never writes either, so
// the located start coordinate is supplied entirely by callers. The axis roles
// (0x412c94 = column added directly, 0x412c98 = row multiplied by the stride)
// are fixed by the addressing form and agree with both sibling files.
// It returns whatever the conductor left in EAX (untouched through the POPs).
//
// TRUE SIZE, derived both ways, both agreeing on 173 bytes:
//   (a) body_end - body_start + 1 = 0x004088c8 - 0x0040881c + 1 = 0xAD = 173
//   (b) the real last instruction is RET 0x4 at 0x004088c6, C2 04 00, 3 bytes,
//       final byte 0x004088c8: 0x004088c8 - 0x0040881c + 1 = 173

// MarkEmptyGridCellsAdjacentToTypeFourAndLocateTypeTwo @ 0x00408284 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NETWALK)
// Sweeps the width-by-height byte grid, writing 5 into every empty (0) cell that touches a type-4 cell, and returns 1 with the coordinates of a type-2 cell that touches a type-4 cell.
// Status: done
//
// Calling convention: cdecl, NO ARGUMENTS, stack-neutral at the RET.
//   Entry filler "PUSH EAX" reserves the one local byte; the epilogue is
//   "POP EBX / ADD ESP,0x4 / RET", and the "ADD ESP,0x4" discards exactly that
//   filler slot. No caller argument is ever pushed here, so nothing is dropped.
//   get_function_variables reports parameters == [] and one phantom Stack[-0x4]
//   byte, which is the result accumulator below.
//
// Two exits:
//   RET @ 0x004082f5  normal end-of-sweep, returns the accumulator: 5 if the
//                     sweep marked at least one empty cell, otherwise 0.
//   RET @ 0x0040834c  early exit from the type-2 search, returns 1 and has
//                     just stored the hit's (x, y) into the two output globals.
//
// Pure leaf: no CALL instructions. Eight distinct absolute data operands.
//
// Signedness note: the JGE / JL comparisons are on the ECX and EBX loop
// counters, which are indices and never negative, so treating them as signed
// is a faithfulness detail with no behavioural effect. The MOV AL,[ESP+0x4] at
// 0x004082ed does NOT read a caller byte - [ESP+0x4] is the local byte that
// this function's own entry "PUSH EAX" reserved (ESP+0 = return address,
// ESP+4 = that filler slot, the lowest addressable slot given the two PUSHes).
//
// Byte-for-byte twin of FUN_004081b8 (0x004081b8), which is 201 bytes of the
// same code with nine immediate bytes changed: it matches neighbours against
// 6 instead of 4 and marks the empty cell with 4 instead of 5. That sibling is
// a fully defined function, not an undefined clone.

//   0x408350 PUSH EAX                         <- reserves the 4-byte RESULT slot
//   0x408351 PUSH EBX                         <- the only real save; EBX is the row counter
//   0x408356 MOV byte ptr [ESP+0x4],CL        <- result := 0, INTO the PUSH EAX slot
//   ... 0x4083bd POP EBX / 0x4083be ADD ESP,0x4 / 0x4083c1 RET
//   ... 0x408414 POP EBX / 0x408415 ADD ESP,0x4 / 0x408418 RET

// caller's argument. GET /get_function_variables returns parameters: [] and exactly
// one local, a phantom Stack[-0x4] byte -- that is this accumulator. Zero parameters,
// stack-neutral at both RETs (both are C3, plain). This is the ADD-ESP-is-a-filler
// case, confirmed at byte level rather than inferred from the shape.

//   caller-supplied byte.

//               6 is also the value written into the cell, so it doubles as "painted code")

 * @0x417234 is polymorphic: the four indirect call sites dispatch to this function
 * or to 0x403d38 depending on which path the caller took. Any statement of the
 * form "@0x417234 is the pointer to <this function>" is only true until 0x403e27
 * runs. This is also why the cluster is tractable: the two bodies are the same
 * hook-and-dispatch thunk with different pre-dispatch fixups.

 * c/WrapGridAxisCursorsStampCellKeyAndRetireSpans.c unpacks the same caller block
 * as ARG_BYTE1(dw)>>8 = mode byte, ARG_DELTA_X(dw)>>16 = X/minor, ARG_DELTA_Y(dw)>>24
 * = Y/major. Independently, FUN_00403d8c builds that dword at [ESP+0x28] from
 * `dword ptr [EDI]` and rewrites byte 1 in place at 0x4040bf..0x4040cd as
 * `CL = byte1 & 0xf0; DL = EBX & 0xf; CL |= DL; byte1 = CL`. Byte 1 is therefore
 * the mode/handler byte, and bytes 2 and 3 are the two signed axes — exactly the
 * layout the sibling assumes and the layout this body forwards. Both files are
 * consistent with each other and with the caller; I make no correction to
 * WrapGridAxisCursorsStampCellKeyAndRetireSpans.c.
 *
 * GLOBALS TOUCHED — the complete set, one entry:
 *   @0x417230  g_pfnCellOperandHook  function-pointer slot, READ (the indirect
 *               CALL at 0x403d15). Set to 0x00402010 by the caller at 0x403de3;
 *               that binding is a 1-instruction no-op `RET 0x4`. The slot sits two
 *               dwords past the axis-state words @0x417220..0x41722c, which is
 *               why it is easy to mistake for a sixth axis word. It is not one.
 *
 * Bridge notes for the parent (no API bug hit, two shape traps):
 *   - `disassemble_function` returned `instructions` with `address` as a STRING
 *     ("00403d10"), not an int; `hex(i['address'])` raises TypeError. Parse with
 *     int(addr, 16).
 *   - `get_function_by_address` is correct for a NON-function address (clean
 *     error), so the undefined 0x403d38 region is reliably detectable that way.
 */

````text
// ProcessPendingGridCellSpanEntry @ 0x004025d0 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Consumes the table entry still pending on the current grid context: retires the topmost live span slot stamped for this context's current cell, then dispatches that entry's script instruction and re-arms the pending-index guard.
// Status: done
/*
 * 43 instructions, 0x4025d0-0x00402653, plain RET (no stack cleanup, cdecl, no
 * parameters). Ghidra prints `void FUN_004025d0(void)`, and that is correct, not a
 * phantom-parameter artifact: GET /get_function_variables returns
 * `parameters: []`, `locals: []`, `total_locals: 0`. Everything arrives through
 * globals.
 *
 * Decompilation and disassembly agree one-to-one. The one place the decompiler
 * renders readably but the disassembly pins down is the match/release test: the
 * decompiler prints `break` after ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord, and that is right —
 * 0x402613 CALL is followed directly by 0x402618 (the first PUSH of the dispatch
 * argument block), NOT by 0x402647 (the loop increment). So at most ONE slot is
 * released per call, and the release falls straight through into the dispatch.
 *
 * Control flow:
 *
 *   ctx = g_pCurGridCtx                        ; 0x4025d3 MOV EAX,[0x417218]
 *   if (ctx->bPendingIndex == 0xFE) return;    ; 0x4025dc CMP EDI,0xFE / JZ epilogue
 *   pEntry = &g_pStateTable[ctx->bPendingIndex]; ; SHL 4 + ADD [0x417248]
 *
 *   p = g_pSlotsTop;                            ; 0x4025ef  (loop body runs FIRST)
 *   do {
 *       if ((p->bStatusFlags & 0xC1) == 0x81 &&
 *           p->wDepthIndex       == 0xFFFF &&
 *           p->wCellCoord      == ctx->wCellStamp) {
 *           ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord(p);
 *           break;                              ; falls straight into the dispatch
 *       }
 *       p -= 0x10;
 *   } while ((unsigned)p > (unsigned)g_pSlotsBottom);
 *
 *   ExecuteScriptInstruction(... pEntry ...);   ; 0x402618-0x402633
 *   ctx->bPendingIndex = 0xFE; ctx->bDispatchFlag = 0xF0;  ; MOV word [EAX+2],0xF0FE
 *
 * ORDER, which matters and must not be reordered: the release runs BEFORE the
 * dispatch. ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord (c/ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord.c @0x4023bc)
 * publishes the slot's cell span into the global extent list and only then returns
 * the slot to the arena; the dispatch that follows runs script code against the
 * same grid state. Moving the release after the dispatch would let the dispatched
 * opcode observe a slot the release path is midway through publishing, and the
 * extent list is order-sensitive.
 *
 * The guard write 0xF0FE is a single 16-bit store covering two adjacent bytes:
 * low byte 0xFE lands at ctx+2 and re-arms the "nothing pending" sentinel that the
 * entry test just consumed (so a re-entrant call is a cheap no-op), and the high
 * byte 0xF0 lands at ctx+3, the flag byte the dispatch just consumed.
 *
 * The caller (FUN_0040279c, the only one) shows the surrounding protocol: it calls
 * this function FIRST to drain the already-pending entry, and only then, if its own
 * flag is set, advances the LCG at 0x4111c8, picks a new index out of a SEPARATE
 * 0x10-stride table at 0x41724c, stores it into ctx+2 with 0x10 into ctx+3, and
 * dispatches with the cursor at entry+0x04. So this function is the drain/step half
 * of a cursor walk over the grid entry table and the caller is the advance/choose
 * half. Note the two cursors differ: the caller dispatches entry+0x04, this
 * function dispatches entry+0x0C.
 *
 * Both callees are recovered: c/ExecuteScriptInstruction.c @0x402458 and
 * c/ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord.c @0x4023bc.
 */
````

````text
// PublishGridCellSpanByDepthIndexToExtentList @ 0x00409360 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Selects the 0x10-stride span-slot record at depth index nIndex counted back from the top of the global slot chain and hands it to AddGridCellSpanToExtentList, a one-argument indexing thunk over the span-publishing helper.
// Status: done
/*
 * TRUE SIZE: 23 bytes (0x409360..0x409376 inclusive). Two independent measures
 * agree: the last real instruction is RET 0x4 at 0x409374, whose final byte is
 * 0x409376 = the reported body_end, so body_end - body_start + 1 = 0x17 = 23.
 * The selector's "24" over-counts by exactly one byte: 0x409377 holds CC (INT3
 * padding). That single pad byte is the ONLY gap -- there is no orphan code here.
 *
 * R44 PARENT CORRECTION (child's orphan claim REFUTED): this file originally reported an
 * "UNDEFINED NEAR-CLONE at 0x409378" (53 53 56 87 ... vs the real 0x40931c's 53 55 56 87 ...)
 * belonging to no function. That is WRONG. 0x409378 is a fully defined, already-recovered
 * function -- ResolveGridReferenceAndAddCellSpan, body 0x409378..0x409566. The child compared
 * bytes at 0x409378 against 0x40931c (= AddGridCellSpanToExtentList, this function's callee)
 * and read the resulting divergence as a clone; the two are simply different functions. The
 * original evidence was the lookup at 0x409377 returning name=None, which is true but only
 * proves the single INT3 byte is undefined. LESSON: "an address between two functions returns
 * name=None" proves the GAP is padding; it does NOT license a claim about what code sits past
 * the gap. Query the candidate orphan address itself before calling it one.
 *
 * Body, verbatim:
 *   409360  MOV EAX,[0x417240]      ; top of the 0x10-stride slot chain
 *   409365  MOV ECX,[ESP+0x4]       ; the depth index
 *   409369  SHL ECX,0x4             ; index -> byte stride
 *   40936c  SUB EAX,ECX             ; one record per 16 bytes, walked DOWN from top
 *   40936e  PUSH EAX
 *   40936f  CALL 0x40931c           ; AddGridCellSpanToExtentList
 *   409374  RET 0x4                 ; stdcall: pops the depth index itself
 *
 * Address arithmetic is plain 32-bit pointer math on a dword global. It is
 * written here through an intptr_t cast purely so the 64-bit host compiler
 * models the same truncation the PE image performs; no widening is intended.
 */
````

</details>

 * a phantom-parameter artifact: this function genuinely takes no arguments.

 * 0x417218, which the PUSH reads directly.

 * that drops the callee's return value: the callee's result is discarded
 * outright and EAX is loaded with the constant 1 immediately afterwards, so the
 * 1 is a hard-coded success flag, not a pass-through of the callee's value.

 * decompilation:
 *
 *   004023bc PUSH EBX
 *   004023bd MOV  EBX, dword ptr [ESP + 0x8]   ; param_1 (caller stack arg)
 *   004023c1 TEST byte ptr [EBX], 0x80         ; flag byte bit 7
 *   004023c4 JZ   0x004023cc
 *   004023c6 PUSH EBX
 *   004023c7 CALL 0x0040931c                   ; AddGridCellSpanToExtentList
 *   004023cc PUSH EBX
 *   004023cd CALL 0x00404b0c                   ; FreeArenaSlot
 *   004023d2 POP  EBX
 *   004023d3 RET  0x4                          ; stdcall, one dword arg

 * c/FreeArenaSlot.c @0x404b0c), so their signatures are used directly here:
 *
 *   - AddGridCellSpanToExtentList(pRec) converts the record's int16 cell
 *     offsets (+0x08/+0x0A) into a bounding rectangle and hands it to the
 *     global extent list, resolving pRec->pRefRec at +0x0C when the record's
 *     own 0x40 flag says the offsets are reference-relative.  It only makes
 *     sense while the record is still live, which is why it is called BEFORE
 *     the free.
 *   - FreeArenaSlot(pSlot) writes 0 to the record's byte[0], clearing the
 *     arena in-use bit, and may shrink the region.  It is called on BOTH
 *     paths, so the release is unconditional.
 *

 *   bit 7 (0x80)  record carries a grid span that still needs publishing
 *   bit 0 (0x01)  arena in-use (owned by FreeArenaSlot's bookkeeping)
 *
 * The record is one 0x10-byte arena slot (FreeArenaSlot's fixed stride), which
 * is why the same pointer serves as both the grid-span record and the slot.

// Sweeps the 16-byte arena chain for span records belonging to one grid cell, retiring up to two of them (each through its own depth-group release path) and then dispatches that cell's state-table entry through the script VM.
// Status: done
/*
 * 106 instructions, 0x402654-0x0040279b, `RET 0xc` (stdcall, three dword
 * arguments, void return). Ghidra's body_end reads 0x0040279b; the last
 * instruction is the 3-byte `RET imm16` at 0x40279a, which ends at 0x40279d,
 * so this is the documented 3-byte-RET under-report. Size taken from the last
 * instruction's ADDRESS.
 *
 * Decompilation and disassembly agree one-to-one, with exactly ONE place where
 * the decompiler's C is a simplification of the machine code — see the
 * `bFullSweepMode != 1` note below, which is a real difference and is modelled
 * from the disassembly, not the decompilation.
 *
 * Frame: SUB ESP,0xc + PUSH EBX/EBP/ESI/EDI => [ESP+0x20]=param_1,
 * [ESP+0x24]=param_2, [ESP+0x28]=param_3, [ESP+0x18]=wCellKey,
 * [ESP+0x10]=bReleaseCount, [ESP+0x14]=cached pEntry.
 *
 * Control flow, in address order:
 *
 *   pwCell = g_pCellEntryBase
 *          + ((nCellMajor << (g_bCellIndexShift & 0x1f)) + nCellMinor) * 2;
 *   if (byte [pwCell] == 0xFE) return;              ; 0x402674 sentinel no-op
 *   pEntry = &g_pStateTable[byte [pwCell]];          ; 0x402684 SHL 4 + ADD
 *   wCellKey = (nCellMinor & 0xFF) | ((nCellMajor & 0xFF) << 8);
 *                                                 ; 0x4026a3/0x4026ab
 *   for (p = g_pSlotsTop; p > g_pSlotsBottom; p -= 0x10)   ; head 0x4026bc,
 *                                                            laddr 0x402733
 *       if ((p[0] & 0x01) == 0) goto next;         ; not an arena in-use slot
 *       if (p[0] & 0x02) {                         ; GROUPED record
 *           if (word[p+0x06] != wCellKey) goto next;
 *           ReleaseSpanRecordByDepthIndex(word[p+0x0A]);
 *           if (word[p+0x0A] != word[p+0x08])
 *               ReleaseSpanRecordByDepthIndex(word[p+0x08]);
 *           if (p[0] & 0x08) FreeHeapBlock(dword[p+0x0C]);
 *           pLastReleased = p;
 *           ReleaseSameDepthGridCellSpans(p);
 *           FreeArenaSlot(p);
 *           SelectNextActiveSlot(p);
 *           if (bFullSweepMode != 1) goto tail;     ; see note
 *           if (releaseCount != 0)     goto tail;
 *       } else {                                    ; ORPHAN span record
 *           if (bFullSweepMode == 0) goto next;
 *           if (word[p+0x04] != wCellKey) goto next;
 *           if (word[p+0x06] != 0xFFFF)  goto next;
 *           if (p[0] & 0x40)             goto next;
 *           ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord(p);
 *           if (releaseCount != 0) goto tail;
 *       }
 *       releaseCount++;                             ; 0x402726
 *   next:
 *       p -= 0x10;                                  ; 0x40272a
 *   tail:
 *   if (pLastReleased) *(uint16_t*)pwCell = word[pLastReleased+0x02] & 0xF0FF;
 *   ExecuteScriptInstruction(byte[1] of pwCell, nCellMajor, nCellMinor,
 *                            0, 0xFFFF, 0, pEntry, pEntry->pCursorB);

 * easiest thing to get wrong in this body. `INC byte [ESP+0x10]` sits at
 * 0x402726, BELOW both release paths but ABOVE the stride step at 0x40272a,
 * and EVERY non-matching branch (not in-use, wrong cell key, wrong stamp, mode
 * off) targets 0x40272a directly. So a slot that is examined and skipped does
 * not touch the counter. Incrementing it once per iteration would cap the sweep
 * after the second slot LOOKED AT rather than after the second record RELEASED,
 * which for a chain with many foreign records would retire almost nothing.
 * Because the counter is only ever 0 or 1 at a release branch, AT MOST TWO
 * RECORDS ARE RETIRED PER CALL, and that is a hard structural fact rather than a
 * policy.
 *
 * THE CELL KEY IS BYTE-WIDE PER AXIS AND LOW-MINOR / HIGH-MAJOR. Both halves
 * come from full dword stack arguments but are copied with `MOV CL,...`, so
 * each axis is truncated to 8 bits, and the minor axis lands in the LOW byte of
 * the key while the major axis lands in the HIGH byte. Written the other way
 * round the file still compiles and still reads plausibly, so it is pinned to
 * the two instruction addresses above.
 *
 * `bFullSweepMode` HAS THREE DISTINCT VALUES, not two, and this is where the
 * decompiler is wrong. 0x4026b3 is `CMP byte[ESP+0x20],1 / SBB EDI,EDI /

 *     param_1 == 1        full sweep: orphan spans are eligible AND the walk
 *                         continues after the first grouped release (2 total).
 *     param_1 == 0        orphan spans are never considered (0x40276f tests

 * disassembly, which is the authority for the third case.
 *

 * `TEST CL,0x2` here both read BYTE +0x00 of the record. ReleaseSameDepthGridCellSpans

 * therefore guarantees it never publishes. So the two "retire a span without
 * touching the extent list" call sites are NOT equivalent: this one can publish,
 * that one provably cannot. Bit 6 (reference-relative offsets) is exactly
 * inverted between them, which is why they select different records.
 *
 * CONTRADICTION WITH SIBLING FILES, reported loudly. Four siblings
 * (ReleaseSameDepthGridCellSpans.c, ReleaseSpanRecordByDepthIndex.c,
 * ProcessPendingGridCellSpanEntry.c and this one's own callee) all name slot

 * nCellMinor). A packed cell key and a stride count are not the same quantity,
 * so the field name is ambiguous across record flavors.
 *
 * It is reconcilable, and the reconciling evidence is in a sibling: the
 * grouped branch here is selected by byte +0x00 bit 1 SET, whereas
 * ReleaseSameDepthGridCellSpans's own filter `(byte & 0xe3) == 0xe1` requires
 * bit 0x02 CLEAR (0x02 & 0xe3 = 0x02). So that sweep can only ever see the
 * ORPHAN flavor, in which +0x06 really is the unset/depth-stamp word; this
 * function's grouped branch sees the other flavor, in which +0x06 is the cell
 * key. Both files are right about the flavor they touch, and the arena chain
 * holds heterogeneous 16-byte records. The field is a union; no file needs
 * retracting, but callers should stop reading "+0x06" without also testing
 * byte +0x00 bit 1.
 *
 * Confirmed against c/AllocGridCellSpanRecord.c (@0x407588) and against the
 * allocating branch of caller FUN_0040283c, which writes the same packed key
 * into the record it builds for this cell:

 * The PACKING CONCLUSION above is RIGHT and survives: byte +6 = minor (LOW), byte +7 = major
 * (HIGH). What was wrong is the variable LABELS and the call-site gloss:

 *   004023e3 JZ   0x00402431                   ; -> plain RET

 *   004023ee SUB  EAX,EDI
 *   004023f0 MOV  ECX,0x10 / CDQ / IDIV ECX   ; ESI = depth index, in 0x10 strides
 *   004023fa MOV  EBX,[0x00417240]             ; scan cursor = arena top
 *   00402400 MOV  ECX,[0x00417240]
 *   00402406 CMP  ECX,dword ptr [0x00417244]   ; g_pSlotsTop > g_pSlotsBottom ?
 *   0040240c JBE  0x00402431                   ; empty chain -> nothing to sweep

 *   0040240e MOV  CL,byte ptr [EBX]            ; slot status byte
 *   00402410 AND  CL,0xe3
 *   00402413 CMP  CL,0xe1                      ; 0xe0 span stamp + in-use, link clear
 *   00402416 JNZ  0x00402426
 *   00402418 MOVZX ECX,word ptr [EBX + 0x6]    ; zero-extended depth stamp
 *   0040241c CMP  ECX,ESI                      ; same depth as the caller's record?
 *   0040241e JNZ  0x00402426
 *   00402420 PUSH EBX
 *   00402421 CALL 0x004023bc                   ; ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord (recovered)
 *   00402426 ADD  EBX,-0x10                    ; next slot DOWN the chain
 *   00402429 CMP  EBX,dword ptr [0x00417244]   ; sentinel RE-READ every iteration
 *   0040242f JA   0x0040240e
 *   00402431 POP  EDI / POP ESI / POP EBX
 *   00402434 RET  0x4

 * ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord -> FreeArenaSlot can shrink the arena and move that
 * sentinel, so the loop bound is deliberately live. It is modelled that way here.

 * publishes the record's cell span into the global extent list when the record's

 *   byte +0x00  bit 0x01  arena in-use (owned by AcquireNextFreeSlot/FreeArenaSlot)
 *               bits 0xe0  grid-span stamp (AllocGridCellSpanRecord ORs 0xe0 in)
 *   byte +0x03  bit 0x02  "still grouped under a parent span" — cleared here
