````text
 *   00402441 JZ   0x00402454                   ; sentinel -> plain RET
 *   00402443 MOV  ECX, dword ptr [0x00417240]  ; g_pSlotsTop
 *   00402449 SHL  EAX, 0x4
 *   0040244c SUB  ECX, EAX
 *   0040244e PUSH ECX
 *   0040244f CALL 0x004023bc                   ; ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord
 *   00402454 RET  0x4
 *
 * THE INVERSE OF ReleaseSameDepthGridCellSpans (c/ReleaseSameDepthGridCellSpans.c
 * @0x4023d8). That function COMPUTES the index — `MOV EAX,[0x417240] / SUB
 * EAX,EDI / MOV ECX,0x10 / CDQ / IDIV ECX`, i.e. (g_pSlotsTop - pRec)/16 — and
 * this function RESOLVES it back to an address with the exact inverse
 * arithmetic, `(g_pSlotsTop - index*16)`. I disassembled 0x4023d8 live to confirm
 * that IDIV rather than trusting the sibling's header comment. So the
 * subsystem's secondary key on a span record is this depth index, not a
 * byte offset, and the two functions are its only two directions of use.
 *
 * WHY 0xFFFF IS A SENTINEL RATHER THAN AN INDEX: the index is a small
 * non-negative stride count, so 0xFFFF cannot be one. The caller's 0xFFFF guard
 * is the same shape as the guard byte in ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord's siblings,
 * and it must be tested BEFORE the SHL: index 0xFFFF would otherwise address
 * 64 KiB below the arena top, far outside the region.
 *
 * THE CALLER (FUN_00402654, the only one — get_function_callers returns
 * count=1, total=1) shows what the index actually carries. It walks the same
 * arena chain and, for a record whose byte+3 bit 1 is set, makes two calls:
 *
 *   FUN_00402438((uint)*(ushort *)(pSpanRec + 10));
 *   if (*(ushort *)(pSpanRec + 10) != *(ushort *)(pSpanRec + 8))
 *       FUN_00402438((uint)*(ushort *)(pSpanRec + 8));
 *
 * i.e. it releases the two WORD fields at +0x08 and +0x0A of the record,
 * de-duplicating when they are equal — a record that references the same depth
 * index twice must not be released twice, and ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord is
 * unconditional (it always calls FreeArenaSlot). So a record here carries a
 * pair of recorded depth indices, at least one of which may be the 0xFFFF
 * "none" sentinel, and this function is how each one is retired. Note the
 * caller frees neither itself nor its record here; it goes on to
 * ReleaseSameDepthGridCellSpans, FreeArenaSlot, SelectNextActiveSlot.
 *
 * CONTRADICTION WITH c/ProcessPendingGridCellSpanEntry.c, reported loudly: that
 * file models slot word +0x06 as `wTagStamp` and requires it to EQUAL 0xFFFF to
 * treat a record as a release candidate. This file's evidence says +0x06 is the
 * DEPTH INDEX, and that 0xFFFF there is the unset/none marker rather than a tag
 * value to match on — because ReleaseSameDepthGridCellSpans compares +0x06
 * (zero-extended, MOVZX at 0x402418) against a derived stride count that can
 * never reach 0xFFFF, and because this function uses 0xFFFF as its own "no such
 * index" sentinel. The two readings are reconcilable (a record with +0x06 ==
 * 0xFFFF is one that was never stamped into a depth group, which is exactly
 * what that caller wants to sweep) but the sibling's field NAME, "tag stamp",
 * is misleading and should be renamed to wDepthIndex. Its header comment also
 * still claims address 0x004025d0 while its body describes 0x4025d0 correctly,
 * and the delegation brief that assigned me 0x4023bc for this sibling file is
 * wrong twice over: 0x4023bc is ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord, and
 * ProcessPendingGridCellSpanEntry is 0x4025d0.
 *
 * The bridge AGREES with the doc row's callee: get_function_callees returns
 * exactly one entry, ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord @004023bc, count=1, total=1.
 *
 * This function dereferences NOTHING — it only computes the address. The struct
 * below exists to give the released address a type and to document the record;
 * no field of it is read here.
 */
````

````text
// ReleaseTopGridCellSpans @ 0x00407624 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Unwinds nSpanCount grid-cell span records off the top of the pending-span stack: each iteration rolls the running X offset back by the popped record's reference span and then hands the record to ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord, which republishes the cell to the extent list and always returns the 16-byte slot to the arena.
// Status: done
/*
 * Disassembly (21 instructions, 0x407624-0x407660, RET 0x4 = stdcall, one dword
 * argument), one-to-one with the decompilation:
 *
 *   00407624 PUSH EBX / PUSH ESI / PUSH EDI
 *   00407627 MOV  EDI,dword ptr [ESP + 0x10]   ; param_1 = nSpanCount
 * loop:
 *   0040762b DEC  dword ptr [0x00412c70]      ; g_nGridSpanStackDepth-- FIRST
 *   00407631 MOV  ECX,dword ptr [0x00412c70]
 *   00407637 MOV  EBX,dword ptr [ECX*0x4+0x412874]   ; pRec = stack[depth]
 *   0040763e MOV  ESI,dword ptr [EBX + 0xc]    ; pRefRec (record +0x0C)
 *   00407641 MOV  ECX,dword ptr [ESI]          ; MOVZX word -> wSrcX
 *   00407643 MOVZX ECX,word ptr [ECX]
 *   00407646 MOVSX EDX,word ptr [ESI + 0x4]   ; signed baseline iBaseX
 *   0040764a SUB   ECX,EDX                    ; uSpan = wSrcX - iBaseX
 *   0040764c SUB   dword ptr [0x00412768],ECX ; roll running X offset back
 *   00407652 PUSH EBX
 *   00407653 CALL  0x004023bc                 ; ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord
 *   00407658 DEC   EDI / JNZ loop             ; post-decrement, no zero pre-test
 *   0040765b POP EDI / POP ESI / POP EBX
 *   0040765e RET  0x4
 *
 * Return value: there is NONE. Unlike the indirect-callee shims elsewhere in
 * this program, this tail is a direct CALL whose EAX is never read afterwards
 * and is clobbered by the following DEC/JNZ path, so the decompiler's `void`
 * is correct here and is not the "dropped return value" trap. The caller's
 * `MOV AL,0x1` at 0x4076f7 supplies its own result.
 *
 * Loop shape: this is a DO-WHILE. The count is decremented and tested AFTER the
 * body, so nSpanCount == 0 would run one iteration and under-run the stack.
 * Both call sites guard with `CMP dword ptr [0x00412c70],0x0 / JZ` first, so
 * the precondition holds; it is modelled faithfully below rather than as a
 * pre-tested loop.
 *
 * Ordering constraint inside the body, which is why the offset rollback sits
 * before the call: ReleaseGridCellSpanRecord frees the slot unconditionally, so
 * the reference record and its span must be read out of the record while it is
 * still live. This mirrors the publish-before-free order inside that callee.
 *
 * Global roles:
 *   0x412c70  g_nGridSpanStackDepth — count of span records currently pushed
 *             onto the pending-span stack. Both callers test it against 0 and
 *             pass it straight in as the count, so it is a live count, not a
 *             pointer; opcode 0x0f resets it to 0 after pushing a group.
 *   0x412874  g_apGridSpanStack — base of the 4-byte-stride array of record
 *             pointers, indexed by the decremented depth (LIFO). The push side
 *             is in the caller FUN_00407664 at 0x407947:
 *             `*(byte **)(&DAT_00412874 + (int)pbVar3 * 4) = pbVar7;`
 *             paired with `DAT_00412c70 = DAT_00412c70 + 1`.
 *   0x412768  g_nGridCellOffsetX — the running X offset accumulator. AllocGridCellSpanRecord
 *             takes `&DAT_00412768` as its in/out offset parameter and ends with
 *             `*pnCellOffsetX += (pRef->wSrcX - pRef->iBaseX)`. This function
 *             subtracts the identical expression, so it is the exact inverse of
 *             that advance: popping a record un-does the offset movement it
 *             caused when it was pushed. That is the "what it writes into the
 *             record" answer for this function — it writes nothing into the
 *             record at all, it only reads +0x0C out of it.
 *
 * Reference record shape (ESI, 8 bytes) — the same GridRefEntry consumed by
 * AllocGridCellSpanRecord and AddGridCellSpanToExtentList: a POINTER at +0x00
 * to the {source X, source Y} word pair (the span is read by dereferencing it a
 * second time, `MOV ECX,[ESI]` then `MOVZX ECX,WORD PTR [ECX]` at 0x407641 and
 * 0x407643), and an int16 baseline at +0x04 read sign-extended. Reading the
 * word straight out of +0x00 would use the pointer's low 16 bits as the span —
 * exactly the failure the sibling AllocGridCellSpanRecord.c documents.
 */
````

````text
// ResolveGridReferenceAndAddCellSpan @ 0x00409378 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Resolves the grid cell's reference record for the current VM opcode mode (a direct reference, or an indexed entry of a nine-slot selection table driven by the opcode byte @0x4177f6 and the operand-state globals), sets the record's source-relative / baseline-relative flag bits, optionally computes the scaled grid offset, and registers the resulting cell span with the extent list.
// Status: done
/*
 * Evidence: decompilation and disassembly (body 0x00409378..0x00409566, 128
 * instructions, RET 0x0C => 3 stack args) agree instruction-for-instruction.
 * No `reliability`/`body_degenerate` field is reported and the stored body is
 * real code (128 insns vs. the 1-instruction stub the flag would indicate).
 *
 * Stack argument mapping (Ghidra params, after PUSH EBX / PUSH ESI so ESP-8):
 *   param_1 -> original [ESP+4]  = byte    bRefRelative  (post-push [ESP+0xC])
 *   param_2 -> original [ESP+8]  = EBX                 (post-push [ESP+0x10])
 *   param_3 -> original [ESP+0xC]= EDX                 (post-push [ESP+0x14])
 *
 * Flag-bit meanings are not guesses: 0x08/0x10 are exactly the bFlags bits 3
 * and 4 that ComputeScaledGridOffset @0x0040921c tests as "X / Y taken
 * source-relative", and 0x40 is exactly the bFlags bit 6 that
 * AddGridCellSpanToExtentList @0x0040931c tests as "offsets are already in
 * reference-baseline space". Both callees are recovered (see their .c files);
 * the grid record layout below is theirs.
 *
 * Grid record (EBX / param_2), reused verbatim from the two callees:
 *   +0x00 byte    bFlags       bit3 (0x08) X source-relative
 *                             bit4 (0x10) Y source-relative
 *                             bit6 (0x40) offsets already reference-baseline-relative
 *   +0x01 byte    bLerpLevel   cleared here
 *   +0x02 byte    bLerpDivisor untouched here
 *   +0x04 byte    bGridX       written here on the non-relative path
 *   +0x05 byte    bGridY       written here on the non-relative path
 *   +0x06 word    wAnchorIndex untouched here
 *   +0x08 int16   iOffsetX     written by ComputeScaledGridOffset
 *   +0x0A int16   iOffsetY     written by ComputeScaledGridOffset
 *   +0x0C dword   pRefRec      written here (the reference record this cell resolves to)
 *
 * Reference-selection record (EDX / param_3):
 *   +0x00 byte    unused by this function
 *   +0x01 byte    bRefFlags  bit1 (0x02) -> OR grid 0x08
 *                            bit2 (0x04) -> OR grid 0x10
 *                            bit3 (0x08) participates in the index-0 test
 *   +0x02 byte    bRefKind   1 = direct reference: the dword at +4 IS the reference
 *                           record and is stored unindexed
 *                           anything else = +4 is the base of a table of dword
 *                           reference-record pointers, indexed 0..8 (9 slots)
 *   +0x04 dword   pRefEntry  that pointer / table base
 *
 * Globals @0x417220..0x41722c are the bytecode-VM operand-state words written by
 * ExecuteScriptInstruction @0x402458 (0x417220/0x417228 mirror operand B,
 * 0x417224/0x41722c mirror operand A), and the byte @0x4177f6 is that function's
 * bFlag / opcode-mode byte. This function only READS them. They are named here
 * exactly as ExecuteScriptInstruction.c names them so the two files agree.
 *
 * The selection index depends on both the mode byte and a signed comparison of
 * the mirrored operand-state words (CMP ECX,dword / JLE / JGE => signed).

 * comparisons against 0x80 / 0x40 / 0x20 / 0x10 are UNSIGNED. Ghidra renders
````

````text
// RestartCurrentGridSpanGroup @ 0x0040760c (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Flushes the span group still pending on the current grid context record, re-arms that record's pending-link byte so the next flush will sweep it, and hands the caller's instruction-stream cursor straight back so the caller can resume decoding at the same byte.
// Status: done
/*
 * Disassembly (5 instructions, 0x40760c-0x407620, RET 0x4 = stdcall, one dword
 * argument), one-to-one with the decompilation:
 *
 *   0040760c CALL 0x00407ce4             ; ReleaseCurrentContextSpanGroup (recovered r32)
 *   00407611 MOV  EAX,dword ptr [0x417218]  ; RE-READ the global AFTER the call
 *   00407616 OR   byte ptr [EAX+0x3],0x2   ; set the pending-link bit
 *   0040761a MOV  EAX,dword ptr [ESP+0x4]  ; load the caller's argument
 *   0040761e RET  0x4
 *
 * RETURN VALUE — this is NOT the dropped-return shim, and the decompiler is
 * right to print `return param_1`. EAX is clobbered twice: the callee leaves
 * the constant 1 in it, then `OR byte ptr [EAX+3],0x2` keeps the record address
 * in EAX, and only THEN `MOV EAX,[ESP+0x4]` loads the argument. So the value
 * that reaches RET is the caller's own argument, round-tripped unchanged; the
 * callee's 1 is genuinely discarded. `MOV EAX,[ESP+0x4]` is a full dword move,
 * not a byte-sized one, so the identity holds for all 32 bits.
 *
 * Ghidra signature `undefined4 FUN_0040760c(undefined4 param_1)` is correct —
 * one real parameter, `parameters: [param_1]`, `locals: []`. It is stdcall:
 * RET 0x4 pops the one dword argument.
 *
 * The two-pass structure is the point. ReleaseCurrentContextSpanGroup
 * (c/ReleaseCurrentContextSpanGroup.c @0x407ce4) hands g_pCurGridCtx to
 * ReleaseSameDepthGridCellSpans (c/ReleaseSameDepthGridCellSpans.c @0x4023d8),
 * which sweeps every still-pending span record at the same depth index and
 * then RETURNS 1. The 1 is dropped. The second step re-sets the very bit that
 * sweep uses as its trigger, so this function does not merely flush — it
 * flushes and then re-arms, leaving the current context marked as "has a group
 * in progress" for the next release to find.
 *
 * The global is deliberately re-loaded at 0x407611 instead of being cached
 * across the call: the callee walks the arena chain and frees slots, which can
 * move the chain top, so the pointer is refreshed before it is written through.
 *
 * Roles of the globals, stated explicitly:
 *   @0x417218 — pointer to the current grid context record, and the ONLY global
 *     this function touches. The record is itself a 16-byte arena slot: the
 *     sweep derives the record's depth from (g_pSlotsTop - pRec) / 16, which
 *     requires it to sit in the same chain as the span records it sweeps, so
 *     "context" and "span record" share one object type here. Two fields of it
 *     are evidenced by siblings, from opposite sides:
 *       byte +3, bit 0x02 — the pending-link / "group still in progress" flag.
 *         ReleaseSameDepthGridCellSpans TESTS then CLEARS it, and its sweep
 *         filter `(byte & 0xe3) == 0xe1` requires bit 0x02 to be 0, so a record
 *         carrying this bit is exactly a record the next sweep will retire.
 *         THIS FUNCTION IS THE WRITER that sets it.
 *       byte +5 — the context's own layer, copied into every span record that
 *         AllocGridCellSpanRecord (@0x407588) allocates while this context is
 *         current. Not touched here.
 *     Naming note for the parent: three recovered siblings name this one
 *     storage three ways — g_pCurGridCtx (ReleaseCurrentContextSpanGroup.c),
 *     g_pCurGridCtx (AllocGridCellSpanRecord.c), g_pCurGridCtx
 *     (InitializeAxisSpanFromSavedPoint.c, which additionally claims bytes
 *     +6/+7 hold the span start coordinates). All three are the same dword at
 *     0x417218; this file uses g_pCurGridCtx to match the grid family. The
 *     parent should settle on one name.
 *
 * Why the callers need the round trip. Both callers are the ENTRY point of a
 * grid-span run, and both use the returned value as the byte cursor they then
 * walk, which is why the identity return is load-bearing rather than cosmetic:
 *
 *   FUN_004079a0 @0x4079a0 — guards on `if (DAT_00417802 == 0)` ("no run already
 *     in progress"), then at 0x4079a9 PUSHes its own 4th argument, CALLs this
 *     function, and stores EAX into the global cursor @0x412760 at 0x4079b2. It
 *     also caches the other three arguments, the reference-table entry
 *     (0x417300 + nGridTabIndex*8), and the context triple
 *     0x417218/0x41721c/0x417214 into 0x412c80/0x412c88/0x412c84, then calls
 *     FUN_00407664(0) to run the loop. So this function is the "begin a run"
 *     step of an already-idle engine: flush leftovers, re-arm, keep the cursor.
 *
 *   FUN_00407a68 @0x407a68 — no idleness guard; it PUSHes its 4th argument at
 *     0x407a71, CALLs this function, and moves the result into ESI at 0x407a7d.

 *     loop walks opcodes and calls AllocGridCellSpanRecord (@0x407588) once per
 *     emitted cell, returning 1. So here this function is "start a fresh run
 *     and give me back the stream pointer to read from".
 *
 * Corroboration that this is the run STARTER and not the flusher: the END of a
 * run does not come through here. FUN_00407664 (@0x407664), the loop engine
````

````text
// SequenceGridMarkingSweepsUntilMatchAndDispatch @ 0x0040841c (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra program NETWALK.EXE)
// Seeds the target cell with a 6, then repeatedly runs the three grid-marking sweeps in order until one of them finds a type-2 cell, and dispatches on the winning sweep: by mode flag either classify the span or route the located cell to the target.
// Status: done
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Calling convention, from the epilogue bytes (NOT assumed):
//   0x40846f  C2 04 00   RET 0x4   (the bail exit)
//   0x408487  C2 04 00   RET 0x4   (dispatch block 1)
//   0x40849f  C2 04 00   RET 0x4   (dispatch block 2)
//   0x4084b7  C2 04 00   RET 0x4   (dispatch block 3, the real last instruction)
// A `RET imm16` epilogue is authoritative: the callee pops its own arguments,
// so this is __stdcall with ONE 4-byte argument slot. There is no PUSH of any
// register in the prologue -- the function allocates no frame and touches no
// local, so every RET reads [ESP+0x4] as CALLER state, unambiguously.
// Ghidra agrees: get_function_variables reports parameters == [param_1 : char,
// storage Stack[0x4]:1], locals == [], total_locals == 0.
// Three verified call sites, all `PUSH <imm32> / CALL 0x40841c` with no stack
// cleanup afterwards (the callee owns it):
//   0x408503 PUSH 0x1 / 0x408505 CALL 0x40841c
//   0x40855d PUSH 0x0 / 0x40855f CALL 0x40841c
//   0x4085ca PUSH 0x0 / 0x4085cc CALL 0x40841c
// The dword is pushed, but the body only ever reads its LOW BYTE
// (`CMP byte ptr [ESP+0x4],0x0`, opcode 80 7C 24 04, at all three dispatch
// blocks), so the parameter is modelled as a BYTE mode flag.
//
// SIZE, derived twice, both agreeing on 158 bytes:
//   (a) body_end - body_start + 1 = 0x004084b9 - 0x0040841c + 1 = 0x9E = 158
//   (b) the real last instruction is `RET 0x4` at 0x004084b7, three bytes
//       (C2 04 00), so its final byte is 0x004084b9, and
//       0x004084b9 - 0x0040841c + 1 = 158.
// Independent third check: summing the lengths of all 47 instructions (each one
// strictly contiguous with the next, min gap 2, max gap 7, no gaps at all)
// plus the 3-byte final RET gives exactly 158.
//
// WHY A SELECTOR WOULD SAY 160: the next function entry is 0x004084bc
// (get_function_by_address returns FUN_004084bc, body 0x4084bc..0x40850f).
// 0x004084bc - 0x0040841c = 0xA0 = 160. Measuring to the next entry instead of
// to body_end swallows the two INT3 pad bytes at 0x004084ba and 0x004084bb
// (both 0xCC, confirmed by read_memory). The selector's 160 is code (158) plus
// 2 bytes of alignment padding -- an over-statement of the same kind the
// skill warns about. Note also that 0x004084b9, which looks like a stray zero,
// is NOT padding: it is the high byte of the RET 0x4's imm16 at 0x4084b7.
//
// CALLEES (get_function_callees: count 5, all LIVE-named):
//   0x004081b8 MarkZeroCellsAdjacentToSixCellsAndRecordTwo          match 6, stamp 4
//   0x00408284 MarkEmptyGridCellsAdjacentToTypeFourAndLocateTypeTwo match 4, stamp 5
````

````text
 *   (b) real last instruction = RET 0x4 at 0x00407cdf = bytes C2 04 00, so it
 *       occupies 0x407cdf..0x407ce1 and its final byte IS 0x407ce1 = body_end.
 *   read_memory at 0x407cdf confirms the tail: c2 04 00 cc cc | ff 35 18 72 41
 *   — the RET's three bytes, then exactly TWO CC (INT3) pad bytes at
 *   0x407ce2/0x407ce3, then 0x407ce4 (PUSH dword ptr [0x417218] =
 *   ReleaseCurrentContextSpanGroup, already recovered). No orphan code here.

 * byte, so it under-reports by 2; re_doc.md's "68B" is the reach-to-next-entry
 * figure (0x407ce4 - 0x407c7c = 0x68 = 104) and over-reports by 2 for the pad.
 *
 * Body, verbatim (33 instructions, 0x407c7c..0x407cdf):
 *   407c7c  PUSH EBX / PUSH ESI / PUSH EDI          ; arg lands at [ESP+0x10]
 *   407c7f  MOV  EBX,[ESP+0x10]                     ; one DWORD read of the arg slot
 *   407c83  MOV  EDI,[0x417218]                     ; g_pCurGridCtx  (context rec)
 *   407c89  MOV  ECX,[0x417218]                     ; reloaded for the byte access
 *   407c8f  MOV  DL,byte [ECX+5]                    ; ctx->bLayer
 *   407c92  CMP  DL,BL
 *   407c94  JZ   0x407cd7                           ; unchanged -> straight to RET
 *   407c96  MOV  byte [ECX+5],BL                    ; latch the new layer byte

 *   407c9d  CMP  ESI,0xffff / JZ 0x407cb5          ; unset sentinel -> skip X side

 *   407cb2  MOV  byte [ECX+3],BL                    ; stamp the X-side slot

 *   407cb9  CMP  ESI,0xffff / JZ 0x407cd7           ; unset -> skip stamp AND call
 *   407cc1  MOV  EDI,[0x417240] / MOV ECX,ESI / SHL ECX,0x4 / SUB EDI,ECX
 *   407cce  MOV  byte [EDI+3],BL                    ; stamp the Y-side slot
````

````text
// Status: done
/*
 * TRUE SIZE (both derivations agree): body_end 0x00409661 - 0x00409600 + 1 = 98 (0x62).
 * The real last instruction is the 3-byte `RET 0xC` (c2 0c 00) at 0x0040965f, whose
 * final byte is 0x00409661 -- it ends exactly on body_end. 33 instructions, counted
 * off the bridge (disassemble_function count=33). PURE LEAF, no CALL anywhere.
 *
 * THE SELECTOR'S 100 IS AN OVER-COUNT BY EXACTLY 2 PADDING BYTES. re_doc.md row 156
 * records the size as "64B" (= hex 0x64 = 100). 100 = 0x00409664 - 0x00409600, i.e.
 * the distance to the NEXT defined function. read_memory over 0x00409600..0x0040966d
 * shows the tail `... b0 01 5b c2 0c 00 cc cc ff 74 24 04 ...`: after the RET's last
 * byte (0x00409661) come bytes 0x00409662 and 0x00409663 = cc cc (2x INT3 pad), and
 * 0x00409664 is the prologue of FillMemoryWithZeroBytes (confirmed live via
 * get_function_by_address(0x00409664); get_function_by_address(0x00409662) returns
 * "No function found", i.e. the pad belongs to no function). Excess = 2 = the INT3 pair.
 *
 * CALLING CONVENTION (RET 0xC => three dword args, __stdcall) AND ARGUMENT MAP.
 * One PUSH (EBX, 4 bytes) before any arg read, so after the prologue ESP sits 4 below
 * entry and every [ESP+X] maps to entry [ESP+X-4]:
 *   ARG1 = body [ESP+0x08] = entry [ESP+0x4]  -- compared against the slot's +0x0A word
 *   ARG2 = body [ESP+0x0C] = entry [ESP+0x8]  -- compared against the slot's +0x08 word
 *   ARG3 = body [ESP+0x10] = entry [ESP+0xC]  -- a POINTER; its word at +0x0A is the index
 * CONFIRMED against the parent's reading.  Because the slot's +0x08 is named iOffsetX and
 * its +0x0A iOffsetY by every sibling that lays the 16-byte slot out, ARG2 is the point's
 * X and ARG1 is the point's Y.  NOTE the swapped X/Y argument order (first stack arg = Y,
 * second = X): the same reversal c/AcquireGridCellSpanRecordAndRetirePrevious.c documents
 * at its own 2nd/3rd arguments, so it is a house convention here, not a misread.
 *
 * THE INDEX SOURCE (ARG3). MOV EAX,[ESP+0x10] / MOVZX EDX,word [EAX+0xA] -- ARG3 is
 * dereferenced as a pointer and a zero-extended WORD at +0x0A is taken as the index.  A
 * word-at-+0x0A carrying a chain cursor index with 0xFFFF = "none" matches the layout the
 * sibling files give the grid context @0x417218 (c/AcquireGridCellSpanRecordAndRetirePrevious.c:
 * "+0x08 word wCurXIdx ... 0xffff = none / +0x0A word wCurYIdx ... 0xffff = none"), so ARG3
 * is most likely that context and the index is its +0x0A cursor.  This body reads ONLY +0x0A;
 * +0x08 is shown in the struct for context and is not touched here.
 *
 * THE SENTINEL. 0x00409609 CMP EDX,0xFFFF / 0x0040960f JZ 0x00409656 (the FALSE return):
 * an index word of 0xFFFF means "none/empty" and short-circuits to a false result before
 * any record is addressed.  This is the SAME 0xFFFF no-slot sentinel the arena code uses
 * elsewhere -- c/ReleaseSpanRecordByDepthIndex.c calls it "'no such index' sentinel" and the
 * caller guards with it; c/StampGridContextLayerAndPublishDepthSlot.c uses "CMP ESI,0xffff /
 * JZ ... unset sentinel"; the context cursors above are 0xffff = none.  (Reported, not edited.)
 *
 * RECORD RESOLUTION: 16-BYTE SLOTS INDEXED DOWNWARD FROM 0x417240.
 *   0x00409611 MOV EBX,[0x00417240]      ; chain top
 *   0x00409617 MOV EAX,EDX               ; index
 *   0x00409619 SHL EAX,0x4               ; *16
 *   0x0040961c SUB EBX,EAX               ; record = top - index*0x10
 * A DWORD at 0x417240 is dereferenced as a pointer (MOV EBX,[0x417240]) and used as the
 * ORIGIN from which index*0x10 is subtracted, so index 0 resolves to the object AT [0x417240]
 * and larger indices walk toward LOWER addresses: records are 16 bytes and grow downward --
 * unusual, but it is exactly the mechanism c/ReleaseSpanRecordByDepthIndex.c (@0x402438: SHL
 * EAX,0x4 / SUB ECX,EAX), c/ComputeScaledGridOffset.c, c/PublishGridCellSpanByDepthIndexToExtentList.c
 * (@0x409360) and c/StampGridContextLayerAndPublishDepthSlot.c (@0x407c7c) all implement.
 * FROM THIS BODY ALONE 0x417240's role is only "the pointer value used as the descending origin":
 * whether it is conceptually a BASE or an END/top pointer is NOT determinable here -- index 0
 * landing ON it (not one past it) is all this body shows.  The sibling files uniformly NAME it
 * g_pSlotsTop, the chain-top pointer, which is consistent but is their reading, not this body's.
 *
 * THE TEST IS A POINT-IN-RECTANGLE (INSIDE), BORDERS INCLUSIVE.  Two mirrored halves, each a
 * signed 32-bit compare whose fell-through branch is the "still inside" case:
 *   FIRST HALF -- the min corner (both fields sign-extended, MOVSX):
 *     0x0040961e MOVSX EAX,word [EBX+0x8] / CMP EAX,[ESP+0xC] / JG 0x00409656 (FALSE)
 *         => fail if iOffsetX  >  ARG2
 *     0x00409628 MOVSX EAX,word [EBX+0xA] / CMP EAX,[ESP+0x8] / JG 0x00409656 (FALSE)
 *         => fail if iOffsetY  >  ARG1
 *   SECOND HALF -- the far corner (min corner PLUS an extent word, extent zero-extended, MOVZX):
 *     0x00409632 MOVSX EAX,word [EBX+0x8] ; ADD EAX, word[EDX]     ; CMP vs [ESP+0xC] / JL FALSE
 *         => fail if iOffsetX + extentW  <  ARG2
 *     0x00409646 MOVSX EAX,word [EBX+0xA] ; ADD EAX, word[EDX+0x2] ; CMP vs [ESP+0x8] / JGE TRUE
 *         => TRUE  if iOffsetY + extentH  >= ARG1
 * So the function returns TRUE exactly when
 *   iOffsetX <= ARG2 <= iOffsetX + extentW   AND   iOffsetY <= ARG1 <= iOffsetY + extentH,
 * i.e. the point (X=ARG2, Y=ARG1) lies INSIDE the rectangle (both <= comparisons make the borders
 * inclusive).  The truth value is "INSIDE", NOT its opposite: the four outside-guards all jump to
 * the XOR EAX,EAX / RET 0xC FALSE epilogue (0x00409656), and only the final JGE reaches the MOV AL,1
 * TRUE epilogue (0x0040965c).  SIGNEDNESS: the slot's min-corner words are read with MOVSX (SIGNED
 * 16-bit) and the comparisons are the SIGNED conditions JG / JL / JGE, while the two extent words are
 * read with MOVZX (UNSIGNED 16-bit) and then ADDED; the box's min corner is signed and its extent is
 * unsigned.
 *
 * THE POINTER CHAIN AT +0x0C IS DOUBLE-INDIRECTED (correction to the brief, which read it as single):
 *   0x00409636 MOV ECX,[EBX+0x0C]   ; ECX = *(slot+0xC)              -> a descriptor
 *   0x00409639 MOV EDX,[ECX]        ; EDX = *(ECX)                   -> a SECOND pointer
 *   0x0040963b MOVZX ECX,word [EDX]      ; word 0 of that target
 *   0x0040964a MOVZX ECX,word [EDX+0x2]  ; word 2 of that target
 * The slot's +0x0C holds a pointer to a descriptor whose first DWORD is ITSELF a pointer (EDX) to the
 * two-word extent pair.  This is the same shape c/ComputeScaledGridOffset.c gives its GridRefRec
 * ("+0x00 dword -> two consecutive int16 words").  The two words are read as UNSIGNED 16-bit (MOVZX);
 * byte order is the little-endian word order of x86 ([EDX] is the low-addressed word, [EDX+0x2] the
 * next).  That they are a WIDTH/HEIGHT (an extent) is established only FUNCTIONALLY here -- they are
 * added to the min corner to bound the far corner -- so this body proves the box dimension in its own
 * arithmetic but cannot by itself fix the field's game name (the sibling calls the pair "source" X/Y).
 * Whether +0x0C is a "reference record" pointer or an "optional heap block" is an open dispute in the
 * siblings; THIS body uses it strictly as a pointer and never as a heap block.
 */
````

````text
/* FunAxisWrapClone_00403d38 @ 0x00403d38
 *
 * Grid-cell operand hook used by ExecuteOpcodeStream when it installs this
 * clone in the window callback slot.  The body is the sibling of
 * NotifyCellOperandHookAndAllocateGridSpanRecord: hand the address of the
 * caller's four-byte operand block to the observer at window +0x6230, then
 * decode byte 2 and byte 3 as signed minor/major axes, add the two axis
 * offsets, reduce each by its stride with a signed remainder, and dispatch
 * AllocateGridCellSpanRecordAndDispatch(major, minor, block).
 *
 * The final word comparison is against operand-block bytes 2..3 after the
 * observer has run.  It returns 1 when that word is zero, otherwise 0.
 *
 * ABI: __stdcall, one incoming dword, RET 4.  ExecuteOpcodeStream and the
 * window table refer to the undecorated C symbol, so the definition carries an
 * explicit asm label while keeping the stdcall epilogue.
 */
````

````text
 * 81 instructions, 0x402a68..0x402bc2 inclusive (347 bytes of code; end-exclusive
 * 0x402bc3). Ghidra's body_end reads 0x00402bc2, which is the ADDRESS of the last
 * byte, not the end — the epilogue is the 3-byte `RET 0x4` at 0x402bc0, so the
 * documented 3-byte-RET off-by-one applies. Decompilation and disassembly agree
 * one-to-one, all 81 instructions, with no simplification worth naming.
 *
 * stdcall, ONE dword argument (`RET 0x4`), VOID return. EAX is heavily clobbered
 * and nothing is propagated to the caller, so `return;` in the decompilation is
 * honest here (unlike the indirect-call shims the bridge docs warn about).
 * get_function_variables: parameters [param_1 (undefined4, Stack[0x4]:4)],
 * locals []. No phantom slots.
 *
 * Frame: PUSH EBX, PUSH ESI puts the argument at [ESP+0xc], so the caller's four
 * bytes are addressed individually:
 *     [ESP+0xd] = byte 1 = mode byte      (only the HIGH nibble is used, 0x402b6c)
 *     [ESP+0xe] = byte 2 = signed axis delta -> X cursor  @0x417220 (MOVSX)
 *     [ESP+0xf] = byte 3 = signed axis delta -> Y cursor  @0x417224 (MOVSX)
 *
 * THE TWO BLOCKS ARE INDEPENDENT, NOT NESTED. The `JZ 0x402b6c` at 0x402a72
 * lands on the FIRST instruction of block 2, so the mode-byte latch runs even
 * when both deltas are zero, and block 1's work is not a prerequisite for it.
 *
 * Block 1 — move the cursor, stamp the key, retire the cell (0x402a78..0x402b65):
 *
 *   g_vmState_0x417220 = (int8)byte2 + 0x417220 + [0x4171e8]) % [0x4171e8]
 *   g_vmState_0x417224 = (int8)byte3 + 0x417224 + [0x4171ec]) % [0x4171ec]
 *       Both are MOVSX + ADD + ADD + CDQ + IDIV + MOV EDX (0x402a78..0x402aae).
 *       The extra `+ mod` BEFORE the divide is a bias to keep the dividend
 *       non-negative, which is what makes this a true wrapping increment rather
 *       than a C `%` that can return a negative remainder.
 *
 *   bSavedLowNibble = ctx->bStampHigh & 0x0f              (0x402aba, BL)
 *   cellEntry[ (Y' << shift) + X' ] = ctx->wStampWord & 0xf0ff   (0x402ac0..0x402ae2)

 *       first, parked on the stack, the index is computed, then the word is
 *       popped and stored. The mask is `AND CH,0xf0`, i.e. the HIGH byte
 *       (= record byte +3) keeps only its high nibble while byte +2 is copied
 *       verbatim — this is byte-for-byte the same masked WORD store that
 *       ReleaseGridCellSpanRecordsAndDispatchEntry performs in its own epilogue.

 *   ReleaseGridCellSpanRecordsAndDispatchEntry(0, g_vmState_0x417224, g_vmState_0x417220)
 *       0x402ae6 PUSH [0x417220] / 0x402aec PUSH [0x417224] / 0x402af2 PUSH 0.

 *       branch entirely and break after ONE grouped release.

 *   ctx->bCellKeyHigh = (uint8)g_vmState_0x417224     (0x402b08..0x402b14)

 *   cellEntry2 = &base[(Y' << shift) + X']            (0x402b17..0x402b31)
 *   ctx->wStampWord   = *cellEntry2                   (0x402b34..0x402b3d)

 * word around the callee: the masked word is handed to the cell entry, the sweep

 *     +0x03  READ  at 0x402aba; OR-ed back at 0x402b47 (byte store)
 *     +0x06  WRITTEN at 0x402b05 — low byte of the packed cell key
 *     +0x07  WRITTEN at 0x402b14 — high byte of the packed cell key
 *     +0x04, +0x05 and +0x08..+0x0F are NOT touched here.
 * It NEVER reads a span record out of the chain itself: the only arena sweep is
 * the one inside the callee.
 *
 * ROUND-37 CLAIMS, VERIFIED FROM THIS BODY:
 *
 * 1. "cell key packs low byte = minor, high byte = major" — CONFIRMED, from the
 *    PRODUCER side and independently of the callee. Three instructions decide it
 *    and they are pinned here:
 *      0x402ae6 PUSH [0x417220] -> callee arg3 = the callee's nCellMinor
 *      0x402aec PUSH [0x417224] -> callee arg2 = the callee's nCellMajor
 *      0x402b05 MOV byte [EDX+0x6],CL  with CL = byte ptr [0x417220]  -> +6 = minor
 *      0x402b14 MOV byte [EDX+0x7],CL  with CL = byte ptr [0x417224]  -> +7 = major

 *    axis, and the byte written to +7 is the one it treats as its major axis.
 *    This is the third independent confirmation of that packing (the other two
 *    are in c/ReleaseGridCellSpanRecordsAndDispatchEntry.c and in
 *    c/AllocGridCellSpanRecord.c).
 *
 * 2. "the arena is heterogeneous, byte +0x00 bit 1 discriminates two record
 *    flavors" — NOT DIRECTLY TESTABLE HERE, but this body SUPPORTS it with new
 *    evidence rather than settling it. This function WRITES the packed cell key
 *    into +6/+7 of the current context record without ever testing bit 1, i.e.
 *    it produces the GROUPED flavor's layout (where c/ReleaseGridCellSpanRecords
 *    AndDispatchEntry.c says +0x06 is the packed cell key) and not the ORPHAN
 *    flavor's (where the same file says +0x04 is the key and +0x06 is an unset
 *    stamp with 0xFFFF as its sentinel). A record left with 0xFFFF at +6/+7 by

 * 3. "slot +0x06 must never be read without testing byte +0x00 bit 1" — HOLDS, and
 *    this file is the WRITER side of it: it never READS +6, it only overwrites it.
 *    Nothing here contradicts the rule and nothing here is entitled to relax it.
 *
````

````text
// Latches the current input byte into the frame-control struct (clearing the latch on control code 0x0E), then, while the struct is running, bumps the frame counter and refreshes the global frame interval whenever the clamped 1..50 frame divisor changes.
// Status: done

// Recovered from Ghidra decompilation cross-checked against the disassembly:
//   - every global and struct offset below is read straight off the 36-instruction body
//   - the decompiler's `undefined4 in_EAX` is an artifact of the partial AL writes on
//     the return paths (get_function_variables reports no parameters), so the function
//     takes nothing and only AL is meaningful in its result.
//
//   00402bc4  PUSH EBX
//   00402bc5  MOV  EBX,[0x00417378]     ; EBX = frame-control struct pointer
//   00402bcb  MOV  AL,[0x00417800]      ; AL  = current input byte
//   00402bd0  CMP  AL,0x0e              ; control code 14 = "clear the latch"
//   00402bd2  JZ   0x00402be3
//   00402bda  MOV  [ECX+0x3],AL         ; ctl->bCharLatched = input byte
//   00402bdd  MOV  [EBX+0x2],0x1        ; ctl->bCharPending = 1
//   00402be3  XOR  EAX,EAX
//   00402beb  MOV  [ECX+0x2],AL         ; ctl->bCharPending = 0   (clear path)
//   00402bee  MOV  [EBX+0x3],AL         ; ctl->bCharLatched = 0
//   00402bf1  CMP  byte ptr [EBX],0x0   ; ctl->bRunning
//   00402bf4  JNZ  0x00402c27           ;   halted -> return 0
//   00402bf6  INC  dword ptr [EBX+0x4]  ; ctl->dwFrameCount++
//   00402bfb  CMP  byte ptr [EBX+0x1],0x1    ; clamp divisor to a 1 minimum
//   00402c03  CMP  byte ptr [EBX+0x1],0x32   ; ... and a 50 maximum
//   00402c0d  MOV  AL,byte ptr [EBX+0x1]     ; divisor = ctl->bFrameDivisor
//   00402c10  CMP  AL,byte ptr [0x0041727b]  ; changed since last refresh?
//   00402c18  MOV  [0x0041727b],AL           ; cache it
//   00402c1d  PUSH EAX
````

````text
// SetFrameIntervalFromDivisor @ 0x0040c148 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project /NETWALK.EXE)
// Sets the global frame interval to 1000 / divisor milliseconds and always returns TRUE; a zero divisor leaves the interval at 0.
// Status: done
//
// Recovered from Ghidra decompilation cross-checked against the disassembly.
//
//   0040c148  MOV  dword ptr [0x00416f18], 0x0
//   0040c152  CMP  byte ptr [ESP+0x4], 0x0
//   0040c157  JZ   0x0040c16c
//   0040c159  MOV  EAX, 0x3e8          ; 1000
//   0040c15e  XOR  ECX, ECX
//   0040c160  MOV  CL, byte ptr [ESP+0x4]   ; zero-extended divisor
//   0040c164  CDQ                      ; EDX:EAX = 1000 (signed)
//   0040c165  IDIV ECX                 ; EAX = 1000 / divisor
//   0040c167  MOV  [0x00416f18], EAX
//   0040c16c  MOV  AL, 0x1             ; return TRUE
//   0040c16e  RET  0x4                 ; stdcall, callee pops the 1-byte argument
//
// The division guards against a zero divisor, so IDIV cannot fault. Only AL is
// written on the return path, i.e. the meaningful result is the low byte (TRUE).
//
// The stored global is the millisecond budget the main loop in FUN_0040ca54 waits
// on between frames:
//     while (timeGetTime() <= DAT_004170c8 + _DAT_00416f18) { ... }
// so the divisor is a frame-rate divisor: interval_ms = 1000 / fps.
````

````text
// WalkGridSpanChainAndDispatchInputByte @ 0x00403314 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetwalkHermes)
// Walks the descending 16-byte grid-span record chain from the top pointer (0x417240) down to the bottom pointer (0x417244), and for every record whose low tag byte matches the (byte & 0x87) == 0x81 shape it copies two bytes out of a linked record named by the record's +6 word index and then advances that record's cell sub-span; afterwards it feeds the live input byte (0x417800) to the one-byte command-stream interpreter when it is SPACE or CR, or when it is some other byte and this function's own argument is 0x0e.
// Status: done
/*
 * ============================================================================
 * SIZE - 148 bytes, confirmed two independent ways.
 *   (a) selector: body_end - body_start + 1 = 0x004033a7 - 0x00403314 + 1
 *       = 0x00000093 + 1 = 148.
 *   (b) entry-to-next-entry: the function that follows begins at 0x004033a8
 *       (AdvanceActiveGridCellSpanToOffset), so 0x004033a8 - 0x00403314 = 148.
 *       There is NO inter-function padding here (unlike ProcessGridSpanCommandStream,
 *       whose next entry was padded); the two agree exactly.
 *
 *   THE PARENT'S SIZE CLAIM IS HALF RIGHT / HALF WRONG.  The parent asserted
 *   "body_end 0x004033a5 minus 0x00403314 plus 1 gives 148".  0x4033a5 - 0x403314
 *   + 1 = 146, NOT 148.  The parent took 0x4033a5 (the ADDRESS of the second RET
 *   0x4) as body_end, but RET imm16 is a THREE-byte instruction (C2 04 00) that
 *   occupies 0x4033a5..0x4033a7, so the TRUE body_end is 0x004033a7.  The selector
 *   get_function_by_address returns body_end "004033a7", and read_memory at
 *   0x4033a5 returns c2 04 00 53 80 3d ... : the RET's three bytes are c2 04 00,
 *   the next byte (0x4033a8 = 0x53 = PUSH EBX) is the head of
 *   AdvanceActiveGridCellSpanToOffset.  ARITHMETIC: 0x4033a7 - 0x403314 + 1 = 148.
 *   The SIZE 148 is correct; the body_end address the parent stated is wrong by 2.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * THE CHAIN AND ITS DIRECTION - walked DOWNWARD, half-open range (bottom, top].
 *   Entry (0x403314 PUSH EBX ; 0x403315 MOV EBX,[0x417240]) loads EBX with the
 *   value of the TOP global pointer 0x417240.
 *   PRE-TEST (0x40331b..0x403326): MOV EAX,[0x417240] / CMP EAX,[0x417244] /
 *   JBE 0x00403376.  If top <= bottom (unsigned) the WHOLE walk is skipped, so an
 *   empty or single-record chain is handled at the top as well as the bottom.
 *   POST-TEST (0x40336b..0x403374): ADD EBX,-0x10 / CMP EBX,[0x417244] /
 *   JA 0x00403328.  The step is MINUS SIXTEEN, so records are SIXTEEN bytes and
 *   the walk DESCENDS in memory (EBX decreases from the top toward the bottom).
 *   LOOP CONDITION IN WORDS: continue while the record pointer EBX is strictly
 *   ABOVE the bottom sentinel [0x417244]; stop when EBX is at or below it.
 *   RESULTING SET: EBX takes top, top-16, top-32, ... down to the smallest such
 *   value that is still > bottom.  THE BOTTOM RECORD ITSELF IS SKIPPED (excluded):
 *   when the step lands EBX exactly on [0x417244] the JA fails and the loop exits
 *   WITHOUT processing it.  Likewise, when top == bottom nothing is processed.  So
 *   the processed range is the half-open (bottom, top] -- bottom EXCLUSIVE, top
 *   INCLUSIVE.  The guard is a PRE-TEST at the top (0x40331b..0x403326) AND a
 *   POST-TEST at the bottom (0x40336b..0x403374).
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * THE SHAPE TEST AND THE MASK (0x403328...0x40332e).
 *   MOV AL,[EBX] / AND AL,0x87 / CMP AL,0x81 / JNZ 0x0040336b.
 *   0x87 = 1000 0111b keeps bits 0,1,2,7; 0x81 = 1000 0001b wants bit0 and bit7
 *   SET and bit1 and bit2 CLEAR.  Bits 3,4,5,6 are IGNORED (four don't-care bits).
 *   So the tag byte passes iff (b & 0x87) == 0x81, i.e. it is a FOUR-bit pattern
 *   test over bits {7,2,1,0} = 1,0,0,1 with FOUR don't-care bits {3..6}.
 *   THE PARENT CALLED THIS "a two-bit tag test with two don't-care bits" -- that
 *   is WRONG in both counts: FOUR bits are constrained and FOUR are free.  What it
 *   implies: the record's +0x00 byte is a flags/tag field whose bits 0 and 7 carry
 *   a "kind" (both low/high marker bits set) and whose bits 1,2 must be clear,
 *   while its bits 3..6 are free for other flags -- the test selects one record
 *   KIND while tolerating four unrelated flag bits.  On failure the JNZ jumps to
 *   0x0040336b, PAST the PUSH/CALL sequence (see "THE ADVANCE CALL").
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * THE COUNT CONSISTENCY TEST (0x403330..0x40333d).
 *   XOR EAX,EAX / MOV AL,[EBX+1] / INC EAX  -> EAX = (byte at +0x01) + 1
 *   XOR ECX,ECX / MOV CL,[EBX+2]            -> ECX = (byte at +0x02)
 *   CMP EAX,ECX / JNZ 0x00403361.
 *   The copy is entered only when (+0x02) == (+0x01) + 1.  So the two adjacent
 *   byte fields stand in a "+1" rel-at-ion: +0x01 is a ZERO-based index/count and
 *   +0x02 is its ONE-based equivalent (count = index + 1) -- equivalently the
 *   record is only processed while its sub-span cursor sits at the boundary the
 *   check demands.  A mismatch (JNZ 0x00403361) still runs the ADVANCE call but
 *   skips the cross-record copy.  NOTE: this +1 relation is exact for THESE two
 *   bytes as read; the sibling AdvanceGridCellSubSpan.c binds +0x01 = bSubIndex
 *   and +0x02 = bSubCount but tests them differently (wrap is bSubIndex ==
 *   bSubCount), so whether "index+1 == count" is the same condition the sibling
 *   implies is NOT settled here -- stated as bytes, not resolved to a semantic.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * THE CROSS-RECORD COPY AND THE INDEX ARITHMETIC (0x40333f..0x40335e).
 *   CMP word [EBX+6],-1 / JZ 0x00403361   -- if the +0x06 WORD == 0xffff, skip.
 *   MOV EDX,[0x417240]                    -- EDX = the CHAIN TOP pointer
 *   MOVZX EAX,word [EBX+6]                -- EAX = the +0x06 word, zero-extended
 *   SHL EAX,4                             -- EAX *= 16
 *   SUB EDX,EAX                           -- EDX = top - word*16
 *   MOV AL,[EDX+6] / MOV [EBX+4],AL       -- pRec[+4] = link[+6]
 *   MOV AL,[EDX+7] / MOV [EBX+5],AL       -- pRec[+5] = link[+7]
 *   So the +0x06 WORD is an INDEX naming another record, counted FROM THE CHAIN
 *   TOP (the base is the global 0x417240, NOT EBX): index 0 = the top record,
 *   index 1 = top-16, etc.  It is therefore an INDEX-FROM-TOP link field, NOT
 *   self-relative -- the parent's "SELF-RELATIVE or INDEX" is resolved to INDEX
 *   (the code loads [0x417240], not EBX, into the base).  With the word == 0xffff
 *   the copy is skipped; 0xffff is thus the "no linked record / no slot" sentinel,
 *   consistent with the project's recorded 0xffff no-slot sentinel elsewhere.
 *   The two bytes copied are the LOW and HIGH bytes of the LINK record's own
 *   +0x06 word (its +6 and +7), landing in the current record's +0x04 and +0x05.
 *   ACTIVE function name : the target is named AdvanceActiveGridCellSpanToOffset
 *   in Ghidra; the source record's +0x06 word being the same storage the sibling
 *   c/AllocGridCellSpanRecord.c calls g_wGridUserData (copied to record +6) is
 *   UNDETERMINED here -- the bytes show an index, not that it is that user word.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * THE ADVANCE CALL (0x403361..0x403366) - AND THE PARENT'S CLAIM IS WRONG.
 *   0x403361 PUSH EBX / 0x403362 PUSH 0 / 0x403364 PUSH 0 / 0x403366 CALL
 *   0x00402f34.  The FAILURE paths of the count test (0x40333d JNZ 0x00403361) and
 *   of the word sentinel (0x403344 JZ 0x00403361) jump to 0x00403361, as does the
 *   falling-through success path -- so ANY record that PASSES THE SHAPE TEST
 *   reaches the call, matching or not on the count/word sub-tests.
 *   BUT the SHAPE-TEST FAILURE (0x40332e JNZ 0x0040336b) jumps to 0x0040336b,
 *   which is the ADD EBX,-0x10 step, i.e. PAST the whole PUSH/CALL block.
 *   THEREFORE the parent's claim -- "every record that passes OR fails the shape
 *   test reaches PUSH EBX/PUSH 0/PUSH 0/CALL ... the advance happens for EVERY
 *   record in the chain" -- is REFUTED.  The advance call fires ONLY for records
 *   whose low byte matches (b & 0x87) == 0x81; non-matching records are stepped
 *   over without any call.  Verified byte-wise: 0x40332e = 75 3B (JNZ +0x3B from
 *   the end of the instruction at 0x40332e+2 -> 0x40336b), and 0x40336b = the
 *   ADD EBX,-0x10, ten bytes after the push block begins at 0x403361.
 *   ARGUMENT ORDER vs c/AdvanceGridCellSubSpan.c: that file's recovered signature
 *   is AdvanceGridCellSubSpan(uint8_t bReleaseSlot, uint8_t bFinalPass, void *pRec)
 *   with arg1=[ESP+0xc] bReleaseSlot, arg2=[ESP+0x10] bFinalPass, arg3=[ESP+0x14]
 *   pRec.  __stdcall pushes right-to-left, so the LAST push before CALL is arg1:
 *   the site pushes EBX first, then 0, then 0, giving arg1=0 (bReleaseSlot=0, do
 *   NOT release the arena slot), arg2=0 (bFinalPass=0), arg3=EBX (the record).
 *   The last argument IS the record pointer.  MATCHES the recovered file.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * THE POSTURE: THE INPUT-BYTE DISPATCH (0x403376..0x403392).
 *   XOR EAX,EAX / MOV AL,[0x417800]   -> EAX = the LIVE INPUT BYTE global
 *   CMP EAX,0x20 / JZ 0x00403393      -> SPACE  -> interpreter call
 *   CMP EAX,0xd  / JZ 0x00403393      -> CR     -> interpreter call
 *   CMP EAX,0xe  / JZ 0x004033a2      -> 0x0e   -> return-1 tail
 *   CMP byte [ESP+8],0xe / JNZ 0x004033a2
 *                                     -> if the ARG is NOT 0x0e -> return-1 tail;
 *                                        if the ARG IS 0x0e  -> fall to the call
 *   PREDICATE IN WORDS: the command-stream interpreter is called iff
 *       (input == 0x20) OR (input == 0x0d)
 *       OR ( input is NONE of {0x20,0x0d,0x0e} AND this function's argument == 0x0e ).
 *   The byte 0x0e NEVER calls the interpreter on its own (it always returns 1),
 *   and the ARG==0x0e branch is only reached for an input byte that is none of the
 *   three constants.  The ARG is the single stack byte at [ESP+8] (RET 0x4 -> one
 *   argument; the pre-PUSH value is the caller's argument slot).
 *   WHAT IS PASSED: 0x403393 PUSH dword ptr [0x417800] -- a 32-bit LOAD of the
 *   four bytes at 0x417800 (encoding FF 35 00 78 41 00), then CALL 0x00407664.
 *   The interpreter reads only the LOW byte (it does `MOV BL,[ESP+8]`), so the
 *   effective argument is the input byte VALUE -- consistent with
 *   c/ProcessGridSpanCommandStream.c's __stdcall(byte bFirstCommand), one byte,
 *   RET 0x4.  Confirmed: the call site pushes exactly one dword and does no ESP
 *   fix-up afterwards (stdcall).
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * THE RETURN (0x40339e..0x4033a7).
 *   INTERPRETER PATH (0x403399 CALL / 0x40339e POP EBX / 0x40339f RET 0x4):
 *     the CALL's EAX is NOT overwritten before returning -- POP EBX touches only
 *     EBX -- so the interpreter's return value passes straight through in EAX.
 *     The function returns the CALLEE's value on this path.
 *   RETURN-1 TAIL (0x4033a2 MOV AL,1 / 0x4033a4 POP EBX / 0x4033a5 RET 0x4):
 *     sets AL=1.  EAX was cleared by XOR EAX,EAX at 0x403376 and then held only the
 *     zero-extended input byte, so EAX == 1 EXACTLY here (upper bytes 0).
 *   CONTRACT: returns 1 when it does NOT call the interpreter; returns the
 *   command-stream interpreter's result when it does.  Low byte is the meaningful
 *   result (the interpreter's own contract also only fixes the low byte).
 *

 *   get_function_callers(0x403314) = ONE caller, FUN_0040461c @0x40461c.  That
 *   function is the per-frame UPDATE handler: its single caller is FUN_0040ca54
 *   @0x40ca54, which is the game's message+frame loop (its own sole caller is
 *   `entry`; it imports PeekMessageA @[0x401b6c], TranslateMessage @[0x401b70],
````

````text
// DispatchQueuedMessagesAndStampStartTime @ 0x0040c588 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetWalk)
// Drains the whole thread message queue (removing each message), latches the fatal-message global and returns 0x83 if WM_QUIT was seen, then stamps a timeGetTime() start value through the caller's pointer and returns the pending one-byte command latch after clearing it.
// Status: done
//
// Body 0x0040c588..0x0040c613, 42 instructions, TRUE SIZE 140 bytes by both derivations:
//   (1) body_end 0x40c613 - entry 0x40c588 + 1 = 0x8c = 140
//   (2) the last instruction is RET 0x4 at 0x40c611, bytes c2 04 00, 3 bytes, ending
//       exactly on 0x40c613 inclusive. The next byte, 0x40c614, is 0x53 (PUSH EBX) --
//       the prologue of the following function -- so there is no padding tail.
//   read_memory at 0x40c588 for 140 bytes returns exactly these 140 bytes. The parent's
//   selector figure of 140 is CORRECT.
//
// IAT IDENTITY -- established from bytes, not from the bridge's callee list.
// The bridge's get_function_callees for this function returns, in the order it lists them:
//     {DispatchMessageA, PeekMessageA, TranslateMessage, timeGetTime}
// The SET of four names is correct; the ORDER is not the order the calls appear in the body
// (the bridge lists them by something other than program order, and PeekMessageA is called
// twice). Each slot was resolved by reading the little-endian DWORD the IAT entry holds
// (an RVA into IMAGE_IMPORT_BY_NAME), adding the image base 0x400000, skipping the 2-byte
// WORD hint, and reading the NUL-terminated ASCII name. Confirmed twice: once through the
// REST bridge's read_memory, and once by parsing NETWALK.EXE's PE section table directly.
//
//   slot 0x00401b6c -> RVA 0x16f8 -> hint 0 -> "PeekMessageA"     called at 0x40c5a8, 0x40c5ec
//   slot 0x00401b70 -> RVA 0x1708 -> hint 0 -> "TranslateMessage"  called at 0x40c5cf
//   slot 0x00401b74 -> RVA 0x171c -> hint 0 -> "DispatchMessageA"  called at 0x40c5d9
//   slot 0x00401bd8 -> RVA 0x189a -> hint 0 -> "timeGetTime"       called at 0x40c5f6
//
// PARENT CORRECTION -- the peel flag. The task brief says "PM_NOREMOVE is 0x0", which is true,
// but it then leaves the impression that the pushed 0x1 might be PM_NOREMOVE. It is not.
// windows.h defines PM_NOREMOVE 0x0000 and PM_REMOVE 0x0001. The fifth argument pushed here
// is 0x1, so both peeks are PeekMessageA(&msg, NULL, 0, 0, PM_REMOVE) -- messages ARE removed
// from the queue. That is the only self-consistent reading: under PM_NOREMOVE the message
// would stay queued and this drain loop could never terminate. Note this also means the
// existing sibling file c/DispatchQueuedNonInputMessages.c is wrong on two points -- it
// labels the same pushed 0x1 as "Peel flag is 1 (PM_NOREMOVE)", and its comment "nothing is
// consumed by the app's own GetMessage loop" does not hold for PM_REMOVE. (Left unmodified;
//   that file is not this row's to edit.)
//
// LOCAL FRAME. SUB ESP,0x1c reserves 28 bytes. MSG on x86 is exactly 28 bytes
// (HWND hwnd +4, UINT message +4, WPARAM wParam +4, LPARAM lParam +4, DWORD time +4,
// POINT pt +8), so the frame holds exactly one MSG and nothing else. After the five argument
// pushes are consumed by stdcall PeekMessageA, ESP is back at the frame base E, which is why
// LEA EAX,[ESP+0x10] at 0x40c5a3 (taken while the four constant arguments are still on the
// stack, ESP = E-0x10) yields E = &msg. Only MSG.message at +4 is ever read
// (CMP dword ptr [ESP+0x4],0x12); the other 24 bytes are never touched.
//
// CALLER'S ARGUMENT. RET 0x4 means one 4-byte stack argument, sitting at [ESP+0x20] = E+0x1c+4.
// It is dereferenced as a pointer at 0x40c58f (CMP dword ptr [EAX],0) and written through as
// a pointer at 0x40c600 (MOV dword ptr [ECX],EAX), so it is a DWORD* out-parameter. The three
// callers corroborate this: 0x00406c5a pushes the address of the global 0x412750 and
// 0x00406cad pushes LEA EAX,[ESP+0x14] (a local). A caller later computes
// MOV EAX,[ESP+0x14] / SUB EAX,[0x412750], i.e. a current time minus the stored value, which
// is consistent with the out-parameter being a start timestamp.
//
// LOOP SHAPE. The back edge at 0x40c5f4 is JNZ 0x40c5b2 -- it returns to the MESSAGE TEST,
// not to the first PeekMessageA. So the pump is a guarded do/while, not a while(peek):
````

````text
// ClearBufferRegionsFromDescriptor @ 0x00406164 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NETWALK.EXE)
// Walks the caller-supplied buffer-region descriptor backward and zeroes every region it lists, resolving each destination as that region's stored offset added to the global buffer-base pointer at 0x4173e4.
// Status: done
/*
 * 24 instructions, body 0x00406164..0x0040619c, non-degenerate.
 * The Ghidra decompilation and the disassembly agree on every load, every
 * argument and the loop bounds; where they look different it is only because
 * the decompiler rewrote the descending pointer walk as an affine expression.
 *
 * Stack frame (__stdcall, one argument read directly off the stack):
 *
 *   [ESP+0x10] pDescriptor buffer-region descriptor (param_1, int *)
 *
 * Body, with E = the stack pointer at entry:
 *
 *   0x00406164  PUSH EBX / PUSH ESI / PUSH EDI
 *   0x00406167  MOV  EDI,[ESP+0x10]      ; EDI = pDescriptor (arg1, after 3 pushes)
 *   0x0040616b  TEST EDI,EDI
 *   0x0040616d  JZ   0x00406197          ; NULL descriptor: return, nothing cleared
 *   0x0040616f  MOV  ECX,[EDI]           ; ECX = *pDescriptor, the region tally
 *   0x00406171  LEA  EBX,[EDI + ECX*0x8] ; EBX = pDescriptor + 8 * tally
 *   0x00406174  ADD  EBX,0x8             ;       + 8
 *   0x00406177  LEA  ESI,[EDI + 0x8]     ; ESI = pDescriptor + 8, the loop SENTINEL
 *   loop:
 *   0x0040617a  ADD  EBX,-0x8            ; cursor walks DOWN, one 8-byte record per pass
 *   0x0040617d  MOV  ECX,EBX
 *   0x0040617f  SUB  ECX,ESI             ; ECX = cursor - sentinel
 *   0x00406181  MOV  ECX,[ECX + EDI + 0x4]; ECX = *(cursor - 4) = record.dwOffsetFromBase
 *   0x00406185  ADD  ECX,[0x004173e4]    ; ECX = dwOffsetFromBase + g_base_ptr_a = pDst
 *   0x0040618b  PUSH ECX                 ; pushed FIRST -> lands HIGHEST -> ARGUMENT 2
 *   0x0040618c  PUSH dword ptr [EBX]     ; pushed LAST  -> lands LOWEST  -> ARGUMENT 1
 *   0x0040618e  CALL 0x00409664          ; FillMemoryWithZeroBytes(dwByteCount, pDst)
 *   0x00406193  CMP  ESI,EBX             ; do-while: the TEST follows the body
 *   0x00406195  JNZ  loop
 *   0x00406197  POP EDI / POP ESI / POP EBX
 *   0x0040619a  RET  0x4
 *
 * THE ARGUMENT INVERSION, stated explicitly because it is the easy mistake
 * here. FillMemoryWithZeroBytes @0x00409664 (c/FillMemoryWithZeroBytes.c)
 * takes its arguments as (dwCount, pDst) -- the COUNT FIRST -- and then
 * reverses them into FillMemoryWithByte's (pDst, bFill, dwCount) order. In
 * THIS function the count is pushed LAST (0x0040618c, PUSH dword ptr [EBX])
 * and therefore arrives as the callee's FIRST argument, at [ESP+4] of the
 * callee's entry frame; the destination, pushed first at 0x0040618b, arrives
 * as the callee's SECOND argument, at [ESP+8]. Passing them the other way
 * round would hand a byte count to the callee as a destination pointer and
 * write through an arena offset as a length.
 *
 * Because FillMemoryWithZeroBytes ends in RET 0x8 it pops its own two
 * arguments, so the loop's stack stays perfectly flat and there is no ADD ESP
 * inside it. EAX is never read after the CALL, and the function returns
 * nothing.
 *
 * THE DESCRIPTOR LAYOUT, derived from the loads and independently confirmed
 * by the sibling walker FUN_00406080 (c/), which takes the same argument,
 * uses the same 8-byte stride and the same tally header:
 *
 *   +0x00  unsigned long  regionTally     read once, by 0x0040616f
 *   +0x04  record 0     { dwOffsetFromBase, dwByteCount }
 *   +0x0c  record 1     { dwOffsetFromBase, dwByteCount }
 *            ...        one record per 8 bytes, exactly regionTally of them ...
 *
 * Two independent loads pin the field order down and it is NOT the callee's
 * (count, buffer) order: the load at 0x00406181 reaches cursor-4 and the
 * count load at 0x0040618c reaches the cursor itself, so within a record the
 * OFFSET sits 4 bytes BELOW the count. A record's base is pDescriptor + 4 +
 * 8*i, which is the same index the sibling uses for its own record read.
 *
 * ALL regionTally RECORDS ARE WALKED, indices regionTally-1 down to 0, and
 * no more. The loop is a do-while: the CMP at 0x00406193 follows the body, and
 * the cursor enters the loop at pDescriptor + 8*tally, so the first pass reads
 * record index tally-1 and the loop exits when the cursor reaches the sentinel
 * pDescriptor+8 -- which is the base of record index 0. That is tally passes
 * over tally records, with nothing skipped off either end. FUN_00406080
 * confirms the same tally-1 start under an explicit counter (`iVar4 = *pHeader`
 * then `DEC` before use, `while (iVar4 != 0)`), so there is no off-by-one and
 * the leading dword is a plain record count, not a padded one.
 *
 * One consequence worth recording: because the machine loop terminates on
 * POINTER EQUALITY with pDescriptor+8 rather than on a counter, a tally of 0
 * would leave the cursor at pDescriptor+0 and walk backwards off the front of
 * the descriptor forever, reading pDescriptor-4 and below. The C below
 * therefore carries an explicit zero-tally guard the binary does not have; it
 * is a translation guard, marked as such, and not recovered machine behaviour.
 * A tally of exactly 1 is well-defined in the binary and is NOT guarded.
 *
 * NO BYTE IS WRITTEN EXCEPT AS ZERO, AND EVERY BYTE OF A REGION IS WRITTEN.
 * There is no fill value anywhere in this function -- the 0 comes from the
 * callee's own hardcoded fill byte -- and no partial or start-only write: the
 * length handed to the fill is the record's full dwByteCount, so a region of N
 * bytes becomes N zero bytes and nothing outside [pDst, pDst + dwByteCount) is
 * touched. Regions are cleared one at a time in descending index order, and a
 * zero-length region is simply a no-op inside the callee.
 *
 * NO RETURN VALUE AND NO SIDE EFFECTS ON THE DESCRIPTOR. The records are only
 * read; the function never writes back the tally or any record field, so the
 * descriptor survives the call intact and can be walked again -- which is
 * exactly how its single caller uses it (load the regions, then erase them
 * from the same descriptor).
 */
/* stdint.h is included explicitly for uintptr_t: the compile gate is an
 * x86_64 cross-compiler, so a plain `unsigned long` global holding a pointer
 * is 8 bytes wide there and 4 in the real x86 target, which makes every
 * global-relative address emit a spurious -Wint-to-pointer-cast warning.
 * uintptr_t is pointer-width on both, so it models the target faithfully and
 * compiles clean. */
````

````text
// DecompressLzssBlockToBuffer @ 0x00409e48 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NetWalkHermes)
// Expands one LZSS-compressed block into pbDst: a control byte carries 8 flags consumed
//   LSB-first, a set flag copies the next source byte literally, a clear flag replays a
//   16-bit back-reference token whose fields are
//     bits 15..12 = distance  bits 11..8   (SHR BH,4 at 0x00409e7c -- LIVE: EBX is the
//                                           index used at 0x00409e87, so the distance is
//                                           12 bits, NOT the whole word)
//     bits 11..8  = repeat length nibble   (AND AH,0xf at 0x00409e7f; total copies = +3)
//     bits 7..0   = distance  bits 7..0
//   copied byte-by-byte so overlapping runs expand, and the walk stops as soon as the
//   cbSrc source-byte budget is exhausted.
// Status: done
//
// Recovered from FUN_00409e48. Leaf routine: no calls at all, only its own arithmetic and
// byte moves, so there are no unresolved callees to declare. Calling convention is cdecl
// with RET 0xC:
//     [EBP+0x00] return address (naked)
//     [EBP+0x08] cbSrc    ECX  source byte budget / countdown
//     [EBP+0x0C] pbDst    EDI  output cursor (grows forward)
//     [EBP+0x10] pbSrc    ESI  input cursor (grows forward)
// Register use: DL = control byte under test, DH = bits left in that control byte,
// EBX = negated back-reference distance, EAX/AH = back-reference word / repeat counter.
// Bounds behaviour is asymmetric in the original and is reproduced exactly: the control
// byte fetch and the 2-byte back-reference read both test cbSrc and return on underflow,
// but the literal path only decrements cbSrc without testing it.
````

</details>

````text
// FindFirstDriveTypeMatchAndEmitLetter @ 0x0040b264 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NETWALK)
// Scans a 32-entry byte table (the per-drive-letter GetDriveTypeA result table built by
// FUN_0040b2f8, where index 0 = drive 'A' and entry[i] = GetDriveTypeA("A"+i ":\\")) for the
// FIRST entry equal to bDriveType; on a hit it clears that entry (consuming the drive) and
// writes the NUL-terminated drive label "<letter>:" ('A' + index, then ':') into the caller's
// output buffer, returning 1. Returns 0 without writing anything when no entry matches.
// Status: done
//
// Argument / stack map (RET 0xc => exactly THREE caller arguments; there is no fourth):
//   entry  [ESP+0x00] = return address
//   after  PUSH EBX (0x40b264) + PUSH ESI (0x40b265)  => 8-byte base shift:
//   [ESP+0x08] = return address   (NOT an argument; never read as one)
//   [ESP+0x0c] = ARG1  char   bDriveType      -- target type, read via MOV DL,[ESP+0xc]
//   [ESP+0x10] = ARG2  char * pbDriveTypeTable -- 32-byte table, read via MOV ECX/EDX,[ESP+0x10]
//   [ESP+0x14] = ARG3  char * szLabelOut       -- output buffer, read via MOV ESI,[ESP+0x14]
// All three arguments are read; none is unused. Ghidra's own signature agrees, listing three
// params at Stack[0x4]/[0x8]/[0xc] (entry-relative) and the function reports zero callees.
//
// Semantics: EBX is both the loop counter and the byte offset into the table ([EDX+EBX]); it
// runs 0..0x1f, so exactly 32 bytes are examined. The table byte is fetched through the walking
// pointer ECX (= base + EBX). GetDriveTypeA returns 0=UNKNOWN 1=NO_ROOT_DIR 2=REMOVABLE
// 3=FIXED 4=REMOTE 5=CDROM 6=RAMDISK; the sole caller (FUN_0040b2a8) probes 3, then 5, then 4,
// then 6 -- i.e. it picks the best available drive, preferring fixed over CD-ROM over network
// over RAM-disk -- which is what settles the drive-letter reading of the emitted label.
````

### `io/InitializeDispatchRecords.c`

- Original file: `c/InitializeDispatchRecords.c`
- Original function/symbol: `InitializeDispatchRecords`
- Original address: `0x00406390`
- New module: `io` / `core`
- Source SHA-256: `2746dfb088cb4868b5ae9b8a28f87ac7a66548266546090e7c0e9bb128cf8d05`

<details><summary>Original leading conversion notes</summary>

````text
/* InitializeDispatchRecords @ 0x00406390
 *
 * Load the record-dispatch image described by the save header: open
 * NETWALK<variant>.SAV, validate the two-dword image signature, read the
 * 76-byte header and the three region descriptors, then read every 16-byte
 * record descriptor and its arena/slot payloads from the stream.
 *
 * ABI: __stdcall, one incoming dword, tail `RET 4`.  Every path returns zero.
 * The caller (NwSaveDispatchByMode, mode 2) sign-extends the returned AL.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * EXACT FLOW (verified against the shipped instructions, 634 bytes)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *  1. Open the variant with the same opener/save-name builder used by the
 *     writer.  A failed open jumps straight to the zero-return epilogue: it
 *     does NOT truncate or close the tracked handle, and it does NOT touch
 *     g_flag_417808.
 *  2. Read eight bytes into a local pair and require the image signature
 *     0x3d53563d / 0x80000018.  A short/failed read or a mismatch truncates the
 *     tracked handle to zero, closes it, and returns zero.  No other read in
 *     this body is checked.
 *  3. Preserve header bytes +0x14..+0x18 (five runtime bytes that the header
 *     reader is about to overwrite), read the 76-byte header, then put those
 *     five bytes back.  The reader's write to +0x19 (MCI mode) and to the
 *     trailing dwords is intentionally kept.
 *  4. Copy the ease-target byte into header +0x31, clear +0x32, and invoke the
 *     slot hook with argument zero.
 *  5. Snapshot the header's MCI mode (+0x19, signed byte), pending hook index
 *     (+0x38, dword), and active-record index (+0x3c, dword) in locals.
 *  6. Raise the two load flags, clear g_flag_417808, and run the pending-command
 *     loop with the dword at header +0x08.  Then load the three region
 *     descriptors from window +0x637c, +0x6380 and +0x6384.
 *  7. For the header +0x10 record count: read the descriptor index, read the
 *     slot count into descriptor +0x0c, allocate `2*slotBase + 16*count`
 *     bytes, read the arena into descriptor +0x08, and add the slot delta to
 *     every unmarked slot's +0x0c dword.  Then for each slot whose byte 0 has
 *     both 0x02 and 0x08 set, allocate the state-table byte length and replace
 *     +0x0c with that payload pointer before reading the payload.
 *  8. Clear both load flags, reload the last-record tile cache with flagA=0,
 *     close the handle, copy header +0x33/+0x34 into the frame-control record,
 *     and dispatch the optional MCI mode, pending slot hook, and active-cell
 *     installation using the saved signed tests (negative means "absent").
 *  9. Set g_flag_417808=1, run the global-scope exception dispatch, return 0.
 *
 * The descriptor field at +0x0c is a slot count here.  It becomes a payload
 * pointer only for a marked slot after allocation, which is the representation
 * the save writer reads back.
 *
 * `DispatchPendingCommandLoop` is stdcall (`RET 4`) in this image but has no
 * @4 symbol alias.  The explicit assembler label below keeps the bare symbol
 * while the stdcall declaration prevents the double cleanup a cdecl caller
 * would produce.
 */
````

</details>

<details><summary>Original leading conversion notes</summary>

````text
// LoadDecryptRegionsFromDescriptor @ 0x00406080 (NETWALK.EXE, Ghidra project NETWALK.EXE)
// Walks the caller-supplied buffer-region descriptor backward, loading each listed region from the program's global stream into its slot in the runtime buffer pool and decrypting it in place with a rolling XOR key, returning zero if any region could not be read in full.
// Status: done
/*
 * 47 instructions, body 0x00406080..0x004060ea, non-degenerate.
 * Decompilation and disassembly agree on every load, every argument and both
 * loop bounds; the only visible difference is that the decompiler rewrote the
 * descending pointer walk as an indexed expression and kept a dead variable
 * for the XOR callee's undefined return.
 *
 * Stack frame (__stdcall, RET 0x4, one argument read straight off the stack):
 *
 *   [ESP+0x1c] pRegionDescriptor buffer-region descriptor (param_1, int *)
 *
 * Body, with E = the stack pointer at entry:
 *
 *   0x00406080  SUB ESP,0x8 / PUSH EBX/EBP/ESI/EDI
 *   0x00406087  MOV  EAX,[ESP+0x1c]   ; EAX = pRegionDescriptor (arg1, after 8+16)
 *   0x0040608b  TEST EAX,EAX
 *   0x0040608d  JZ   0x004060df       ; NULL descriptor: skip the loop, return 1
 *   0x0040608f  MOV  EBX,[EAX]        ; EBX = dwRegionTally, the record count
 *   0x00406091  LEA  ECX,[EAX+0x4]    ; ECX = pRegionDescriptor + 4, record array base
 *   0x00406094  MOV  [ESP+0x14],ECX   ; spilled so the array base survives the calls
 *   0x00406098  LEA  ESI,[ECX+EBX*0x8]; cursor = base + 8*tally
 *   0x0040609b  ADD  ESI,0x4          ;        + 4  (one record past the end)
 *   loop:
 *   0x0040609e  ADD  ESI,-0x8         ; cursor walks DOWN, one 8-byte record per pass
 *   0x004060a1  DEC  EBX              ; counter follows the cursor, tally-1 first
 *   0x004060a2  MOV  ECX,EBX
 *   0x004060a4  MOV  EDX,[ESP+0x14]   ; EDX = record array base
 *   0x004060a8  MOV  EDI,[EDX+ECX*0x8]; EDI = record.dwOffsetFromBase (+0x00)
 *   0x004060ab  MOV  ECX,EDI
 *   0x004060ad  ADD  ECX,[0x004173e4] ; ECX = dwOffsetFromBase + g_base_ptr_a = pBuf
 *   0x004060b3  MOV  [ESP+0x10],ECX   ; spilled, the read callee cleans its own args
 *   0x004060b7  PUSH ECX              ; buffer -> callee's arg2
 *   0x004060b8  MOV  EBP,[ESI]        ; EBP = record.dwByteCount (+0x04)
 *   0x004060ba  PUSH EBP              ; count  -> callee's arg1
 *   0x004060bb  CALL 0x0040c998       ; ReadStreamChunkFromDescriptorVerifyCount
 *   0x004060c0  TEST AL,AL
 *   0x004060c2  JNZ  0x004060d0
 *   0x004060c4  XOR  EAX,EAX / POP.. / ADD ESP,0x8 / RET 0x4   ; SHORT-CIRCUIT FAILURE
 *   0x004060d0  PUSH [ESP+0x10]       ; pBuf  -> XOR callee's arg3
 *   0x004060d4  PUSH EBP              ; count -> XOR callee's arg2
 *   0x004060d5  PUSH EDI              ; offset-> XOR callee's arg1 (the KEY INDEX)
 *   0x004060d6  CALL 0x00406054       ; ApplyRollingKeyXorToBuffer
 *   0x004060db  TEST EBX,EBX
 *   0x004060dd  JNZ  loop
 *   0x004060df  MOV  AL,0x1 / POP.. / ADD ESP,0x8 / RET 0x4   ; SUCCESS
 *
 * WHAT IT DOES, IN ORDER, PER REGION: read dwByteCount bytes of that region
 * out of the program's single global stream into
 * g_base_ptr_a + dwOffsetFromBase, then XOR those same dwByteCount bytes in
 * place against the 32-byte rolling key table at 0x411298. The stream reader
 * is the CRLF/CTRL-Z normalising one, so this is a load-and-decode pass over
 * a run-length-free region table: the on-disk form of every region is
 * obfuscated, and the file's regions are materialised and decoded in the pool
 * in one sweep.
 *
 * THE FIRST FIELD IS USED TWICE, AND THAT IS NOT A CONTRADICTION.
 * record.dwOffsetFromBase (+0x00) is added to g_base_ptr_a to form the
 * destination address, and the SAME dword is handed to
 * ApplyRollingKeyXorToBuffer as its dwKeyIndex, where it is pre-incremented
 * and masked with 0x1f to index the key table. So each record carries both its
 * position in the pool and the phase of the rolling key that region is
 * encoded with. Sibling c/ClearBufferRegionsFromDescriptor.c, which walks the
 * identical descriptor, uses that same +0x00 field for the offset only and
 * never looks at the key; the field has two consumers, not two meanings.
 *
 * THE ARGUMENT ORDER FOR THE READ. ReadStreamChunkFromDescriptorVerifyCount
 * (c/ReadStreamChunkFromDescriptorVerifyCount.c, @0x0040c998) is recovered
 * with the two-argument __cdecl form (cbRequestedBytes, lpBuffer) and ends in
 * RET 0x8. Here dwByteCount is pushed LAST (0x004060ba) and the buffer FIRST
 * (0x004060b7), so the count arrives at [ESP+4] as arg1 and the buffer at
 * [ESP+8] as arg2 -- exactly the order that callee file documents, no
 * inversion. The sibling ClearBufferRegionsFromDescriptor does invert its own
 * callee's arguments because FillMemoryWithZeroBytes takes (count, buffer)
 * with a different push discipline; do not carry that habit over.
 *
 * THE ARGUMENT ORDER FOR THE DECRYPT. ApplyRollingKeyXorToBuffer
 * (c/ApplyRollingKeyXorToBuffer.c, @0x00406054) is (dwKeyIndex, nCount,
 * pBuf), RET 0xC. Three pushes in reverse here -- pBuf, count, offset -- so
 * offset lands at [ESP+4], count at [ESP+8], pBuf at [ESP+0xc]: argument
 * order preserved, and the key index really is the offset field.
 *
 * THE RETURN VALUE IS A BOOLEAN, AND THE DECOMPILER PRINTS A STALE ONE.
 * The C body reads `return CONCAT31((int3)((uint)uVar3 >> 8), 1);`, where
 * uVar3 is the result of ApplyRollingKeyXorToBuffer -- a void function whose
 * EAX is never written. The real contract is in the two epilogues: AL is
 * set to 0x1 at 0x004060df on the success path and EAX is zeroed at
 * 0x004060c4 on the first short read, with the high three bytes never written
 * on the success path. So it returns 1 for "every region was read and
 * decoded" and 0 for "some region was short", nothing else. Both callers
 * (0x0040621c, 0x00406390) call it for effect and discard the result, which
 * is consistent with a load step whose failure is handled elsewhere.
 *
 * FAILURE IS IMMEDIATE AND PARTIAL-WORK-SURVIVING. The TEST AL,AL at
 * 0x004060c0 returns 0 on the first region that does not arrive in full; the
 * regions already loaded are left decoded in the pool and the records below
 * the failure point are simply never touched. There is no rollback and no
 * unwinding of what has already happened.
 *
 * A NULL DESCRIPTOR IS SUCCESS, NOT FAILURE: the JZ at 0x0040608d jumps to
 * the same epilogue as the completed loop, so "nothing to load" and "loaded
 * everything" both return 1. Both of this function's callers pass the raw
 * contents of a region descriptor global that is 0 in the static image, so
 * the NULL path is the pre-initialised path and is exercised.
 *
 * ALL dwRegionTally RECORDS ARE WALKED, indices tally-1 down to 0, and no
 * more. The DEC at 0x004060a1 happens at the TOP of the body, before the
 * load, so the first pass touches index tally-1; the TEST EBX,EBX at
 * 0x004060db is the loop's only exit test and it fires when the counter has
 * been decremented to 0, which is after index 0 has been processed. That is
 * tally passes over tally records with nothing skipped off either end -- the
 * same tally-1 start and the same count as the sibling walker, confirmed
 * there under an explicit `iVar4 = *pHeader; DEC; while (iVar4 != 0)`.
 *
 * One consequence worth recording: because the machine loop is a do/while
 * whose counter is decremented before it is used, a tally of 0 would send it
 * to 0xffffffff and then walk record bases at roughly -8 GB from the array.
 * The C below carries an explicit zero-tally guard the binary does not have;
 * it is a translation guard, marked as such, and not recovered machine
 * behaviour. A tally of exactly 1 is well-defined in the binary (one record,
 * one load, one decrypt) and is not guarded.
 *
 * THE DESCRIPTOR LAYOUT -- AGREES WITH c/ClearBufferRegionsFromDescriptor.c,
 * established here independently from this body's own two loads:
 *
 *   +0x00  unsigned long  regionTally        read once, by 0x0040608f
 *   +0x04  record 0     { dwOffsetFromBase, dwByteCount }
 *            +0x0c  record 1  { dwOffsetFromBase, dwByteCount }
 *                       ... one record per 8 bytes, exactly regionTally ...
 *
 * The load at 0x004060a8 reaches the record's FIRST dword and the load at
 * 0x004060b8, via the cursor at ESI, reaches its SECOND -- so within a record
 * the offset sits 4 bytes ABOVE the count and the record base is
 * pRegionDescriptor + 4 + 8*i. That is the same layout, the same 8-byte
 * stride, the same tally header and the same index arithmetic the sibling
 * reports, with no contradiction on any of them.
 */
/* stdint.h is included explicitly for uintptr_t: the compile gate is an
 * x86_64 cross-compiler, so a plain `unsigned long` global holding a pointer
 * is 8 bytes wide there and 4 in the real x86 target, which makes every
 * global-relative address emit a spurious -Wint-to-pointer-cast warning.
 * uintptr_t is pointer-width on both, so it models the target faithfully and
 * compiles clean. */
````
